I write this from a wooden hut in the jungle of a lesser known island in the Indian Ocean. 

Living in the blinks between timezones, I’ve documented the last 10 years of my life through 1000+ microsongs – threads of transient nostalgia captured on tape.

Now trading nature immersion for urban hustle, I’m knitting together the last decade via release. “Old Friends New Cities” is a collaboration with photography platform Analogue People, and 10 photographers (5 men and 5 women), from around the world.

Curating a collection of 10 photos paired with the music of Old Friends New Cities – Analogue People has juxtaposed the realities of nomadic city life over a longing familiar to the metropolitan among us – a return home; to nature and to our roots.

records.title: Sixteen

records.note:
When I make any good song (at least in my opinion), it starts where I don’t think about anything in particular, so that in the moment - I won't be critical of anything. I enjoy freedom in painting the melodies, then seeing what words come out, and experimenting with the beat that is presented to me. Sometimes I change the lyrics, or sometimes, I don’t. Case by case, I think the feeling of the song can speak either way. On Sixteen, I liked the dark melodic tones and the busy hard hitting drums. I wanted the song to match that same feeling and not seem to overpower the music but to compliment it. It feels somewhat easy listening to me as well.
	It made sense for this song to be released with sound.xyz not only because of the lyrical ode to Hodling crypto, but because I believe in Web3’s future in the world. I wrote "In My Mind" as a way to express my struggles with mental illness and depression that I’ve dealt with for most of my life. It was a cathartic process, to put into words the thoughts and feelings that had been swirling inside my head for so long. It wasn't until I started writing this song that I truly realized the extent of how freeing it felt to transmute that energy. 

I put my heart and soul into this song, and I hope that it will resonate with others who have struggled as well. I want people to know that they are not alone in their struggles and that there is always hope for a better tomorrow. The song ends with a sense of hope, and it's the message I want to convey, that no matter how hard it gets, there's always a way to break free from the depression and find the strength to move forward.

"IN MY MIND" is a very raw and personal song that I hope will bring comfort to those who need it, and remind them that even in the darkest days, there's always hope for a better tomorrow.

records.title: Summer's Lovers
records.creator: 0xF64579f9F76E060e6E3fC88441d5147f722e9405
records.note:
Hi, I go by Parrott. I’m a 26 year old visual artist and musician from Seattle.

You may know me for my visual work. I've been creating on web3 for nearly 3 years as an artist on SuperRare, NiftyGateway and more.

What you may not know is that I’ve been a music producer for more than half my life. Music has been my passion, my language and my truest expression of myself for as long as I can remember. 

I first started producing in fifth grade, my parents bought me an old desktop with a bunch of cracked software on it and there I began tinkering with noise (it wasn’t music yet). 
We didn’t have wifi, cable or video games growing up - so everyday after school I would find myself at my computer trying to make something that sounded like how I saw the world.

Over the years I had a few releases on some record labels, went on a few tours, played some festivals and even got to open up for some of my biggest inspirations - but I never found a way to survive off just my creativity alone. 
That is until 2020 when I found some of my life long dreams coming true through my visual art. 

The success happened so quickly and seemingly overnight, that both my public identity and the way I navigated the world changed - I was no longer “Parrott the Producer”, I was now “Parrott the Artist”. 

With the success, I found new struggles, new stressors and an ever hungry market for my art. This effectively killed my ability to create anything related to what I was then putting out. I felt watched, expectations were high and I became alone and isolated. 
I poured this into the only creative outlet I felt I had left - music. 
No one seemed to care about my music anymore, just my art - and this let me write music just for myself, for the first time since I was a kid. It was liberating and I wrote albums worth of material. 

These songs come from pain, triumph, loss and growth. These songs are honest, created for myself - and I’m more proud of these than anything else I’ve ever created in my life. 
I plan on releasing them slowly over the next year and invite you all to participate with me in this journey.
I can’t begin to describe how excited (and nervous) I am to share this part of myself with the world again. 

This first song “Summer’s Lovers” is a love song. 
It’s a warm breeze on a mid-august night. 
Scorched grass pricking your feet. 
The smell of hot concrete. 
An embrace of a lover that sends butterflies to your belly. 
A kiss that hints at a summer that never ends.

Foreve

records.note: Pray was written towards the beginning of 2020. I remember playing my guitar one afternoon and I stumbled across the guitar melody that you hear throughout the song. I kept playing it until I found the words "I got a problem." The rest of the song fell together. Usually, whenever I start writing, the song writes itself. Sometimes all it takes is a good melody that helps describe how I feel at the moment.  Within two days I wrote “Pray” which is about my conflicting feelings towards wanting to love and being obligated to love.  I wanted to write a song that was sonically darker than many of my others.  Pray is the only song from my Don't Overthink It EP that features percussion. Pray is a song that I am most proud of and I hope you love it as much as I do.

records.note:
Who are Beachcrimes? We’re a duo from LA and we spent the last year making songs in hotel rooms around the world. Beachcrimes is the soundtrack to that adventure.
 
We made a lot of songs, and we’re excited to share them with you. All of them. This year we’re releasing 24 songs in 48 weeks, in web3 and beyond. We want to build this album in public, and bring our holders into the creative conversation as we go.

If we’re being real, it’s actually two albums – there’s AM and there’s PM. AM is the lite stuff, PM is the nite stuff. Think of it like the Summer Olympics and Winter Olympics, but for dance music. WATCH THIS SPACE.

“Do It Better” is the 2nd of these 24 singles. AM through and through. But don’t get us wrong - you can still play it on a boat at ear-shattering levels. This is our 2nd mint on Sound XYZ. Jump in and build with us. Next single will be out 2 weeks from today, and the following single 2 weeks after that.

“Do It Better” was born in a hotel room on Lake Como in Italy last summer. We tested it on a boat and trust us - it works. This was the anthem for our summer and we hope it will be your anthem for next summer.

We feel like this could be the start of something special, a grand experiment we can’t wait to bring into the world, and we’d love for you to jump in and build with us.

records.title: Beautiful Tragic
records.creator: 0x16d2EB949eAAb2FF1EFb9c16f29a4532EDF42D11
records.note:
There's a quote by French writer and columnist Jean D’Ormesson that I have kept close to me since I was about 12 years old and it goes like this:

“Do not let yourself be fooled or abused. Remember to beware. And even of the obvious: as she (the obvious) spends her time changing. Do not place people or things too high. Do not place them too low. No, do not place them too low. Rise. Renounce hatred: it harms those who feel it rather than those who are the object of it. Do not try to be wise at all costs. Madness too is wisdom. And wisdom, madness. Escape the precepts and the givers of lessons. Throw out this book. Do what you want. And what you can. Cry when you need to. Laugh. I laughed a lot. I laughed at the world and at others and at myself. Nothing is very important. Everything is tragic. All that we love will die. And I will die too. Life is Beautiful.”

I wrote Beautiful Tragic, on one of those afternoons where one can feel kind of defeated and deflated about things, the world, life, and so on. It's a reminder of the small ways in which I have found and continue to find joy, through dancing, self-expression, and fighting for things I want and believe in while remembering that nothing is promised, nothing is guaranteed, and everything will end eventually, and thats okay. Everything is beautiful, everything is tragic.

This entire EP was written, produced, mixed and mastered in 48 hours. Kevin and I set ourselves a challenge to not question any creative decision we made. To entirely act on instinct. There's something enlightening about being against the clock. Decisions that previously were arduous and sometimes impossible to make became easy. The resulting music isn't perfect, but it's some of the most honest and raw stuff that we've made and we're both immensely proud of it. We hope you enjoy this insight into our creative process and remember to trust your instincts.

records.title: Breakdown
records.creator: 0x625307dE45Bd25AD6bf6cC7391a308fc84067cf7
records.note:
This song came at a crossroad for both Elle and myself. We were both going through similar situations and emotions without knowing it. We were inspired to write this song but the truth is..we weren’t. This song came to us in a wave of emotion at a time that we were feeling completely broken down by life and all that entails it. 

Everything around us was falling to pieces and we did not know how to express ourselves to anyone, let alone ourselves. This song is a representation that even though one may seem fine on the outside, you never know what someone is dealing with on the inside. We used to try to make everyone happy, pouring until everyone's cup was full but that often left us feeling empty, which over time left us feeling broken. 

This song is a reminder to give yourself some grace and remember it’ll be okay, no matter how hard things may seem. We all have our moments when we feel like breaking, and sometimes what looks like a breakdown could actually be a breakthrough.

Performing Artist: Elle Symone 
Producer: Pete Rango

'Back Home' is a tale about a musician's life on the road touring, chasing a dream while missing the people they love the most and leave behind while on their musical journey.

records.note:
It is often hard to ignore the negative thoughts and doubts that circulate in our heads. We get so caught up in the fear of things and forget about the excitement that exists on the same path. DON’T LOOK DOWN can hopefully serve as a reminder that those negative thoughts are just like clouds passing by - they will eventually clear.

I wrote this song from the heart, hoping it would give you the strength to keep going and encourage you to keep your head up. 
One of the lyrics from the song goes ‘stars will shine on, after they burn out’ - the noise in your life and the hard days don’t diminish who you are, or the shine that you have.

records.title: Sign-in with Ethereum
records.creator: 0x077Fe9e96Aa9b20Bd36F1C6290f54F8717C5674E
records.note:
The Silicon Valley tech companies have become the new banks. They hold all of our data. They control our digital identities. 

Sign-in with Ethereum is the solution. It’s one of the first steps for users to own their data across the web. Instead of logging into the platform, the platform logs into your account. You own your data. You own your identity. You have a self-sovereign, universal login for the internet. 

Wayne Chang is a researcher, the co-author of the Sign in with Ethereum (SIWE) Standard, and the co-founder and CEO of Spruce, a company that is working to grow SIWE adoption to become the standard way to log into the internet. 

Chang believes that SIWE will lead to a more sovereign, decentralized, and free internet for the world. 

Crypto is known as a technology to separate money and state. Identity is no different. 

This podcast marks the beginning of the separation of identity and state. 

Art visualized from the timestamp [1:21:22 - 1:21:56]: “Sign in with Ethereum is the first step for users to own their data across the web….” 

10% of all proceeds go to Bankless DAO.

records.title: Half Life - Green Ring Remix
records.creator: 0x63aC987cE0A27F7fCDFc7dE87F3305dbd2B51473
records.note:
A Message From Green Ring:
‘Half Life’ has such a cool story and meaning in Rosalie’s journey, so I was honored when she asked me to put together a remix. The song mostly came together in the very first session as the original has some incredible material to work with. I just tried to bring the song into my own world by adding some new sounds and letting the idea flow freely. Really happy with how it turned out. I hope you enjoy, and thank you for listening.

A Message From Rosalie:
I remember the first time I heard a song by Green Ring on a Songcamp call. Something immediately perked up in me. He has this beautiful and unique way of taking me on a journey with his music that feels like I'm traveling somewhere between Dr. Who's time vortex and wherever it is that our imagination lives. I think one of the many things that draws me to Green Ring's music is his sense of melody. Even though his music is typically instrumental and slightly ambient, he has this pop sensibility woven through. When deciding that I wanted to do a remix for Half Life, my intuition told me to reach out to Green Ring. I was so excited when he said yes and so curious how he would interpret this song. I love that you can hear so much of both of us in this remix, and it has me dancing down the wormhole that his music always puts me in. The original song was about such a dark and sad time in my life, and how beautiful that writing about that time has brought in so many blessings.

records.title: Drift
records.creator: 0x61315007451e00451305f63c93Af8CDd866F6Bc9
records.note:
I love the unique timbre of a felted piano. Placing felt between the hammers and strings of a piano changes the instrument's tone, accentuating its percussive quality and bringing out subtle resonances.

I wanted to highlight that ethereal sound in Drift. The song is composed of changing patterns that create a rhythmic flow. The meditative ostinato moves into a more percussive section before receding into its daydream. I wanted the two contrasting ideas to blend together, with one drifting into the other.

My music features repeating melodic ideas that gradually layer and develop creating a hypnotic energy and a contemplative ambiance. 

I recorded Drift on a Kohler & Cambell at Christopher Lippincott's studio in East Nashville.

If we’re being real, it’s actually two albums – there’s AM and there’s PM. AM is the lite stuff, PM is the nite stuff. Think of it like the Summer Olympics and Winter Olympics, but for dance music. WATCH THIS SPACE.

“Let’s Play House” is the 1st of these 24 singles. PM through and through. And we’re excited to launch this project on Sound XYZ today with our genesis mint, limited to 24 editions at .01 ETH. Jump in and build with us. Single two will be out 2 weeks from today, and single three 2 weeks after that. More on that later.  

“Let’s Play House” is our debut mint, the genesis key, the access pass for everything else we’re planning in this space. We made the song in Milan last summer. records.title: Stories
records.creator: 0x702947630A359934d74418eAFc9E589438C1A27f
records.note:
I sing about love a lot. There is a need for more love in the world, and my goal is to connect people with it. That being said, love can look a lot of different ways. During a meeting with my team, they were adamant about getting me to talk my shit on a record. “Do you not know who you are? You’re Ballad! There isn’t anyone else like you. You can’t be afraid to say that and believe it.” That got me thinking of the kind of love I don’t usually sing about. That’s when “Stories” was born. It’s about having love for yourself and keeping those who don’t deserve your love out. 

We often let people enter and exit our lives without recourse. They take from us, and they leave us no better off than when they came. " Stories" is about taking control of your space and setting boundaries. You’re not a revolving door and you shouldn't be treated as such. This record is about honoring yourself and restricting your energy from those who only stand to use you. Why leave space for someone who never pours into your cup? If we allow people to treat us in such a way, what does that say about us? That isn’t the type of love we should accept. We fail to honor ourselves when we take less. 

We have to be unapologetic in the way that we say no. The same way that they were unapologetic about getting comfortable and constantly letting us down. With "Stories", I’m saying “keep your distance”. I know my worth. I know what I deserve. I value my time and I'm saying enough is enough. I’m also talking my shit at the same time. If you miss me, you can do it from the sidelines. On my story to be exact. You no longer have direct access.

records.title: Don't Really Mind
records.creator: 0x456D8ab48020cb339BFdCAea018Ed805dB78f7f1
records.note:
Hey everyone, my name is Tyler and I’m so stoked to be dropping my first record on Sound! Like so many others, I think this space is revolutionary and am glad to be here contributing a small part to web 3.

I’ve traversed a lot of genres in my time making music, beginning as a guitar-driven instrumentalist who evolved with an obsession for the entire process. Striving to communicate as best as I could over the years has lead me down a path of singing, songwriting, production, and self-engineering. BARDZ began as a project heavily influenced by the indie-electronic space, but has grown and changed so much with these additions. That culmination is truly represented by the song I’m dropping here on Sound.

Don’t Really Mind was the most visceral experience I’ve ever had for an idea. Usually the process is’t that sexy: I sit down, iterate on riffs and motifs until something catches my attention, nurturing it from there. With this song, it came to me in 4k laying hungover on a friend’s couch. Trust me when I say nothing creatively good ever happens to me when I put my health last - except for this one. The hook and bassline permeated my thoughts on a loop until I was able to reach my computer a couple days later. The lyrics came naturally, somewhat indicative of the night I had before the inspiration. On the surface, it’s a song about cat and mouse. Under the hood, it’s a commentary on dancing with indecision, internal dialogue with yourself. At the end of the day, your lens is how you view the world, and our relationship with ourselves makes all the difference.

records.title: Caught Up
records.creator: 0x06246c2444aA68187f198AD4C640E367F6B4a779
records.note:
I am BYHAZE, the Architect of Holistic Sounds and I create authentic music that creates space for healing and introspection. I hope to create art that changes people’s perception about what “healing” looks and sound like. Sometimes crystals and sound bowls aren’t enough to get you through that healing, sometimes you have to use that throat chakra to set boundaries and affirm your needs. 

Caught Up was a song I started in 2019 after experiencing a lot of growth in my personal life and career as an artist. I was in a rediscovery phase and sonically I wanted to try something new. I’ve always loved pop and disco music growing up so it felt like a fun way to pay homage to my younger self. This was my first time back in the studio after a few months and it was such a cathartic experience. We free-styled a bit and came up with the melodies and the idea of caught up was born. The pandemic slowed us down a bit and we had to stop recording but we finished it in 2020 so it felt like the perfect song to release for my sound.xyz Genesis! I pulled influences from Earth Wind and Fire, Chromeo and Janelle Monae to create a feel good song with a message.

This song feels like a journey to self acceptance on a holistic level. The message of this song is not to get caught up in the idea that others may have for you because in turn you could end up living a lie. Sometimes people visit our social media pages and create an assumption about who we are or how we act and it can sometimes lead to disappointment if we don’t live up to the perceived expectation. This can happen platonically or romantically and since I experienced it from both ends, I was inspired to make song that made light of the situation. The song encouraged me to lean into my authenticity more and not settle for a love or situation that makes me me to dim my light. The chorus gives language to anyone that is looking to affirm their boundaries and not get caught up in the “lie” that someone creates about them. The song is infused with joy and takes listeners on a journey, ultimately reminding them that their authenticity is their superpower and the best way to honor themselves is by being them! Setting boundaries isn’t always fun, but I hope that singing this song can make it a little bit easier.

records.title: Haymaker
records.creator: 0xF180F7c066C9Af638b73CEEF139D5AdDE0D4265F
records.note:
With an earnest lyrical style and big hooky choruses, our sound lives inside a lush world of textures and riffs and a laid-back Californian sensibility.

ABOUT THE RELEASE:

Welcome to the Fever Dream sessions.

The songs from this session have an energy that came from being pent up and isolated for over a year during lockdown, to being around each other again and playing music in the same room. And it wasn't just any room either, our friend Darrell Thorp invited us to record this 3-track session in the gorgeous rooms at The Village in LA.

After an anxious year of pandemics, covid variants, personal health scares, and all the other bad juju the quarantine era brought, this session was a perfect oasis to break the anxiety that had built up since the lockdown began.

That's why the joyous energy had us buzzing. How cool was it to be around each other again, playing music with the best people, in the best place? Hopefully, some of that good vibe comes through in the music, and that the songs will help release the feverish anxiety into joyous catharsis.

Track 1 of 3: Haymaker

Edson Choi on the meaning behind the song:

‘I used to be deeply religious, doing ministries and community outreach weekly. One day, the sum of my doubts just hit me. I realized this or any religion wasn't for me.
 
I had built my life up to that point around this ideology; my friends, my community and plans for the future were centered around this faith. But to stay would be to betray myself and my new epiphany. And so, despite the comfort of belief and loving friends I made through my years in the ministry, I walked away and had to relearn thinking and how I should be living.
 
This rude awakening hit me like a punch to the gut, a blinding haymaker to the face. 
 
The song came many years after that experience, and it instead of it being a bitter takedown of faith and belief, I hope it highlights the beauty in the flaws of our world now. I hope it gives the energy of appreciating the beauty of our world and this life here, not a distant heaven. I tried to capture this thought with the song's closing lines:
 
"I'm just staring at too many stars again…don't judge me, cause we're all gonna go sometime."’

Soufside Baby is a ode to the hometown of Crook Brown, the Southside or affectionately the “Soufside” of Atlanta. Particularly the area/city known as College park. It is a soul, funk, and hip-hop fusion over hard knocking drums and a grooving bassline. 

Crook takes you down his very own personal memory lane exploring his upbringing in the area. It is an in depth look at family life, street life, and the regular ebbs and flows of a normal life all mixed together. It is essentially a story of what it means to be born and raised on the “Soufside”.

Crooks vocals are like a paint brush with wide gliding strokes on a soulful canvas. You can hear the emotional attachment to the very place he calls home. Despite the areas shortcomings, he still finds peace there, because after all it's still home. Crooks raspy southern drawl adds a flavor to the track that makes it a one of one. records.title: Jump Off

Peace - I’m Low Leaf ! Imma Filipino/American, multi-instrumentalist (pianist, harpist, guitarist) and producer born in Hollywood n based in LA. I’ve been independently releasing music since 2012 and it’s always been my dream to awaken the world to the cosmic song within & all around us ~ by simply being true to who I am n singing my heart’s song. Bc of this I’ve journeyed deep with my relationship to music and nature as a means to communicate with the divine throughout the years. 

“Jump Off” is special AF bc I wrote it when I was on a year long sabbatical, and felt how freeing it was to jump off the timelines of social media ~ how amazing it felt to reclaim my aura, my mind, my body, and fill myself up with my own energy again. I hadn’t realized how much I was pouring into so many people outside of me, energetically, creatively and psychically. 

I also wrote this the day after I watched the Kurt Cobain documentary Montage of Heck. I was inspired by his raw spirit, and how he was able to translate his soul so clearly in everything he made. I saw parts of myself that I’d been repressing in my own art. Whenever I was depressed, I wouldn’t feel like creating cuz I always thought that music was like an energy capsule - I didn’t wanna spread my sadness. I’ve come to find that I was expressing an incomplete picture of who I was, n limiting my own creativity. Although we are divine beings, we are also human. 

Inna way, this song is also a timeline jump… into a reality where I’m able to receive insight from my future self, and give insight to my past self / timeline jumping into a version of me where I’m more liberated and whole / embracing the multi-dimensionality of what it means to become more human.

records.title: Cool With You?
records.creator: 0x14e5D778c77574106f8241303C9Ec5F418A82085
records.note:
I remember having a conversation with a "music exec" in the past for some critiques and insight on my music.

I was told: "The music is great. You rap great, the production is great  and love music with this type of message. But the masses won't tune in to this kind of music. The world is too dark its not you." When I asked what that meant, I was told in so many words I needed to have a rough childhood upbringing turned positive to make my message loved and respected by people. If not, then I needed a gimmick of some sort.

That convo put me into a small stint of depression and snatched the inspiration right out of me. I'm grateful for friends with wisdom that told me that person was very likely trying to make me their industry pawn but also made it clear to me that -- MY story? Was indeed needed in the world via my music.

Not too long after that, I was inspired to produce and write this song. It was a letter to my listeners asking them an important yet somewhat rhetorical question: 

this is my life and experience...is that cool with you?

I hope this record can be an encouragement to all artists of all genres and forms to always stay true to you. We should all strive to become great at what we do and explore new sounds and ways to create. But we should never lose who we are for the sake of money (USD or ETH) or just to attract a large audience. Because you can really die while you're still alive.

Cool With You?

records.title: FOREVER FORNEVER
records.creator: 0x13eF06797F095D5C62BabF704d983cf1B4bDE9E5
records.note:
When the pandemic hit and they said "stay inside" I replied "bet"...

The first thing that I did was queue up my favorite anime, Yu Yu Hakusho, to rewatch it for the first time in maybe a decade. 

Through the course of watching the series I was overcome with nostalgia, particularly in Season 2 when "Sayonara Bye Bye" plays as the ending them. I also felt a strong connection to the protagonist, Yususke Urameshi, so much so that I googled this fictional character's given date of birth. Much to my liking, I realized that Urameshi was an Aries as well and his birthday was just two days before mine!

What took place after that was a combination of my love for music, anime, and basketball (I was watching the NBA bubble season too). 

I wrote this song from the perspective of Yusuke in relation to his love interest, Keiko Yukimura, while weaving in the pieces of my own life that felt relevant. The title, FOREVER FORNEVER, is the last phrase that you see on screen when the series ends..one that resonated with me deeply. The meaning of which, the writer left open to interpretation generating years of debates and think pieces from devoted fans (me).

At the time, I was fighting through the pandemic but also depression as I'm sure many were at the time - this song was a huge release for me emotionally but then also statistically being one of my most successful records generating over 100k streams across DSPs and nearly 100k views on the music video.

In fact, if you google "forever fornever" this song is the top result.

records.title: Scorched
records.creator: 0x291a1CacD70F571FDB445f1899a75afE3E774Faa
records.note:
I go by Ricky Lake - I’m a musician based in San Francisco, California. I was first inspired to record music in high school while living in Nashville, Tennessee. From there, my passion for it only grew. After moving to The Bay, I was lucky enough to meet Patrick Brown and Tiffany Wilson over at Text Me Records, who opened doors for me to not only expand my career as a musician but to explore new sounds and genres I had never been around before.

	 It was with Text Me Records that I was first introduced to Bobby Renz. We started working together a lot, either at Different Fur Studios in the Mission District or towards Daly City at Bobby’s own studio. He produced a few songs on my debut album “Last Summer Sucked” and our bond only became more solidified from there. We actually finished up this song the week that Covid lockdown started in 2020. The hook had been giving us mad problems - We couldn’t figure out what would really fit. But we knew the verses, the beat, and the vibes of the song were on point. Finally Bobby recorded himself singing something as a reference and sent it over to me. I tried to sing it myself but I soon realized the recording he’d made should just be the hook as is. This goes to show the kind of musical friendship Bobby and I created. We were (and still are) truly friends when we made this track and we worked together by bouncing ideas off each other, shedding our egos and letting our ears take control. 

	If our memory isn’t failing us, Bobby and I both took a little bit of mushrooms before we started working on this song. For some reason my mind found itself at a 1980’s house party, surrounded by narcotics, amazing food, loud colorful clothing, and beautiful women. And it was this vibe that became the inspiration. This was the sparking point for the creative flow that would become the lyrics for “Scorched”. My favorite line of the song is probably: “I’m glad I wasn’t there - That police raid like Counterstrike - Smoked a Parliament and thought about the afterlife”. It captures the constant contradictions my life has consisted of. That time off Charlotte Pike in Nashville when the house I’d been selling weed out of got raided by the Sheriffs office - but luckily I wasn’t there because I’d recently made amends with my mom and moved back home. The fact that we are here one second and gone the next - but in the time we still exist we find ourselves thinking of “what ifs” and “what comes next?” instead of existing purely in the moment. T

records.note:
hi friends! thanks for tunin into kyb's first jump into the blockchain. we present to u: too late, too soon (orchestral rendition)

too late, too soon is an introspective song about looking back at the crossroads we stand in front of and the choices we make in our lives. It has a nostalgic, wistful perspective that swirls youthful metamorphosis, hope, regret, concessions, resolutions, and the wishful introspection of someone grappling with the proverbial question: what if I had gone another route?

“at the heart of much of my songwriting is introspection. we have all been forced to pivot in some way in 2020 due to circumstances beyond our control. but what if we could stand at the crossroads in
our lives and really dig deep into the hope, regret, resolutions, and concessions we have made and must still make to get us to our authentic selves and better choices. 'too late, too soon' embodies all that internal struggle I certainly grapple with and I like to think others do too. I keep digging in, knowing I have changed but into who? I just think we all have had to dig deep into our own dirt and sort out the hard stuff. that’s what 'too late, too soon' is for me.”
                                                                             - Cameron Lavi-Jones

For my first Sound drop I spoke about often second guessing ideas and sacrificing consistency for comfort, which often resulted in a lot of the music I create never reaching the ears of listeners. After seeing the amazing response to my Genesis release and once again looking at all of the unreleased music in my catalog I landed on this record “So Many Ways.”

“So Many Ways” is a record that Da-P and I worked on in the Summer of 2022 while he stayed with me in LA as we finished our EP “It’s Not That Deep.” I thought no better way to kick off 2023 and my first Web3 release of the year than with this record that I think builds on this theme from my Genesis release and is a sort of reminder to myself to not overlook all of the work put in along the way and to sometimes just “let it fly” when it comes to the music my friends and I work so hard at creating.

I hope you enjoy “So Many Ways” and that this record can be a public reminder to myself about remaining consistent, inspired and out of my own way in 2023 and beyond. Thank you for coming along on this journey with me. I’ll be back soon!

records.title: Move Your Mouth
records.creator: 0x47C82C4c99e2855a4926068AC7557Da9e5ebAFE4
records.note:
Padma is a 19 year old first generation Indian-American artist. Having grown up with one grandmother who was a renowned poet and another grandmother who sang in Indian temples, she was inspired at a very young age to write and sing. She wrote her first song at age 15 and has since written 300+ songs. Her musical influences range from The Smashing Pumpkins to HAIM to Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan.

Most recently, in 2022, she released her debut EP “Daisy,” which received several editorial nods including a major look from her motherland: Rolling Stone (India)

‘Move Your Mouth’ is the first single off of her next EP. The song opens with a reverb kissed lead guitar line and is followed by a pumping bass line and crunchy drums. The rhythmic and airy vocals create a pocket that is bound to make your head bop. The simplicity of the production leaves room for Padma’s vocals to draw in listeners and hear the story she is telling.

The upbeat and grunge pop sonics of ‘Move Your Mouth’ contrast the darker meaning behind the lyrics. The song was inspired by the thoughts you have when you start to sense that a relationship is turning sour. It’s about realizing that your partner was more focused on your body than your emotions throughout your relationship. The phrase ‘Move Your Mouth’ is a way of asking your partner to “say something” and give you a reason why they’re treating you this way.

records.title: Emotions
records.creator: 0x51a8B04E69B1E8AEc0A110A9E9Ff9870377b1993
records.note:
Emotions explores the complex push and pull dynamics that can sometimes exist in relationships. If everything isn’t perfect, should I leave? Or do I love you or this so much, maybe more than myself, that I am willing stay and tolerate less than I deserve? We’ve all been here.

Healing is my Superpower and Music is my weapon. You probably know me best for T-Shirt and Impossible. I’ve written songs that you know, for and with major artists like Bruno Mars, Pitbull and Rihanna but I also write for myself. I got sick and tired of feeling like a slave at Universal so here I am in web3 banking on myself and building with my supporters and other like-minded Creatives. I wrote Emotions years ago, in the midst of battling myself in a war of Passion. I fell deeply in love with someone who couldn’t truly be mine. A wild love. I struggled. Is this a conflict worth battling? Or simply just the Universe’s funny way of making sure I never take love for granted? I couldn’t figure it out. So I wrote a song instead. 

Produced by: Shane Can Türkili
Written by: Shontelle Layne & Camille (Adaeze) Evelyn
Mixed and Mastered by: Miro Markus

COOL STORY. 

This was supposed to be a Fetty Wap collab and I wrote his parts. Never happened since sadly he’s locked up. So what you hear in the bridge is actually me modulating my voice to reflect his style and cadence. Rarely do I share the behind the scenes stories and process of my art or how I approach writing for others. Humbly letting you in. A moment in my life shared with the people who ride with me the hardest. You’ll be the only people EVER to own this version of Emotions.

The artwork was created by me. Kinda. I know many talented visual artists, but I wanted to try an experiment. The artwork including the Golden Egg, was created by AI, prompted by images of me and the lyrics of the song. I wanted to experiment to see what my words and feelings would inspire. So the art is truly unique and specific to Emotions. It’s also the 1st AI art I ever created.

Thanks to web3, these unreleased songs from my heart get to reach yours. I’m grateful for you. Grabbing these lets me know who my day ones are so I can hook you up later ;) 

xoxo.

In addition to golden eggs, collectors will receive access to exclusive content such as demos of the song, photos from the time at the shelter and more.

Here’s to new beginnings <3

records.title: Joyful Resistance Part I
records.creator: 0x3360A4e0Eb33161dA911B85f7C343E02ea41BbbD
records.note:
"Joy as an act of resistance" - quoted from poet Toi Dericotte, is an idea, a way of being, and turn of phrase that I was introduced to visiting Initiatives of Change in Richmond VA, January 2020 at the invitation of cultural storyteller and curator Alicia Aroche. Two months later the whole world shut down. Two months later, George Floyd's murder inspired a long-overdue global action, thought and consciousness mobilization putting BLM front and center of the world stage.

Summer 2020, at the peak of the protests, I sat down to create with all this on my heart. Joy is an energy. It's the antidote to so many negative and destructive emotions and ideas, instantly breaking down barriers and fortifying spirits and minds with an infectious, and freedom-focused, powerfully positive expression: the power of joy rooted in intention, and the force for change and evolution that it can be. 

Out came these sounds... brooding piano leading the way into a 3/4 head nod, with moogs dancing free form around the harmony-dense groove... anchored by shapes designed to inspire curiosity, possibility, nostalgia and newness all at once. Change starts in our minds and hearts and this is offered in gratitude to the power of music to reach inside us, uplift, inspire and unite.

records.note:
I miss Summer, like not just the season but like what "Summer" meant to me as a kid. It seemed endless at times. 

The nostalgia for Summer that this beat triggered inspired me to write as if I was literally driving down memory lane. 

As you listen, imagine yourself ghost riding the whip down a foggy street that everyone you ever knew still lives on, watching you drift pass.

More about PAISLEY....

In 2017, I had a thought, “patterns prevail”. It was derivative of a quote from my best friend and frequent collaborator, Sky Welkin, which read “passion prevails”. Sky is a talented cartoonist that embeds profound messages like this throughout his work.

During our college years, he’d often come by and draw while I made beats, this was our ghetto co-working era, and in these sessions we’d smoke, engage in discourse, and share ideas about the respective worlds we were building in our art. In fact, I was very much into doing something new each album, but Sky was the primary influence for me to get into world-building and having a particular sense of style that was cultivated over time.

In one of my college apartments, I decided that to let Sky use all of the walls in my room as a canvas - the few hundred dollars that I’d spend to have the room repainted when I moved was minuscule compared to the living art piece around me. Every so often I would discover some new character scene or phrase that he’d drawn without me noticing, but one of these phrases was placed in such a way that I couldn’t miss it as soon as I woke up, “passion prevails”.

Web3 has offered much in the form of expansion for the experiential qualities and monetization of my art. We always say things like, “time passes quickly in web3”.

As much as I agree, I find it interesting that time also seems to stay still - art is appreciated for it’s beauty regardless of age and with the possibilities available to me with NFTs, something like my debut album, can no experience a new form of appreciation.

As I begin to release works from the PAISLEY collection over time, it was only fitting that I began with the short film.

When I was working on the album, I connected with my friend and collaborator, Dawit N.M. to share the pattern theories I was creating from and what I was aesthetically into at the time. Dawit went on to handle the art direction for the album, as well as bringing my convoluted story concept to life as a film.

I wanted to articulate the feeling of not giving a shit about anything, or anyone. It's the second before the last song on my album that I have been releasing on Sound. This song felt so honest when I wrote it, that I almost didn't release it. But that wouldn't have been very "nothing matters, I'm having an existential crisis" of me. The drums in the song are actually just me tapping on my desk (aside from the kick). Obviously I spruced them up and OTT'd them to hell. 

For the record, I love second dates.

records.note:
‘Ello loves, my name is tyler coolidge (all lowercase please) and I am an artist, producer and writer from the Bay Area, California. I’ve been on the artist-grizzle for a little over ten years now, specializing in Hip-Hop and R&B music—often a fun blend of both at the same time. I believe anyone who knows me well would say that my personality matches pretty closely to the music I make, which is usually smooth/chill and easy-going, but with sprinkles of high energy all over the place. (I’m an espresso guy)

The track I’ve decided to finish and share with you all is called “NO SCOPE,” which is produced by my good friend Future James and also features the extremely-talented Sacramento native Nate Curry, making this track an all-Bay Area collaboration! The track is easygoing, playful and catchy while also capturing an element of fun in it, which I alluded to in the last paragraph—I think this track encapsulates who I am and what I’m like pretty well. My favorite thing to make music about is the early stages of a fresh romance, where you have to choose words carefully and put on your best outfits and stuff like that, lol. It’s just a fun, nervous, almost juvenile-feeling time and “NO SCOPE” is about “shooting your shot” in those situations! Shooting your shot… no scope… get it?????

I am extremely grateful to be up here on the Sound.xyz stage sharing my new art with this awesome and loving community that I’ve seen grow over the past year, and can’t wait to interact with y’all and build even more together. Thank you Sound so much for having me, and shoutout to my man Greydient for helping me get here. Plenty more to come, much love to allayall! <3

records.title: Ayahuasca Riddim
records.creator: 0x4d1AeA7b20F04b1F9f18222a5BDA1d380Be567Cd
records.note:
This track is really special for me because it came to me after a dream about doing ayahuasca in the amazon rainforest. The interesting thing is I have never participated in the ceremony but in the dream I did. I remember hearing a melody that I could not forget. When I woke up I could still hear it and ran to my setup and started sketching out the idea. In a couple of hours this track was complete and I just sat with it for awhile. I never felt the need to go back into it or change anything it was kind of like a download from the ether that just happened and felt finished. 

I haven’t release much music since my EP FREE MUSIC that came out in 2021 and this track feels like the perfect continuation of the feelings that I was communicating on that project. I produce for a handful of amazing artists but when it comes to my own personal work I like to bring the spirits of my ancestors and indigenous atmosphere. This track really speaks to that for me and brings me back to that dream like it just happened. I hope it does the same for you

I have a (bad) habit of staying up all night until 7 AM working on music because sometimes that’s the only time of day I’m able to pursue my passions. ‘7AM’ is about the workaholic tendencies we fall into when we become addicted to progress, desperate to make our dreams a reality. This record is about the dangers of conflating productivity with self worth, and a reminder that great things take time, so we have to take care of ourselves in the process.

records.title: I Got Time Today
records.creator: 0x4a5A71184Bf725b86a132990EAE29031AFf2eE9e
records.note:
I'm Tyler. I go by Mozado, but you can call me Zado if that's easier. I'm a diy artist out of Boston. My introduction to music was in 4th grade when I started playing sax in the school band. I ended up playing all the way throughout college, but senior year of high school I came across FL Studio for the first time. From then on my goal was to be an EDM producer prodigy like my idols Avicii, Zedd, Porter Robinson, and Madeon. I honestly got pretty close when a bootleg remix of a Chainsmokers song got reposted by the duo themselves on Soundcloud and amassed over 300k plays in a few hours before Sony Records PROMPTLY took it down. I was sick to my stomach not gonna lie.

A couple years later I was in an original song contest and got to attend EDC Las Vegas. It was an amazing experience but bittersweet because I realized that maybe EDM wasn't what I loved most. So after that I rebranded to Mozado and started secretly practicing my singing and rapping. Eventually in 2018 I released Hellacopters, the first song I not only produced, but sang and rapped on too. And just like that, I was a real life recording artist. All my music is still produced, mixed, and mastered by me in my basement, Bomb Shelter Studio (literally a bunker room in the house I live in). 

I pride myself on my versatility and I'm pretty sure I'm dope but the music industry is humbling as hell for upcoming artists. Sound.xyz will be seeing the full scope of that versatility. For example this drop is a very different vibe than the rock and hip-hop sounds of my debut album Girls Run The Internet. Being in Boston means cold winters and I often make beachy summer songs as a coping mechanism lol. That's what this song is.

Coming to all major DSPs soon.

records.title: That's A Wrap (ft. Jon Kupper)
records.creator: 0x665aa84BdCc8307149E09F4BCcc481766dfA9C7A
records.note:
In January 2022 there was an event at Record Plant, a studio in Los Angeles, that chillpill hosted to help onboard artists onto web3. A few of us snuck into the control room and made this song. Naturally, people would hear the bass through the wall and slowly leave the live room where the event was to see what was going on. The night ended with 40+ people crowded around the computer blasting the finished version. That is how our year started so we thought it made sense for it to also be how we wrap it up. 

We had Jon Kupper step up to help us with the intro and outro. KAJÉ went crazy on the beat with chillpill. & I recorded in front of more people than I have in my life. 

Hope you blast this at your NYE party, web3 gets it first.

PAISLEY had already been released by the time we made this, but it was a lock to add it on as a bonus track for the deluxe edition released 6 months later.

This song will be both Darius and Brea's first NFTs.

During our college years, he’d often come by and draw while I made beats, this was our ghetto co-working era, and in these sessions we’d smoke, engage in discourse, and share ideas about the respective worlds we were building in our art. In fact, I was very much into doing something new each album, but Sky was the primary influence for me to get into world-building and having a particular sense of style that was cultivated over time.

In one of my college apartments, I decided that to let Sky use all of the walls in my room as a canvas - the few hundred dollars that I’d spend to have the room repainted when I moved was minuscule compared to the living art piece around me. Every so often I would discover some new character scene or phrase that he’d drawn without me noticing, but one of these phrases was placed in such a way that I couldn’t miss it as soon as I woke up, “passion prevails”.

records.title: SUGAR
records.creator: 0xd68892aEd5b3a9B1E419B8a2C0D2c6A9C17d7679
records.note:
2022 has been a revealing year in so many ways. not only have i started a new duo music project “GLOWSTONE” with sober rob, which has been nothing but creatively liberating, but i am also gradually coming out of a producing hiatus for my own project. over these past few years, i’ve been suffocating myself with pressure, afraid to even touch ableton again, and am now learning how to finally let go and find experimentation in different dance genres. “SUGAR” is the launching pad for this next era of self-produced music and ideas, which i couldn’t be more eager to put out. 

with that being said, this year has also been revealing for the rest of us as a society; we’re still trying to process the holidays post-pandemic and an all-around new normal, there are the biggest social and womens’ rights movements happening across the world right now (hence the roe versus wade overturn reference). the weight of the world hit me hard as i was sick one week; i thought about the holidays coming up and what they would signify for certain groups and disconnected families, which prompted the first couple lines of “SUGAR”. 
 
while it is a love song at heart and reflects all the loves i’ve found over 2022, including producing, it also is a tribute to light in a dark world that is yearning to be better. 

co-produced and mixed with my partner in crime, rob. <3

I wrote “Mantra” having in mind certain relationships and also experiences of isolation. It’s hard when certain people leave your life and sometimes it’s you that no longer can maintain.

At times I escaped into solitude, so called self-care. While it’s usually good, sometimes it’s easy to burn the bridges instead of confrontation - we push people away to protect ourselves - and sometimes that becomes our mantra, even if things get better. And I’ve seen spiritual people who weren’t that spiritual in the end.        It’s my second performance as a vocalist, and I want to invite you on my journey in making actual songs, not only instrumentals. I’m thrilled to hear what you think.

"Glass Jedi" was the first song created for my debut album, the landscape for the world I was about to build. I had a very close friend put me in the studio with Deaton Chris Anthony & Jean Dawson and this was what we created. 

I had written out a very detailed map of the sounds and feelings I wanted to  evoke in the project which were serious, sexy and multi dimensional. 

At this point in my life I was going through huge transitions out of a super toxic relationship, so writing this was like being born again. Jean and I mostly worked ways to iterate finding an exit sign in the back of my head so the hook turned into "In the back of my mind there's a white hearse or a limousine " 

I also yell and scream words like "salt all in my veins" , "black veil on my baby face" "all I feel is everything" then "in the back of my mind there's a white hearse or a limousine" transitioning into a much smoother moment of release. 

This is the world opener of the album because it's the most intoxicating and boundary pushing I felt I had been in my career yet. the collaboration couldn't have been more special to be re presented.

records.title: Break The Tension
records.creator: 0x7e8608f5893A6a57602A014aB190f7af8069D1E1
records.note:
I'm beyond excited to present "Break The Tension" as my Genesis track on Sound. 

Break The Tension is a smooth R&B track written, produced and performed by myself. Created back in 2021 this song talks about the a particular instance between two people slowly building up powerful feelings for one another, to the point where there is only one direction to go. Seizing the moment, action is finally taken and the release of the intense build up results in an eclectic emotional and physical experience, finally feeling free around one another. 

My musical journey has been building up for some time and as this new year has started I am excited, inspired, and more ready than ever to share my art with the world. Thank you for being apart of this journey. 

- Max

records.title: Deja Vu
records.creator: 0x13eF06797F095D5C62BabF704d983cf1B4bDE9E5
records.note:
Deja Vu was my first record to cross 100k streams on any platform. 

This was an effort

More about PAISLEY....

In 2017, I had a thought, “patterns prevail”. It was derivative of a quote from my best friend and frequent collaborator, Sky Welkin, which read “passion prevails”. Sky is a talented cartoonist that embeds profound messages like this throughout his work.

During our college years, he’d often come by and draw while I made beats, this was our ghetto co-working era, and in these sessions we’d smoke, engage in discourse, and share ideas about the respective worlds we were building in our art. In fact, I was very much into doing something new each album, but Sky was the primary influence for me to get into world-building and having a particular sense of style that was cultivated over time.

In one of my college apartments, I decided that to let Sky use all of the walls in my room as a canvas - the few hundred dollars that I’d spend to have the room repainted when I moved was minuscule compared to the living art piece around me. Every so often I would discover some new character scene or phrase that he’d drawn without me noticing, but one of these phrases was placed in such a way that I couldn’t miss it as soon as I woke up, “passion prevails”.

Web3 has offered much in the form of expansion for the experiential qualities and monetization of my art. We always say things like, “time passes quickly in web3”.

As much as I agree, I find it interesting that time also seems to stay still - art is appreciated for it’s beauty regardless of age and with the possibilities available to me with NFTs, something like my debut album, can no experience a new form of appreciation.

As I begin to release works from the PAISLEY collection over time, it was only fitting that I began with the short film.

When I was working on the album, I connected with my friend and collaborator, Dawit N.M. to share the pattern theories I was creating from and what I was aesthetically into at the time. Dawit went on to handle the art direction for the album, as well as bringing my convoluted story concept to life as a film.

The story of PAISLEY exists in a universe in which we've all been made to forget true selves. Though, there are those of us that break free and reawaken, remembering all the knowledge of self that was once lost. A human that knows who they are can no longer be controlled and is thus a threat to those in power.

This is the case for our protagonists Figaro and Paisl

records.title: Find Your Tribe
records.creator: 0x284d2102464347a50C9c582643C315aD19156Bf5
records.note:
Find Your Tribe was written as my way of calling in my community in the hopes of connecting with people who felt like-hearted, kindred, and whole. At the time that I wrote Find Your Tribe, I had realized the people I was closest to were no longer in alignment with who I was. I kept thinking about the expression “your vibe attracts your tribe” and went inward to see what vibe I was attracting. It was lonely at first, but this work was important for me to find my community with clarity and strong self-awareness. 

I’d learned from my project “Mantra Loops” how powerful writing things in the affirmative had been for me and wrote “Find Your Tribe” as a way to imagine what being in a healthy community would feel like. I thought about the freedom that comes from being truly comfortable amongst the people you love. The more I sang this song, the more people I met who made me feel comfortable, confident and whole. My vibe was attracting my tribe! That’s the power of word vibration! 

I chose this song for today’s drop because I feel like web3 came at a time when people were feeling isolated and seeking community. So many people I know are finding their tribe here in web3 and I’m excited to be integrated into such a genuine, loving, and supportive community. It was important to me that I recorded this song with people I considered tribe, so this is a family effort between me, PRVDNT, an artist and friend I’ve worked with for 10 years, my brother Joe Deadwildin, who would MD my performances in New York and new sisters, Tanee Osborne and Joanna Gerolaga who performed at the TED Women Conference with me last December. Executive produced by my husband, my friend of over 20 years, Dominic Malone, who also created the cover art. 

The winner of the Golden Egg will receive a special recording with a live performance take at the end and a BTS video of the live session that was recorded at the end of this song with PRVDNT & Joe Deadwildin'

records.title: Half Life (Binaural Atmos Mix)
records.creator: 0x63aC987cE0A27F7fCDFc7dE87F3305dbd2B51473
records.note:
Half Life is about struggling with depression. It’s about looking at my life and being afraid that I wasn’t living up to my full potential. About feeling like I had worked so hard and been through so much, only to feel like I still wasn’t living up to the expectations I had for myself. About the kind of hopelessness that settled around me when I felt like I was failing at living my purpose.

The depression was trigged after getting traumatized by web2 pressures - how empty and inauthentic I felt trying to go viral on TikTok; how I had hired a TikTok coach and posted every day for a month, but none of my videos took off; how I felt cringy and embarrassed of some of the content and started making them private; how I had to spend my time making covers for YouTube instead of making songs that meant something to me; how social media made me feel like shit, but I felt I had nowhere else to turn when everyone in the industry was saying I didn’t have a choice; how I felt like my experimental and boundary-pushing music wasn’t bite-sized enough and I was being asked to water myself down. 

And then one day, scrolling through Instagram, I saw a story from Matthew Chaim. He posted an article Time did on Songcamp’s songwriting camps and I felt a spark. I had followed him a while back because he was one of the few artists I knew of at the time that was doing experimental pop music and getting Spotify editorial support, and I was mad inspired. As someone who made up her own genre-blend called deep pop, his experimental pop music was a north star. I didn’t know him at all then, but I got a bit of courage, and DM’d him to see how I might be able to get involved. He responded, and told me Songcamp meets every Monday, and to come to a call. I remember running to tell my mom after getting the DM I was so excited. I joined the call the very next Monday, and fast forward to now, the Songcamp community is filled with people I call dear friends. 

In contrast to feeling so abandoned and isolated in web2, everyone on the Songcamp call was immediately warm and welcoming. I felt like they saw me and accepted me for who I was. They were kind. They loved pushing boundaries and exploring new tech. For the first time in my life, I felt like I had found my tribe. From there I was a part of Songcamp’s CHAOS project, met friends that eventually would form cornerclub together, and was introduced to the promise of web3. That one DM literally changed my life. Finding web3 is what gave me my h

records.title: SUP - Golden Egg
records.creator: 0x050D7634A0CA8bdFDA1E8b2f7fDe4eaffb338815
records.note:
“SUP” is an unveiled glance into male vulnerability in the digital age — a minimalistic love song for the hopeless romantic trying to express deep affection in an age of brevity and emojis. “Sup” can mean so many things depending on the tone and context. The goal behind the track was to show the many iterations of “Sup,” and poke fun at how difficult it can be to express the simplest and most profound emotions.

The song was produced by my in house dream team: award winning composer/producer Lyell Evans Roeder and Kirk “KJ” Follette  — a process that was rather quick to compose but took months to mix and refine to our liking. Sonically, we stuck to a formula of melding contemporary drum production with a simple yet textured melody — sophisticated ignorance. 

This is my first legitimate release as an independent artist since leaving my record label during pandemic, it means the world to be so vulnerable on so many levels in this web3 space that’s redefining possibilities for working artists. I have two full length projects almost done being mixed and mastered for 2023, consider this the first official crowdfunding effort in this new independent chapter! Your support means the world.

records.title: TREBUCHET
records.creator: 0xe01fA6fC6E6C26cA44561B88f49ffd639585F2dC
records.note:
I created TREBUCHET to tell - and write - my story from here going forward. Earlier in my music career I had the opportunity to sign to a record label, and I did. I seized what was (at the time) the best option I had to take music seriously (and convince my family that it could be taken seriously…). Signing that deal opened so many doors, and taught me so much about who I was, who I wanted to be, but most importantly who I was not. As time went by I wandered further and further away from why I started creating in the first place, eventually arriving at an unrecognizable version of myself. 

I spent much of the pandemic questioning who I was (as a human and as an artist), what I was creating, and whether or not it was worth continuing. But through time and sustained chipping away I started to remember and re-recognize the kid who first started creating - the one who rushed to open Ableton in any spare free time and express himself honestly and openly - before all the expectations and extra cooks came into the kitchen. This song is my most honest return to that, and I think sets the tone for all of my music that will follow.

I provide this context so that you might better understand TREBUCHET as a song and metaphor. I made this record exactly as I wanted to - with its weird, yet super personal sonic choices, somewhat nebulous lyrics, and a key change at the end (among other things) - because for so long I wasn’t free to create in the way that I know I’m supposed to: following only my own ideas, experience and intuition. The song feels right at home with some of the records I’m most proud of from my past, and combines my newly rediscovered creative drive with my last few years of production and songwriting experience for something I’m finally proud of once again. 

I hope you love it as much as I do.

records.title: DISPOSABLE
records.creator: 0xBeC2635b44D26AcF54DDa59644ddB71FB0e0268D
records.note:
6 years ago I received a package from 5,000 miles away. My ex-girlfriend from Buenos Aires had shipped me a shoebox full of mementos from our relationship and a goodbye note. I remember receiving the package and sitting with it for a few minutes in silence before picking up my guitar. I sat on the floor at the base of my couch, and this song came out in a matter of 15 minutes or so.

Disposable is the first song that I wrote and released as a solo artist in 2017. Throughout 2017-18 I hosted artist showcases in my basement to spotlight student artists at my university - the cover art for this drop is a photo from one of the first of those shows where I debuted my EP "Purple Line". The golden egg is the album artwork of that EP - my first and only release as Oddentity. That night was my first time ever performing original music - it was an intense and beautiful moment that I will never forget.

records.title: LikeSo
records.creator: 0xA3288b2bBF311A7FB68c7f07c326217b0b0DbCb9
records.note:
EVAMM02

This track is for me and my ailments. My body is starting to fail and struggle in various ways, and this is the sound it makes. There is beauty in the decay.

I wrote this song while in a considerable amount of physical pain. It’s not usual for me to want to create when I am not feeling my best physically, but this was a chance to make a change in my writing process and challenge myself. I usually hit pause on my entire life when I’m sick. I  just sort of dissociate and consume in bed until it’s over or I’ve healed, but this time I chose to actually create something in this state. I wanted to process my emotions in real time. The pain is gone for now, but the feelings remain in this piece of music. I listen back and it helps remind me that everything is temporary and there can always be light even in the darkest moments.

LikeSo was created on December 13th, 2022. A tempo of 68.19 beats per minute was chosen because it was less painful to move slow, and the key of G minor best represented my emotional state at the time. The song features a one-take performance of rhythms that were designed on an Octatrack MK II and the rest of the melodies and pads were created using a Prophet ’08 PE running through a Microcosm delay pedal. The song crescendos into warm keys from my Wurlitzer 200A which is hands down my most cherished instrument and where most of my writing either starts or ends.

I keep my tears in the keybed.
Music can alleviate.

Written & Produced by Eva Myra May

Mixed & Mastered by Eva Myra May

Generative Artwork by Jeres
Golden Egg features 1 of 1 special art with “extra processing.”

Special thanks to Kyle Nelson for additional production help and for just being in the studio with me while I processed all of this. It’s too hard to do it alone.

Run is written as a tough love lecture from God. I often imagined God as a having the demeanor of a black mother. 

I wrote this while literally and figuratively on the run. I was running from a lot in my life but hadn't yet realized what i was running towards, but in the context of the song we are always running back to the source. 

It doesn't matter what path we take, they all lead back home eventually.

More about PAISLEY....

In 2017, I had a thought, “patterns prevail”. It was derivative of a quote from my best friend and frequent collaborator, Sky Welkin, which read “passion prevails”. Sky is a talented cartoonist that embeds profound messages like this throughout his work.

During our college years, he’d often come by and draw while I made beats, this was our ghetto co-working era, and in these sessions we’d smoke, engage in discourse, and share ideas about the respective worlds we were building in our art. In fact, I was very much into doing something new each album, but Sky was the primary influence for me to get into world-building and having a particular sense of style that was cultivated over time.

In one of my college apartments, I decided that to let Sky use all of the walls in my room as a canvas - the few hundred dollars that I’d spend to have the room repainted when I moved was minuscule compared to the living art piece around me. Every so often I would discover some new character scene or phrase that he’d drawn without me noticing, but one of these phrases was placed in such a way that I couldn’t miss it as soon as I woke up, “passion prevails”.

Web3 has offered much in the form of expansion for the experiential qualities and monetization of my art. We always say things like, “time passes quickly in web3”.

As much as I agree, I find it interesting that time also seems to stay still - art is appreciated for it’s beauty regardless of age and with the possibilities available to me with NFTs, something like my debut album, can no experience a new form of appreciation.

As I begin to release works from the PAISLEY collection over time, it was only fitting that I began with the short film.

When I was working on the album, I connected with my friend and collaborator, Dawit N.M. to share the pattern theories I was creating from and what I was aesthetically into at the time. Dawit went on to handle the art direction for the album, as well as bringing my convoluted story concept to life as a film.

records.title: Distanced
records.creator: 0xcF669804AC78CFc589bEaE782f045f961fC10381
records.note:
My very first house track, dated pre-Soulection, that started my journey and transition from mere bedroom/dorm room beatmaker fawning over FlyLo's "Reset" EP, to electronic music producer trying expand his horizon past the then-overly popular J Dilla aesthetic, aspiring to Daft Punk more than Slum Village (the funny part being my favorite track the time was a Dilla/Slum Village remix of "Aerodynamic", lol).

That was the scene that set up this track, which I've revamped countless times after to feature in mixes everywhere, on Soulection, on BBC Radio 1, but never officially released; until now, of course.

Though this is a rare one, I want as many people as possible to listen to it AND have a chance to get what is possibly, literally my rarest gem drop yet out of my vault. This one is just pure vibes, but I meant it to really just take you somewhere, but nowhere in particular either; distanced from this reality into another, if that's what calls to you...

Le Mav produced the track with me in Lagos Nigeria last year. The sonics on this track is our signature sound. I immediately found the hook. "I must I must admit I must" The verses took me time to write. Through out the verses I breakdown the honesty of leaving someone you love but shouldn't be with. The song was very therapeutic to me. records.title: Alprazalam
records.creator: 0x1946dEEa31307e66CEd73360e023AAaC0E770458
records.note: Alprazalam’ references Alprazolam, the generic name for Xanax. The lyrics allude to both my friends, as well as a woman I grew up around who struggled with tranquilizer/opiate abuse. A Cancer, the sensitive crab who would never leave her bedroom (her shell) and was largely absent during my young childhood. Aside from taking inspiration from that astrological archetype, I am without hands during the entire video. Not “of this world” and trying to escape that painful reality. The visual is playful and absurd and punky, but there is a dark and melancholic undertone to both the video and song itself.

records.title: Hurts (feat. Sara Phillips)
records.creator: 0xD01D744Ae46b1B80ed908479B8e704Ebd8a53ad7
records.note:
I love heartbreak, to be honest. I often find inspiration in memories or images stuck in my head; very visual, and very vivid.

When I reached out to Sara, I remember telling her about this idea of being in a new relationship while still dreaming about the previous one. It’s a tough spot you know? It hurts. I guess we all have that past relationship that hasn’t really allowed us to move on, that messed us up. As a result, we end up unconsciously looking for that person in everyone we meet, which most likely won’t happen and will end up hurting the other person.

So this song is about that, how cold and lonely it feels to be with the wrong person. How painful it feels to hold on to one and not have the courage to let go. How we lie and say we are fine, hurts like hell.

Special thanks to Sara for making this vision a reality and putting it into words, it means the world to me. Also, shoutout to Jack Hentosh for mixing and mastering, and Nicolas Melo for the amazing artwork.

With love,


Charlie Crown

records.title: America
records.creator: 0xF0f5316D0b0473F36E545193B141304806eFE792
records.note:
This holiday season a lot of us are blessed with the opportunity to spend time with our loved ones. Whether it be lighting the candles together, decorating the tree, frosting cookies, or tearing open gifts like there's no tomorrow. The holidays, as we know them, are a time of love, joy, and bliss. They are a time to put all your worries and fears aside and just be happy. 
The families and friends of the 41,477 people lost to gun violence in America this year alone, will not have that. Their holidays will be filled with grief and times of remembrance. There will only be the pictures and videos of their passed loved ones from past holidays, as they hold onto their laughs vibrating through the speakers over and over again. 

I wrote America after the Uvalde Elementary shooting. I remember waking up to twitter threads of kids faces who died and rage tweets from all of the people who are over the fact that this can happen due to our lack of gun safety and control in America. Even now as I recount that morning I can feel the sadness from that memory seeping through me and trying to escape. But we can’t let go of these feelings until there is change made. I will stay sad, and I will stay angry until our people are safe. As of October 2022 there have been 257 SCHOOL shootings alone in America. That is an increase from 2021 at 250 school shootings. So things are NOT improving as the stats are showing.  And a direct quote from Snopes states, “Many of these shootings were not the mass killing events that schools typically drill for. Rather, they were an extension of rising everyday gun violence." 

I know we all have busy schedules and as much as I know a lot of us wish we could constantly be doing research and hands on help after these shootings take place, it’s just not reality. That’s why I have decided to donate 75% of proceeds from “America” to Brady. Brady is a foundation with their hands deep in making change around gun violence. A direct quote from their site being “Brady emphasizes education, litigation, and legislation to ensure that every community is safe, not only from mass shootings, but also from the daily toll of gun homicide, domestic violence, suicide, unintentional shootings, and police violence that plagues so many communities.” 

I hope with my full heart that you listen to the lyrics of this song and want to do nothing more but to help with a small yet such LARGE part in making change and that is donating to the cause. As an independent artist,

this is a remix of one of the very first midnight snacks - i made the original early 2020, right when touring came to a standstill and i was missing that feeling of flying at cruise altitude across the planet to visit faraway places, and share music with friends old and new. my sonkei ('respect' in japanese) remix is inspired by, and in memory of, the late great nujabes - the legendary japanese producer who left us way too soon (if you're not familiar, samurai champloo is a great entry point to his music via a classic anime). 

I've always loved how nujabes is the consummate improvising b-boy musician, flipping jazz, breaks and samples. i tweeted recently reflecting on how we were born the same year, have similar musical dna, were always barely even one degree of separation from each other, but despite all the time and community i've had in japan, never had the opportunity to meet. he's someone i would love to have had a chance to break bread with, vibe and create with.

with all that in mind (!), fresh out the lab, here's the new sonkei remix, slowing [37,000 feet] down to a jazzy head-nod and sending peace and love out to nujabes - RIP 🙏 ✨

records.title: EAST SIDE
records.creator: 0x96C1a82864671fBc31F8Ddf3F862999734ab7C29
records.note: East Side is a record I wrote with Oliver Malcolm, one of my best friends and also one of my favorite artists.  He's produced songs for me like Heartstrings with Carlos Santana and Ghosts Around Midnight.  We made it in one day and wanted to capture minimalism within a record.  There were so many opportunities to over produce this record, to add booming drums, to do the most...  And after playing with it for months we all agreed that the first day's version - which just features me playing and singing on the guitar, my brother Sol's infectious bass line, and Oliver's short appearance - was the one.  The song is about precisely what the lyrics are talking about.  Growing up on the east coast in Trumbull, Connecticut, I spent a lot of months admiring the ruthlessness of the winter and the feeling that winter has left me with has lingered in my sounds for as long as i've been creating.  Even after years of being in the California sun, the cold wevva on the east side has left its imprint on me.
