records.title: Paint in the Dark
records.creator: 0xE7907a934bf32607D8eB7698FF9ad5701f174c6a
records.note:
I wrote Paint in the Dark because I needed the reminder that relationships can be playful and colorful instead of defining them by their mistakes. Over the past few years, this song has become a guide back to my emotional center in both my relationships to those around me, as well as in the relationship I have with myself. It has also reminded me how to believe in the joy of relationships again, and I hope that it can be there for anyone who needs that reminder too. 

I cowrote "Paint in the Dark" with one of my best friends on the planet, Dean Woodson, in his bedroom in North Hollywood in late 2019. There was something really special in the air that day. We got together to finish a completely different song, and in the process of recording a guitar part for that song, the guitar part for PITD popped right out. It was as though lightning struck and we could feel it; the static in the room drew the lyrics and melodies out of us effortlessly in a matter of minutes. All of a sudden, the song was done and we celebrated with a burrito from Cilantro Mexican Grill (our favorite local spot at the time).

As the pandemic slowly closed the world, Dean flew back to Paris and we decided in late 2020 to begin producing Paint in the Dark long-distance. We spent countless nights staying up late producing with one another over zoom and facetime, and we were constantly sending texts and voice memos of ideas back and forth while the other slept. It was a beautiful way to continue our friendship and keep ourselves inspired during a moment when the earth felt like it was at its darkest. When we had a good picture of the final song, we brought it to our mentor, Rob Cavallo, to help us over the finish line. 

"Paint in the Dark" released in late 2021 along with an amazing music video shot by one of my best friends Vinsint (@vinsint). I hope you enjoy listening, and as always, thank you for collecting <3

Minimalistic in its nature, Saucy is a bouncy hip hop record made for the people who embody what it means to have “sauce”. Sauce can’t be taught. Sauce is a lifestyle. Sauce is an energy. Sauce is an aura. If you know, you know.

records.title: Graffiti
records.creator: 0xd17cC306A72B53834bFe0f5B636F60b03bfe8BBf
records.note:
I took a lot of trips to NYC over the last year to work on my second EP and to live a little life outside of my suburban bubble. During one of these trips I was on the bus to a friend’s apartment when an old drunk man began reciting bible verses while waving a kitchen knife. I was already deep in this weird, reclusive funk - and this whole drunk Jack Sparrow wielding blade situation made me feel like Brad Pitt in Fight Club or DeNiro in Taxi Driver - like I was caught in the middle of some larger plot being poked at by the universe. I marched around NYC that day imagining I really was the main character - and that every crack in the concrete and every character on every bus and every piece of graffiti on every subway platform was deliberately placed to remind me of a past relationship that I couldn’t shake. I wrote the first verse and first half of the chorus on a bench in NYC over a short piano loop I made with my little OP-1 synth. I brought these orphaned pieces to my dear songwriter friend Jesse Fink. He suggested the lyric that drives this whole song: “the writing on the wall is just graffiti with your name” and the whole song clicked. My friend Sean Cook added some guitars and synths and his brother Ryan Cook laid down some real life tasty drums to bring the whole record together.

written by ben kessler, jesse fink
produced by ben kessler, sean cook
artwork by josefine cardoni

records.title: While I Write About You
records.creator: 0x414CA9c0e2FcCc222ca1c5f4cC77Ca685dd03F7d
records.note:
I wrote this in June. During that time I was getting over someone, writing a bunch of songs about them as a way of venting. And after many short lived voice memos and poorly played guitar songs, I created this one. This is probably the final song I’d written and recorded about them, and a great ending to that chapter. 

I love this song with all my heart. I’m in love with the story that progresses as you listen. It starts off painting the picture of seeing someone again for the first time in a while. That feeling where your heart isn’t fully healed from whatever had happened previously between you both. The chorus talks about a part of that person that you can never fully get over. “Those beautiful eyes will never let me go”. 

True. 

I love the back and forth between me describing my feelings and contradicting them with the idea of it being pointless to write songs about this person, because they don’t care. And as you continue to listen, the story evolves. The second verse reminisces on old memories. Staying up till 6am. It compares these memories to how things are in the present: “Now we act like none of it ever happened”. I mention the fact that they won’t get the satisfaction of seeing me hurt, because I’d already given them so much before. 

And the last minute reflects on what could’ve been and what actually happened. It ends off by mentioning the whole point of this person toying with my emotions while I’d been in the process of writing about them. Hence the title, 

“While I Write About You”.

records.title: Metropolis Jawn
records.creator: 0x26eF03A20AaeDA8aaFCeE4E146DC6B328195947C
records.note:
Long Story Short, I've been producing & rhyming since 1995. The Golden Era of Hip Hop and the inception of the internet musician, from irc's to aol, message boards to myspace, to blogs,  The internet was once a much smaller pond where if you curious, passionate and slight tech savvy it was so easy to find like minded people & find resonance. Released a few singles on Vinyl while still in Highschool and blew up from internet rumor that Bill Gates was suing us, "Equilibrium" for sampling the Windows 95 startup music for one of our b-side tracks titled "Windows 98". During this time I also began recording my first solo album as Dutchmassive - "Junk Planet" (recorded 1997-2002, released 2004) by the time the album was released world wide, I was in my 20's and had long pivoted from the fun, ego driven battle raps after realizing I had so many people hanging onto my every word. Like The Pharcyde said, "I gotta say something that means something".  I took having an audience with more responsibility and did my best to be introspective and inspiring .I began recording my sophomore solo album titled "Crush Your System" which was originally supposed to be a double album, the 2nd disk containing my Instrumental album "Music 2 Sleep To" but in 2007 I was approached by Rawkus Records to release the album as apart of what would be the world's first large scale digital campaign "The Rawkus 50" with production from ILLMIND, Samiyam, 14KT, Dela, etc.  It didn't make sense to release my old beats next to such dope producers. 
 
This was also around the time,  Instrumental HipHop without any vocals began taking off with events like Beat Society, super crews like Beat Fanatic and countless blogs dedicated to showcasing instrumental albums but still,  Instrumental only releases were by no means normalized or acceptable to most people but the production was always the first thing that captured my heart.  After both of my Major releases met the same fate of 3 months after release, the labels filed for bankruptcy and no one got paid. I decided to take a break from recording records and focus mainly on production.  I was always Producing alongside emceeing but I was mainly known as a Rapper.   
The Long Story Short isn't as short as I thought so lets truncate as I explain the intentions of "Metropolis Jawn"

My Production was always a hybrid of 90's boom-bap, Jazz, soul with a touch of Video game OST sprinkled in and occasionally some deep house.  Like if Pete Rock, Dj Premier, J D

records.title: Love Again
records.creator: 0xB25e1b7d4A5b0486285A60501B05A45A6A6cb6Ba
records.note:
Imagine you could go back and tell your 17-year-old self “I’m good enough as I am.” Imagine what could’ve been one of life’s biggest failures turning into triumph.

Many moons ago as a senior in high school I was given the task of completing an exit project, where I would research poet Elizabeth Barrett Browning and one of her works and write about it. My English teacher was very vague with instructions and it left me feeling lost. So I procrastinated. Why? I started reading at a year and a half, I went to gifted and talented schools my whole life, why was this challenging? The me of today (post a late stage ADHD, Anxiety disorder diagnosis) would reach out for clarity and understanding of expectations.

But the me then who knew more than I gave her credit for, turned to music. The one constant, the one bit of clarity even when nothing else fell into place. I thought I knew the person I’d love forever and while that is not true- I did know then how profound, forgiving, patient and other worldly love was and still is. 

So I wrote Love Again but never turned in my project OR the song. I just knew it wasn’t good enough. I Technically flunked high school. As a result I had to do a semesters worth of English projects in one week to graduate on time. And did.

This recording was created 2years later @ 19 years old. The first song I ever wrote recorded, vocal produced, and co produced with my brother B. Sharpe. I was good enough then. And I’m good enough now.

It takes tremendous shadow work, to reach back into the past, and soothe the pain of a younger self. That is the point of life. That is the point of love.

records.title: Saw
records.creator: 0x70940c838e738bF66849D8Db657034E7eCE6172A
records.note:
Peace! You can call me Jack, and I’m an artist from the DMV. My creative style embraces all mediums for the sake of passionate storytelling, transformation, and awakening. Just as I have been finding my way within this world creatively, I can’t help but notice a sense of being found: the absorption into something bigger, more expansive, and often beyond words.

WAYSPACE is the name I’ve given to this bigger dimension of awareness that lies within us, both collectively and individually. It also happens to be the name of my debut album, which was released on Halloween 2022.

This new song, Saw, serves as a prequel to the album. It represents the mess, the breakdown, the disappointment, and the suffering aroused by loss, grief and nostalgia. Saw also reveals a quiet willingness to see the beauty in every difficulty. When we hear the words “Could it be that we’re just on the scenic route? Seeing tears on everybody coming down” we are offered a chance to embrace the suffering and understand that it connects us through compassion.

This was one of the first songs that my closest collaborator, Fabrizio, and I ever made together. Fabrizio is also the main producer on the album, so it means a lot to be able to share a song that is so dear to both of us. I’m grateful that it now has a home right here.

records.title: Eclipse29
records.creator: 0xd794a656aD0dcf4FAD4Be309Fdc3Cb1700a7dB0B
records.note:
The easiest way to introduce myself to you all is to start exactly where my life began. Old Orleans is an embodiment of where I come from; New Orleans. It is the place that taught me all that I know, and I owe it so much.

The universe works in the wildest way, being that this is my golden year (29 on 12/29), and I’ve been in the space of reflecting on everything in life. The ups and downs, the lessons learned, the hardships but also the joy life brings and being able to move through it all. I never saw myself making music or even being in this position of calling myself a “rapper” to be quite honest. I just needed an outlet to use my voice to amplify what it is I feel to the world. And here I am.

ECLIPSE29 is a piece of art producer Aston Woods and artist/vocalist Brooke D. came together to create. Timely enough I feel as though we all were in a space of reflecting on growth in life, so it was only right this record be filled with our love to be able to express the things we’ve come from individually that we may not even be aware of collectively. To speak for myself, this record is me. It’s my life from a child to a man and beyond, and I hope it lives on and speaks healing to anyone it touches in the future.

records.note:
In April of 2020, separated by an ocean and 3000 miles, both of us went into self-isolation. Physically, of course -- like everyone else. But also musically.

Turning inwards, we scoured the Refs instrumental vault for our most menacing, introverted and brooding soundscapes -- and proceeded to write 12 songs in 12 days. 2 years later, we offer up our debut album, "New Religion".			

Our song "I Should Be Alone Right Now" featuring our friend Kevin Garrett mirrors the calm-before-the-storm state of the world circa April 2020. In some ways, it holds even more water now, in light of ever-present systemic and cultural decline.		

The animated image we chose for artwork is a taste of an unreleased "New-Religion" themed collectable project. Owners of "I Should Be Alone Right Now" NFTs will get a sneak peak of what's to come.

-Dessauer and Rich

records.note:
The stories that we tell ourselves determine our self-image, which determines how we move through each day. NOT4ME is about recognizing and releasing the habits, patterns and stories in life that hurt us more than they contribute to our healing.

NOT4ME has been an affirmation for me throughout the 6 months since I wrote it - it is the story that I told myself to reclaim my identity and learn how to love myself despite persistent feelings of guilt and shame. Releasing these negative feelings allowed me to better show up for myself, re-center creativity and welcome healthier habits into my life.

This song is more relevant to me now than ever. It has made me more discerning of what supports my growth and what is simply…not for me 🤷🏽‍♂️

I hope NOT4ME supports your journey in some way.

I hope it makes you smile.

I hope it makes you dance.

records.title: Me and my gang
records.creator: 0x96C1a82864671fBc31F8Ddf3F862999734ab7C29
records.note:
Me and my Gang was written with a friend of mine named Dwayne who is from Oklahoma.  Dwayne has a natural southern cadence.  An old-timer rhythm to his speech.  Now I come from more Northern tongues - but I've evolved my slang into a blend of North American phrases...creating some form of new age broken down, gen-z english.  We love folk music.  But we like going to the clubs.  We like strippers, but we also like fire pits.

Me and my gang was written after a night of driving around Los Angeles looking for something to do.  Hanging out with friends and pretty women and coming home unfulfilled. An LA tale that seems too familiar to even the most clouted.  

This was a record that wasn't supposed to be on the upcoming album, Bad Radio.  I really had no intentions of writing for the album/ and thought it was done. But after writing this one late summer night, and recording it the next day, we started to feel the untamed honesty that the song mirrored back to us.  While playing the song back, Dwayne recommended we go to his spot in Oklahoma to do the video.  Two weeks later we're at a rodeo at Cowboys Oklahoma City with a film crew shooting one of my now favorite visuals.

If you're reading this, the song and video is out.  
On the cover, you'll find Callie.  A sweet girl from OK who helped us film the video.

Thank you everyone for the support.  Album dropping December 9th.

-felly

When I write music, I like to tell a story. I don't go through enough in my life to write songs that pertain to me so I usually draw inspiration from outside sources.

The concept of "Get Involved" came to me when I was listening to love songs about cheating but they were always either "breakup songs" or "take me back" songs.

records.title: PROOF
records.creator: 0x515014A3E5c3F0D4EE6b85C40a7892753d074a91
records.note:
Moving from England, to New York, then Los Angeles gave me my fair share of being out of my comfort zone and feeling lonely, so much so that it became a pattern. The only consistent thing in my life up till now was uncertainty itself and my music career. This pattern conditioned me to keep my friends and loved ones at a distance so that I could focus on the one reliable thing, music. 

I created this piece literally on the plane back to LA from being in England over the most part of covid living with an ex. I think writing this song came at the perfect moment, as I was feeling frustrated by how much time I was spending on a person who ended not working out when I could have been putting that energy back into my music. It felt as though he was living proof that the no one in my life was going to be consistent (as depressing as that sounds). 

Now that I am fully settled in LA I still find it hard to let myself completely get attached to anyone because of my past. I wrote this song as a sort of “apology” note to the people in my life who I push away. A sort of explanation as to why I act the way I do and that they should not be taking it personal. I also want this to be a song to those who struggle with attachment based on their past. What better way to explain yourself then through a song?

records.title: HERO
records.creator: 0xA29510a6d6de5F05659d1683A5D01A8E392c264a
records.note:
I would like to start by saying thank you. To you show my gratitude, my supporters will be receiving a special package from me personally in the mail. If you’re a collector of this NFT, DM me.

Hero is about a powerful person feeling powerless. Hero came to me on a run last summer in rainy Paris amidst the demise of my first real romantic relationship (right around when I wrote Boded, my other sound drop). Directionless and phone-less, I ran, ran, and didn't stop running until I reached a soccer field where I sat on the ground cinematically asking god and the higher powers to show me the way. In my head, the phrase "I'm no hero, I'm no hero..." was on repeat, haunting me until I entertained it. In the midst of feeling truly average, "just a sovereign waiting for the bus, I'm no hero" came to me and I stepped into the powerlessness cause I knew the song existed there, in the surrender to what seemed like weakness. What I only figured out in retrospect is that this "low point" swerved me into a lane that gave me a simply complex song about crumbling in order to build again. This song heavily references things that have made me who I am - Paris, Back to Black by Amy Winehouse, Miles Davis trying to stay relevant after his peak, needing a spaceship to dance cause I take up space, me being a full time artist with other jobs, being my parents pride and joy even when I don't feel like I am worthy, and bleaching my hair only to see the my natural hair come back in relentlessly (this timeless feat is as literal as it is metaphorical). This song was written as a freestyle over a Dolceola line and a hip hop inspired drum beat, layered with ethereal background vocals. I hope it finds you as much as it found me.

records.title: GLORiFiED

Welcome to a new ERA in MAiWORLD. 

WORLD 1 (a 7-song origin story of how MAiWORLD began) was my first Web3 release across Catalog, Audius, Emanate, and my custom contract. I even turned the storyline of WORLD 1 into a playable Gameboy game that mirrors MAiWORLD's creation with playable levels based on the songs. Although, to be honest, GARAGE TAPES VOL. 1 was originally going to be the first project I ever released as an artist. 

GARAGE TAPES is a catalog of songs initially made in my garage. In the earliest stages of MAiWORLD's creation, I made an entire ERA of music from MAi garage.  I experimented with making many different songs during this time, and a relationship I was in at the time was one of the biggest inspirations for me. "GLORiFiED" is a song about that relationship. 

Initially written and produced five years ago from the garage, "GLORiFiED" has been reproduced/mixed countless times; this was going to be one of the first songs I released as an artist.

The song starts off with a raw (and real) voicemail that leads into the lyrics that paint a scene from that time.

From the relationship I was in, to the music I was making, I didn’t want to give up on either; but I felt like I was giving my all for something that I could never do.

Welcome to GARAGE TAPES VOL. 1

records.title: Son of a Gun

records.note: Son of a Gun.  One of my favorites off the upcoming album.  Something that feels like it has centuries of history behind it.  It was supposed to be the intro, then the outro, then found itself at track 10.  This song is probably the most New England//CT thing I’ve made.   I was scared of it for a while because of this reasons - it's out there. It has a lot of “Christian Felner” (my real name) in it.  Felly takes a seat for this one.  But it has this dark tone to it that I think is sacred and true to me. It feels like a horse.  You ever look into a horses eyes?  Feels like you can see hundreds of years in there.  I don’t think many people understand this song and I always look at people after playing it and just sitting with the fact that, from where I stand, it seems it went right over their head. The song is sort of about only being here for a period of time. The fragility of life, and how we're all alone.  And that feeling you can reach in life where there is no place to actually call home.  Being cast into the world alone…pretty much.  It comes from touring, from meeting so many strangers, and ultimately feeling like its still just me.  If you get this one you get it and if you don’t that's alright with me.

records.title: HOLD ON
records.creator: 0xBee3AB5f0FE1600C1ca08d3d71e712AA31E5f6c2
records.note:
I started making music in my childhood bedroom when it was just me and a cracked version of logic. Back then, I released about a song a week on SoundCloud, but after signing with a label, I had to distribute my creativity between creating a brand and making music. I've got great people around me helping me get back to the process I fell in love with; conceptualizing, recording, and just putting it out there. 

The eeriness flows from those intrusive thoughts, you know, the ones that hit you late at night and send you in a never-ending loop. Finding something to hold onto, whatever that may be brings you back to the reality that you are in control of how you deal with shit. Being able to embrace the ebb and flow of making music in a digital world.

“HOLD ON” started with this gritty guitar riff which got me thinking about my experience in the cycle of highs and lows in the music industry. We wanted this darker tone with dryer vocals but to also have fun with it. When the lyrics started flowing, it created this dance between the lyrics guiding the beat and the beat driving the lyrics.

records.title: how do u feel?
records.creator: 0x4f6D0cA7E66D5e447862793F23904ba15F51f4De
records.note:
I don’t always like the world I’m in so I build my own. Wherever I go. I’ve always found escape in music when the world around me got scary or disappointing. My earliest memories are of being alone with my CD player and imagining things in my head — like playing shows with giant crowds and my guitar. I felt a lot of pain and rejection, and created my own reality where someone like me is a superstar. 

I created Krash World, a magical world made in my own image loosely based on reality, back in 2019. It’s a world for anyone feels out of place to be a superstar. I want to show kids and adults alike that they don’t have to fit into anything, they can carve out their own space.



“how do u feel?” is my take on 80s synth pop/rock. my most recent explorations have been with four on the floor kick patterns, simple dance-inspired drums, groove and lots of room for vocals to shine. 

i made this song reflecting on myself and failed relationships, desire and love addiction. if you ever felt like there’s a person you just can’t seem to shake emotionally even after a breakup, this song is for you. i reflect the idea that you can become addicted to a person just like someone might be addicted to drugs or alcohol or caffeine, and what that feels like. 


there’s a desperation to these feelings that is equally intoxicating and irritating. there’s a lot of double meanings throughout the song, reflecting the dual nature of love, desire and love addiction. red is the color that came up when i listened back to the song and it was the perfect tone for the feeling i got. red can mean STOP, danger, anger, and blood or it can stand for love and desire.

two sides of the same coin.

records.title: There's No Other One
records.creator: 0xc2469e9D964F25c58755380727a1C98782a219ac
records.note:
I’m Glassface. I’ve been creating music my entire life. I’ve spent the past 10 years working as a music video / commercial director and visual artist, moonlighting as a producer & songwriter for other artists. In the past few years I’ve come to realize the importance of sharing my music with the world, putting my head down to finish some of the myriad of demos I have in the vault. Putting everything into the music. In the past 3 months, I’ve released 3 new songs with accompanying visuals. “There’s No Other One” is my 4th release this year, and is truly special to me. Oh, and I’m just getting started.

There’s No Other One is a mix of some of my favorite things. Produced by Matti Free and me, we brought together live guitar and drums, pitched toms, analog synths under a cutting vocal. Minimal 80’s-inspired pop rock leading into a crescendo of maximalist electronic production.

Nodding to favorite artists of mine including Daft Punk and Francis & The Lights - the song is an amalgamation of influences. It’s really important to me to make the music that I want to hear. Lyrically, it’s about a moment of clarity - that feeling when everything comes together and makes sense. A somber night drive of self-discovery. The electricity you feel after a life-affirming realization. Disguised as a love song, I’d say “There’s No Other One” is more of a self-love song. When I realized I was the only one who could accomplish my dreams, it empowered me, and I knew I was unstoppable. It’s about staying the course and letting that feeling be a North Star. I really believe in what I’m doing. This song is for anyone who has had that realization that they are that one.

records.title: evil
records.creator: 0x5Bf82000F39fc02eAF98929b3F411A0234d0fDca
records.note:
Sometimes, as artists, and simply as people, we go through periods where nothing we create feels quite right. These periods normally expire within a relatively short timeframe, but can feel like an eternity. We bang our heads, over and over again, trying to find the perfect sound, paired to the exact feeling we mean to convey, and while this may seem fairly straightforward, it can feel like a truly insoluble puzzle. 

It had been a few months since I'd made a song I felt connected to, and I had been operating within said headspace throughout these months. Life just felt a bit lackluster, as it always seems to do when the one thing I care about most becomes the hardest to make; music. I'll never know whether it was due to the personal affairs of my daily life, or something indescribable much deeper inside me, and truly I'll never care. The reason for this is, I view these periods of dullness as essential for artists. In the same way that happiness is hard to understand without a grasp on sadness, an artist cannot create their absolute best without experiencing their worst.

Entering this mode of uncertainty always seems to be a slow trickled effect, while exiting it is usually quite sudden. Many times it's an experience which wakes the artist up, other times it is a new song or album they hear. For me, it was a person, another music creator, who took me out of my creative hole, and helped me create this art.

I made Evil with my close friend and collaborator, Jason (JVSE). His style of music creation is extremely unique, and from the very first time we worked, I could tell my days of uncertainty within my own music creation were over. We have created quite a bit of music together, but the night we made “evil,” we both knew it was special. The song was unlike anything either of us had ever made, joining elements of both of our individual styles in a way we could never imagine without actually putting it on the paper. I truly believe being in the headspace I was in gave the song room to be authentically sorrowful, and Jason always understands how to create a perfectly represented production for whatever my lyrics and melody ask for. So to simplify things, “evil” is really a marriage between the dullest and most difficult moments in my life, and the highs and inspiring moments. Without experiencing the contrast of both, there is no evil, and truthfully, there is no lilspirit.

dilip:
greydient and I kept running into each other in multiple discords in late 2021 and a friendship was quickly born. I sent him a rough demo for a song idea. Since then, we’ve experienced Songcamp’s Camp Chaos together, performed at NFT NYC together, and now finally turned the demo into a song together. 

greydient:
I remember getting this song idea from dilip while I was in Austin at CabinDAO’s node 0. I knew that there was something to this song, but not sure how I could fit my style into it. It wasn’t until I got back home to Toronto and pulled up the song during Xmas holidays that the magic began. I infused a little of the Toronto darkness into dilip’s original idea and the rest you’ll get to hear on the song. 

This drop is just the start of a musical history together. If you want to know what else we’ve got cooking up our sleeves, you definitely want to get tapped in.

records.title: Paramount - Golden Egg
records.creator: 0x905BC9437f48c87dE598648d051d6cD6fbdf036D
records.note:
Have you ever found yourself metaphorically staring at the mountain of things you have to do and becoming anxious?  Has fear ever stopped you from following through? I know I have.  The very appearance of my lofty goals can sometimes paralyze me.

Paramount examines this paradigm between two perspectives: first from a third person’s rhetorical vantage point and then from my own personal experiences with complacency, procrastination and failure.

I’ve learned in this life, you can’t be afraid to fail.  Every great anything/anybody has failed, often times, more than they succeed.  I’ve come to find that the true secret to success is not being afraid to risk not obtaining it.

As a listener, I hope this song is your new anthem to get things done!  Remember those things that are paramount in your life and keep climbing!

records.title: In The Smoke
records.creator: 0x40d65Ec8870D0fCA1197593291F873Fb0B3787Db
records.note:
In The Smoke is my genesis Sound.xyz drop and my third music NFT, following two sold out collections earlier this year. It’s a self-confronting song about choosing to leave the life you have in pursuit of the unknown. It’s from the perspective of a woman on the edge, where it’s uncertain if she’s having a breakdown or a break through. Perhaps a combination of both. 

Growing up in a small town in the north east of Scotland, I’ve always been exposed to the great outdoors, bad weather and a kind of social conditioning that you shouldn’t ask for too much in life. Much of my music takes influence from those themes, of wondering what it would mean to take a certain fork in the road and what my place is in the world. Since discovering web 3, I can feel my own internal changes taking place as new paths present themselves. The music community, specifically, has provided me with all the tools, unwavering support and cultural values I was struggling to find elsewhere. To be looking out towards a future where I’m able to exist in this space as a full time, independent artist is something I still can’t quite believe. I’m wholeheartedly embracing it.

Although I wrote and recorded this song here in Edinburgh, I also brought on my longterm producer Lucas Mendes to make his web 3 debut from his studio in London. We wanted to be fairly restrained in our approach to this song and to capture its uneasy nature. Lucas intricately layered guitars and plucked strings and provided the texture, detail and depth that the song required. He also mixed the song remotely with me - one of my favourite parts of the creative process where you can map out every nuance. He is my wizard.

I hope my music will provide a little salve to your wounds and act as an outlet for whatever you need it for.

emma xx

records.title: WTH
records.creator: 0x3470151D1c87597623E53FaE98E4Bc585e6cC709
records.note:
It all started when I picked up my father’s guitar and taught myself how to play some chords on Youtube. That moment alone led to me writing original songs and finding my true identity.

After making it to Top 200 on American Idol but later getting rejected, I found the courage shortly after to drop myself out of University and make the 14hr drive to Music City aka Nashville, TN, where I found my calling. I knew when my windshield met the Batman building in the skyline, that’s where I was meant to chase my dreams.

As a Cuban-American singer/songwriter, my purpose is to represent the Hispanic culture in Modern Country. I didn’t see any other artist filling those boots so I saw that as a great opportunity to start a movement and bring awareness to the genre by combining my love for Latin music and the storytelling element of Country Music. 

After 13 years of writing thousands of songs, working with many other writers and even being signed and dropped by Sony Music in 2017, I continued strumming along and found some hope on Spotify and TikTok. I dropped by debut album Oct 2021 and found some success on TikTok and Instagram Reels, gaining over 40M independent music streams and over 100M video impressions in under 2 years. This led to nationwide tours, incredible brand partnerships and way more…

In Nov 2021, I was introduced to web3 and NFTs by a close friend from back home in Miami, FL. Little did I know, this introduction was gonna change my career and my life forever. Since starting my NFT journey, we have sold over 6500 Music NFTs and proudly stand as the founder of 3 Music NFT collections -  METAGIRL, Pulse Pass & PIXELATED. These were all released on my own smart contracts and were organically minted via Twitter Spaces and rigorous hours connecting with the community on Discord. 

My genesis drop on Sound is “WTH” (What The Hell). This song was inspired by stubborn love and chasing someone knowing that it’s only gonna end in heartbreak. 

As someone that considers himself a hopeless romantic, this song definitely means so much to me. I look forward to releasing this one out in the world and hope it resonates with other hopeless romantics hopelessly loving someone as they hear this song.

- SAMMY

records.title: Mirror
records.creator: 0x96C1a82864671fBc31F8Ddf3F862999734ab7C29
records.note:
While working on this record I was aware that this didn’t sound anything like how I’m supposed to.  But I guess that’s why it excited me.  I always talk with artists I work with and we frequently get on the subject of how their music never sounds like what they actually like to listen to.  I always thought that was odd, almost wrong.  Mirror sounds like the type of music that I…usually listen to.  Not all the time, but if I’m on a plane or just cooling out…I’m playing stuff like Bon Iver, the Shins, Modest Mouse… Almost calming, soul nurturing records. I was laughing with a friend about how everyone’s always trying to make the hardest most in your face record (which I’ve done dozens of times), and about the power in the opposite.  

I’ve been working on this record for 2 years and always knew it would eventually come out, just needed to find the right time.  I played this last week for my friend Rey, who is one of my favorite painters/artists probably living, his response was “I can’t believe you made this”.  That’s probably the best thing I could have heard.

The songs about being honest with yourself, even about the ugly shit.  It’s a tune of ambivalence.  And is sort of on the subject of not knowing.  Not exactly being sure.  Trying to face yourself but the image keeps changing.  Trying to see what is actually there, and what you’re just dreaming up.   I think today people can toxically be like, “Face your demons! Change your life! Get your act together!”  I think it’s way more complex than that and that we are constantly shape-shifting.  Sometimes you’re the fool, sometimes you’re a genius, sometimes criminal.  The song sort of deals with facing all of these sides. 


My good friend and touring partner Sol Was played bass on it, his brother Henry played the drums. Johan Lenox did the strings and backgrounds.  Hope you enjoy.

records.title: Brothers Talk Demo
records.creator: 0x889ca9161034ECC87D51677C0D775Fbe1D3499e5
records.note:
I started working on a project called OG Cool (Only Good Comes Out Of Living) in the fall of 2013 with one of my best friends, super-producer, Nash B. During that period of time we recorded 30-40 songs towards what I thought would be the final album. The summer of the following year I lost the only hard-drive that had every session file/track-out and bounce for my entire catalog of unreleased music (1200+ songs/production/demos) to that point, (OG Cool included). A few years ago I began to recover some of the music from that hard-drive (Thank God for clouds and email accounts lol) One of my favorites from those album sessions (and closest to me) is a song called "Brothers Talk".

Growing up in the states as a child to an immigrant family, I grew used to not having a lot of blood-related family around me. It was always just me and my little brothers. This upbringing conditioned me to value the people closest to me as family and not just friends.
"Brothers Talk" was a chance for me to hold a conversation with two close friends (that have always been brothers to me) during their times of need. One friend lost a father and the other lost his way.
I originally intended on placing this on the album but for now this is a just a marker for major moments in time. This is the last bounce I did after I originally recorded the record at my home studio.

Much love to the good homie, Myles Stefan for the amazing guitar solo at the end and my lil bro Nash B for supporting me getting back to my production (I made this beat). This song is in honor of my blood brothers Chris and Thorence (Long Live Baby Thor). I consider the people who care enough to listen to and support my music my family. records.title: Snow Globe
records.creator: 0xD08924607d051ab304A319BCfBa040c8F3E75B11
records.note:
We wrote Snow Globe after being hit with the first major snowstorm of the season in 2021 while writing our record, Islanders, on Mackinac Island. We’d anticipated being snowed in prior to moving into our Island apartment and setting up our studio. When the snow started falling from the thick clouds, engulfing the island, we knew it was time to start in on our song "Snow Globe".

Weather can change on a dime on Mackinac Island because of its position nestled in Lake Huron and north of the 45th parallel. The aim was to capture the other-worldly phenomenon that only this small island can experience; existing in a real-life snow globe.

"Snow Globe" was produced by FINKEL and Josh Stadlen, mixed by Khushi, and mastered by Dale Becker. “Snow Globe” is the last song of our album, Islanders, which also serves as the score of our feature-length documentary also titled, Islanders. To watch the documentary, head to islandersfilm.com.

Listen is track 4 off the new project, which I haven’t officially announced to the public.  But it is coming in December.  The project is a journey, almost feels like a road trip, reminiscent of a kerouac novel - but tinted by the strange, modern, polluted times we are in now.   

I remember playing this record after previewing Young Fel 2 to my label at the time.  We had just finished playing a lot of the darker records off of YF2 and some of the label heads had stepped out to take calls, and finish their business.  I continued playing unreleased records of mine and Listen was the first one I played after the album.  It lit up the room.  It felt like the light at the end of the tunnel and I remember my friend Clay (who did the artwork for this nft as well as all the upcoming ones), giving me this look of…shit, well when is that one dropping? records.title: when you feel like dying
records.creator: 0xC59ADDC6EF782e002332BC8E4442bCc6b4879B01
records.note: This song is the title track for my album. This album means everything to me. I have never poured out my heart the way I did with these songs. I have a fear of not making the best music I am capable of making before I die, so I push myself as hard as I can everyday to try and achieve that. For every chip on my shoulder that I have gained, this album is in retaliation for that. Every time I have been pushed and shoved to be a certain type of artist, it has brought me closer to this. I once had a manager threaten to ruin my career, and told me I'd be singing songs in my room for the rest of my life. My career hadn’t even started yet. When I was with a major label, nothing I made was good enough. I was never good enough. I went on a TV singing show and I was told I wasn't good enough in front of millions of people, and was bombarded with so much hate on the internet, it made me throw up. I have had my indie managers that told me I was "way too basic and nothing about me was special", and my pop managers told me "if it's not a hit then throw it away. You have to be perfect." I was born and raised in West Hollywood, so maybe these are years that I couldn’t have avoided. After dealing with that for 6 years, after feeling like I was a piece of dough for everyone to mold, I finally snapped. I shut all the voices out. I’m not impressionable anymore. The freedom I feel to finally be creating whatever I want, is the most incredible feeling in the world. Produced, written, & mixed by me.

records.creator: 0x3585CA22dF80D70f6D1cC0867D8387c360181349
records.note:
Hip Hop, Jungle and UK Bass are musical siblings, eternally connected through their cultural roots. So it is no coincidence that the heart of Kabuki beats for all of these seemingly disparate genres. For more than 20 years his music productions covered the full spectrum of beat science, but misty-eyed nostalgia isn’t Kabuki’s thing. Instead, he is more interested in the present and future of electronic music. And more than style and aesthetics he is in pursuit of the elusive element that keeps it all moving: the soul

For me a good remix should showcase an aspect of the original that went by unnoticed. So my first course of action was to familiarise myself with the source material in search of a creative spark. I eventually found a background vocal which became the nucleus of the track, adding a completely new twist to the melody by means of reharmonisation. I also wanted to expand on the UK Garage vibe of the original by adding a Jungle twist and paying homage to my. roots. The end result stays true to the original while sitting comfortably between all genre definitions.

records.note:
AmbieNFT is a generative modular synth music NFT project that has topped the top of the blocks and plumbed the depths of synthesis depravity. Over the past year sixty-two pieces have been generatively created and human refined … their traits, modules, tempos and keys governed by an all-seeing hexadecimal hash.

On this Sound of Fractures remix I worked backwards from the shuffled chorus shaker, anchoring the track around it and introducing some polyrhythms by displacing elements of the original beat. Some house’y arpeggios quickly materialized and before long I had worked my way backwards all the way to an ambient rhodes + modular synth introduction that laid a nice foundation for a verse vocal feature.

records.note:
I released the official production of “Grateful” a few weeks ago, and I wanted to try something new on here. First off, as a thank you to everyone who collected the first edition, you are all receiving this drop for free! And to anyone who wasn’t able to collect the official drop (*cough cough my dad*) this one is for you. This release is actually the first demo that I made of “Grateful” back in 2020. The execution of the vocal is emotional yet super raw, and the lyrics aren’t quite as locked as the official drop, but there is a magic to it that I am so in love with and I think deserves to be appreciated too. Which, of course, made me think of you all! I love the idea of web3 setting the standard for a new artist/fan/friend relationship, and I want my work here to reflect that. This drop for me represents the opening of my green-room, and a welcome to my studio, where I get to share all the mistakes along the way, all the lessons learned, and all of the fun behind writing and producing music I love. Y’all all the first to hear this version of the song, and if you feel inspired to collect it, thank you, and I appreciate you so much. Cheers to getting to know one another!

-Nico

"Grateful" is about how to ease the blush of unfamiliarity when entering a new relationship. I wrote it when I made friends with the feeling of having just enough fuel to jump AND just enough fear to shut my eyes when I do it. This song is quite a bit more specific than my previous releases. As “Stuck” talked about trusting the feeling over the circumstance, and “Paint in the Dark” described the over-arching agreements that I have observed in the healthiest love, “Grateful” exemplifies these themes using the intimacy of a pillow talk conversation. It is about putting what I’ve learned into action and trusting what happens next.

records.title: ENCARTE
records.creator: 0xa49F720BF331A5E701F452321d997a01336eD315
records.note:
“Encarte”, tiene un sonido fresco electrónico, pero con un trasfondo íntimo que contrasta el sonido de la canción, aquí se habla sobre los problemas de ansiedad, y ansiedad social que enfrenta todo el tiempo una persona, estos problemas le hacen tener miedo a enamorarse y dejar que se enamoren de ella, haciendo que su primer pretendiente entre en alerta antes de decidir entrar en una relación amorosa con la misma.  “Encarte” es un término muy utilizado en Colombia para referirse a cosas que se interpreten como una carga pesada difícil de llevar, muy molesta e incomoda. 

Verónica Caicedo, actriz, cantante, rapera y compositora de Buenaventura - Colombia, estudiante de Licenciatura en Arte Dramático. Desde el 2018 comenzó un proceso musical que incluía videos y composiciones caseras, se hizo muy conocida en varios lugares del país, y más adelante formaliza su entrada a la industria musical lanzando sus dos primeras canciones, “Don José” y “Yo Soy Dios”, ambas producidas por Colombo, y Sammy el Comandante, estas marcaron el inicio de su carrera musical y hoy con 5 lanzamientos musicales es una de las referentes de la cuarta generación de artistas más importante de su país.

"Encarte" has a fresh electronic sound, but with an intimate background that contrasts the sound of the song, here we talk about anxiety problems, and social anxiety that a person faces all the time, these problems make them afraid of fall in love and let them fall in love with her, causing her first suitor to go on alert before deciding to enter into a love relationship with her. "Encarte" is a term widely used in Colombia to refer to things that are interpreted as a heavy load that is difficult to carry, very annoying and uncomfortable.

Verónica Caicedo, actress, singer, rapper and composer from Buenaventura - Colombia, Bachelor of Dramatic Arts student. Since 2018, he began a musical process that produced videos and homemade compositions, became well known in various parts of the country, and later formalized his entry into the music industry by releasing his first two songs, "Don José" and "Yo Soy Dios" , both produced by Colombo, and Sammy el Comandante, these marked the beginning of his musical career and today, with 5 musical releases, he is one of the references of the fourth generation of most important artists in his country.

records.title: Don't Have to Explain
records.creator: 0x414CA9c0e2FcCc222ca1c5f4cC77Ca685dd03F7d
records.note:
While I continue to grow up and be a teenager, I feel so many emotions all at once. The good, the bad, the crazy. It’s hard to pinpoint where everything stems from. I tend to struggle with how fast time flies by, too busy focusing on trying to slow down the present, that I miss what’s already happened. And there are times where I find people questioning my beliefs, or my feelings towards others. As humans, we are constantly juggling so many different aspects in our life, trying to find a balance. 

Devan and I love this track. We make all our music together and give it our all every time. Magic is the only outcome. I like to think that this song creates an escape for all of us. Or even a safe place to be ourselves. A place to finally exhale. Without judgment, without fear, without stress, and without worries. 

‘Don’t Have to Explain’ spreads a little light on all the flourishing stresses we have. About making decisions, wanting to pause and be in the moment, and even protecting our own space. We should never feel obligated to have to explain ourselves. We should be open and understanding of each other. We should encourage and learn from one another. 

Be present.  
Be mindful. 
Be grateful. 
When you listen to this song, know that you are here. 
And you don’t have to explain a thing. 

- mia lailani & devan ibiza 
<3

records.title: Sundreamer
records.creator: 0x17c72771bB6B283baDe0C07E0901744C37Ff8c41
records.note:
'Sundreamer' represents a bit of a rebirth for me. Going through the loss of my father this past year crushed a lot of my creative spirit. My dad was someone I could always send my demos to and he would use his keen ears to give me feedback. Part of the joy I got from making music was getting to share my work with him. Losing him took a lot out of me. 

Even before my dad got sick, I was on a strange trajectory with music. I was pretty caught up in trying to make music that would perform well on streaming services. Often I would optimize my songs to fit Spotify playlists so I could make a decent income. The downside of that was that I was making quite a few creative sacrifices and just wasn’t enjoying what I was making anymore. 

With ‘Sundreamer’ I’m going back to my roots of making music for the joy of it. I’m in a new creative chapter now and am shedding that popularity-centric point of view. Music and creativity are so important to me that I need to let them flourish before I worry about anything else. 

I’m back to basics, making music that speaks to my soul.

Last month I did a free drop for the demo of this song on Sound, and now before releasing on any other platforms, I'm dropping the full song! 

To catch you up to speed on the story of the song: 
Earlier this year, I was in a long-distance relationship with a girl from Florida. Shortly after her and I broke up, I was back down in Florida with Friends and spent a little too much time and money trying to forget I was hurting. I went to bars and casinos and let loose. Weirdly enough, I had started a demo called "down in florida", months prior, that nearly described the exact situation I now found myself in with her. I didn't have the words to finish the song until I was back in Nashville a week later and decided to continue writing the song from my current situation. Hence, the opening of the second verse "i'm back in Nashville..." This track tells the story of how I did anything but face the truth of my reality. I wasn't ready to face the consequences of my actions.

My team and I are committed to growing in the Web 3 space and are confident that your investments in my music will be more than worth it! I've amassed over 200 million streams independently and, as I'm now dropping a song every two weeks, the music will only grow quicker than ever. - Munn

records.title: Probably Nothing
records.creator: 0xbeEb460081C1E3820A6AFAa309C6D3C45F465335
records.note:
This was one of those songs that took me back to a moment in time when I wrote it...

Early 2010
Hollywood, California
Los Angeles Recording School

I was 17 years old when I graduated high school. I almost immediately moved from Orange County to LA. I couldn't get out of my mom's house quick enough. I just wanted to feel like an adult. To be in my own apartment. To be in college. To just live.

I thought going to recording school was the answer to all my prayers. I would learn everything I needed to know about recording + engineering. I would graduate and start making music. Then get signed. Then... I don't know. That was as far as I thought it through. Everything would go as planned.

Yeah... nope.

School just wasn't for me. Los Angeles wasn't for me. Hollywood wasn't for me. And truthfully, there was a time when I thought music just wasn't for me.

This song is about that time.

Looking back I feel like I needed that experience. I feel like understanding what we don't want is sometimes just as important as understanding what we do want.

And I don't want that life. Of course I want to be able to live and create and provide for my family but I don't believe that the "Hollywood Route" is the only way.

So here we are 12 years later in Web 3 dropping NFTs and just figuring this sh*t out.

And I'm not mad at it...

Thank you to all of you for showing me that there's another way.

All love, always.

Push Me Too Far

cover art blend with ai and edited by Mari

In my feelings one night, playing with ableton, this song started to pour out. I was tired of being caught in cycles that never break no matter how painful they become. Patterns in music and patterns in life. Cycles of abuse or misunderstanding that led to pain in intimacy, community and larger exploitative institutions. Infused in this song is a vow: this will be the last time. With this release I am empowering myself as a sovereign artist and individual: alive, human, imperfect, and fully embodied.

After living with this song for a while, I brought it to Segnon’s studio to track some bass from Clark Simz. Clark laid down his brilliant bass and Seg and I watched the song shift directions. This version was asking to be more raw. Channeling being pushed too far, I broke my voice, then sustained that tension until my breath went out and the song could find release. 

I love that the culture and technology within web3 allow us to break free from institutionalized patterns of control. And I won’t come back ;) This is the first drop from MARI season 1.

records.title: cantaloupe ave.
records.creator: 0xC59ADDC6EF782e002332BC8E4442bCc6b4879B01
records.note:
I’m Valentina Cy, and I’m an LA born and raised (and never left) artist. I have been singing since I could speak, and I was raised in a house where making music was second nature. When I was 22 I went to a scholarship program created by Mike Posner called Amor Fati, where he took 5 artists and 10 mentors  to Telluride Colorado, and taught each one of all skills that we needed to become better artists. I was taught how to make a demo on Ableton. Since then I have been producing, writing, and mixing all my music. 

I am a self-managed independent artist, and I am gearing up to release an album November 16th. The album is called ‘when you feel like dying’. The first song I am dropping on Sound is a single from the album. It’s called ‘cantaloupe ave.’ and it’s a song that I had to cry a lot to make. I used a voice memo from someone in my past, and I wrote the song about them as well. The cover art is also a picture of the street that they used to live on. This song is essentially very simple. It’s comprised of a cut up voice memo, my friend Gabe Noel on the cello, a kick, some fucked up piano, and vocals. I like when a song is able to hit me where it hurts, and this one did that for me.

A few months ago I almost quit music and I didn’t really feel like I had a purpose in life anymore. It took me making cantaloupe ave., and this entire album, to make it feel like I had something worth living for. That might sound ironic since the name of the album is ‘when you feel like dying’, but sometimes you have to leech all the bad out to feel something good.

There's a yearning for liberation that can only be satiated in private. By recording myself alone, I found the prowess to move and perform freely, capturing moments that wouldn't have existed otherwise. “Private Room” is a song about wanting to share that private liberation with someone. 

I had stopped making music for a while before working on this track. Changing my stage name from Eunice to YUNICE symbolize my recommitment back into being an artist. I moved to LA from Lisbon in June ’22 with four suitcases and my cat. Feeling the bear market struggles, I crashed on friends’ couches while looking for a private room to rent, and took the plunge into the music NFT scene. 

TB, a music producer who’s worked with major label artists, found me on instagram and wanted to work together. I was skeptical at first but took the chance and met with him. We clicked instantly on a profound artistic level. We wrote “Private Room” in our first meeting. It was almost too intense how much he understood my vocals and vision. I wanted dark and sexy and some cello, and we made just that.

records.title: NEW TURN
records.creator: 0xBb81E31F69181C5B74C126D8cC2B036801AF04b8
records.note:
Hello!

Everyone of us has a new turn in life we eventually all take. For some it can be warm, tender and harmonious. For others it's rough, dire, and difficult. In this life, everyday, we experience situations that lead us to two things: a choice and a chance. The combination of these two concepts can create a New Turn for the best or for the worst. Living in New York City, I'm constantly witnessing these new experiences unfold. Dreamers come to the big apple for a New Turn to make their dreams come true, their goals a reality, to pursue the life they dream of having, and some come here simply to escape their own reality.

As I grew up, discovering music as a full time career became my New Turn. In the midst of all the noise and ruckus this city brings, I find the most clarity and silence through it all. I met Deffie IRL back in May 2022, though before the real life interaction, we had been connected over Discord during the pandemic. We managed to create an 8 track project consisting of features from MIA GLADSTONE, as well as co-production from myself. Before the collaboration, for years, I was a genuine fan of DEFFIE’s. I remember regularly playing some of his biggest hits on Soundcloud like “Backstroke” & “Gaskethead”. Upon creating this tape, we both were beginning to find a home in web3, and as we're rolling out our own projects a year later, here we are creating a New Turn in the space, hoping this sound inspires anyone to take that leap of faith themselves.

- THOMAS

records.title: Thank You
records.creator: 0xDdA26Be4311Ed1f7159f97B9a97021581a85889B
records.note:
As somebody who is always moving and shaking, I felt it was a period where God forced me to sit down and reevaluate whats really important in life. The song “Thank You” was inspired by that time. I had a ruptured achilles which put me out of work, and in what I call a “space boot” (cast)  for six months. For the first few months I could hardly do anything. I Even needed my wife to get in and out of the shower. 

  It was starting to get depressing, but then one day at physical therapy I was looking around at people in way worse situations than me. Some we’re probably never even going to be able to walk again. But they were all smiling and doing what they had to do to improve their situation. It was that moment something clicked for me, and I started to look at my own situation in a positive light. 

  I was finally just home. No traveling, none of the constant stresses of work, and most importantly I got to be with my wife and kids everyday. We would take frequent vacations and even though I couldn't walk, I was happier spending time with my loved ones than I had been in years. Time is the most valuable thing that we have on this planet, and it’s expiring from the very second your born. I wrote this song because I was thankful for that time period. My family and friends showed me that even when your out hustling trying to elevate in life, never lose sight of whats truly important. God showed me the real reason to be Thankful. Thank You…

records.title: DIE DOWN
records.creator: 0x70E74826bc0237662F4BF6190093d5226F1661a3
records.note:
Hi my name is Cailin Russo. I’ve been a singer-songwriter for almost 10 years. I was raised in San Diego California by 2 punk rock and rollers and a fan of music since the day I entered the earth. My father is in a pop punk band called Unwritten Law, he was the first to invite me into the songwriting space when I was 16. We had just suffered a house fire and were staying at a family friend's house who had the first recording equipment I had ever seen (consciously). From that point on I wrote songs semi religiously. 
 
	I signed to a label a couple years later and began my serious musical journey. I dropped my first song called “September Rose” which did really well and is still one of my highest streamed songs, it is about love coming in at the wrong time. This tone of writing became a staple in a lot of my songs; very melancholic, feminine/ sexy. From there I continued to drop 2/3 more songs in a similar genre then completely switched up everything and started a very no doubt esq feeling band. The band lasted about 2 years and then we broke apart for me to continue to see my solo career bloom. 
 
	After breaking apart from the band and label completely I was on a quest of rediscovery and rebirth. I made a complete body of work compiling all my favorite elements from indie, electronic and r&b. Independent from any label I am dropping my second single off the album “DIE DOWN”. DIE DOWN is a dark electronic song that was made by myself and JJ Scheffy in his basement mid pandemic. The story around the song is about 2 star crossed lovers that take their romance and inhibitions all the way to a point where nothing else exists. Everything else dies down.

records.title: has anybody seen me?
records.creator: 0x19250B770Efd981c855195d0CE674F811f350f42
records.note:
Several years ago, seemingly out of nowhere, my mind sort of betrayed me. 

I had developed an anxiety disorder that was, in a word, crippling. 
'Panic disorder', my doctor called it. 
In a nutshell, my mind would play games on me. When explaining it  to people now, I sometimes say to imagine that heightened anxiety or fear you get when something scares you (a feeling that usually dissipates after you realize you aren't in real danger) as a permanent feeling. Like the pit you get in your stomach during the free-fall of a rollercoaster ride, except it never goes away. 

At the time, I felt like I couldn't talk to anyone about what I was feeling because I thought no one would understand- I myself barely understood what was happening to me. It was an incredibly scary and lonely experience, (that fortunately I was eventually able to come out of thanks to therapy and medication), and I really felt like a complete stranger to myself and to everyone around me.  

I wrote 'has anybody seen me?' about that time. 

I really hope you enjoy this record. It was produced by two incredible producers, Mike Daley and Mitchell Owens. 

10% of the sales of this record will go directly to one of my favorite organizations, The Loveland Foundation, providing opportunity, therapy and healing to communities of color, especially for Black women and girls. Thank you for helping support this incredibly important organization.

records.title: Better With You
records.creator: 0xbeEb460081C1E3820A6AFAa309C6D3C45F465335
records.note:
I feel at peace after my last release.

I feel like there has been a lot on my head + heart lately that I needed to get off before moving forward. Life can throw a lot at us and I know that things can not always go as planned but I'm in a space where I just want to share my music with you all. 

I don't want to overthink it. I don't want to stress. I don't want to wait. So this is the first of my weekly releases to close out the year.

Each of these songs are moments in time and I'm grateful that we can share them together.

I remember recording the hook to this song first which I usually never do. It was like 3 in the morning and I had so much energy but I couldn't come up with the words to fill in the verses so I decided not to force it.

I probably let it sit for another day or two then when I finally came back to it the words just flowed.

"Tell me baby one time at least..."

And this song was born. It also has one of my favorite bars I've ever written:

"I think about you daily, you like my blood you call me 'Bae' I'd rather call you brazy... I saw the red flags early."

Like... come on guys. 🤣

I know I repeatedly say this, but Web³ has completely changed how I think about my music. How I release it. The value I place on it. What I truly want my message and impact to be.

And I will always put the music first. That is my only promise. There may be times where I need to tend to me. Times where I'm not as active on social media or I can't show up in the ways I would like to. But I promise you that if I put a song out into the world that I gave it my all.

Thank you guys for supporting me. For the constant reminder that I am walking the path I am meant to walk. 

All love, always.

records.title: White Paint (prod. Sango)
records.creator: 0xECB18Df1b88A0Bb623C28831806DB123CEb7d73c
records.note:
An artist's journey 

With every project and musical endeavor I always try to approach it with a different perspective, like all artists I assume, in hopes of creating something new. That journey has brought me to the web 3 space and Soundxyz.
 
Like many artists, I’ve spent the last couple years exploring web 3, studying the use cases and trying to pinpoint just exactly where I fit in the space. I always aim to maintain a sense of quality and authenticity with the content I release, even when it may result in great ideas being left on the proverbial cutting room floor. 

‘White Paint’ was one of the songs born from many sessions, originally supposed to land on an EP I made called ‘Vista”. When Sango sent the original beat, and while writing the song I remember thinking “this is different, this is new”. This is the moment we as creatives strive for right? To break new ground within ourselves, taking a risk on you and it actually working out. 

When going over the tracklist for the project, ‘White Paint’ ultimately didn't make it. It may have been too different from what everything else on the EP sounded like. Which unfortunately, was what a lot of music we listen to now sounds like. I have a tendency to second guess an idea that doesn't “fit”, deem it unworthy of consumption, and ultimately regret my decision. 

As an artist the last thing I want to have are regrets when it comes to my output. So with my genesis drop I’m letting it fly, because in the end it won't matter the excuse, only that I again denied myself the opportunity to be vulnerable in my art.

Since the age of 5 years old my dad had me using a Roland MS 1 sampler i’ll never forget that day sitting on the edge of the couch using it and me pressing the pads to hear my voice say “yeah baby”.

From that day, I knew what I wanted to be in life… which was to be like my father. From seeing him drawing every day,  doing animation, photography, and making music he is the greatest artist I know. The beauty of it is he’s all self-taught.

This release, it’s a tribute to my Parents. From the hand-drawn cover, to the music, to the sounds that are in the music. Without my parent's support and encouragement, I wouldn’t be here today. In the beat there's half of a speech from my friend saying to follow your dreams and goals and that's something my parents always told me and supported, at the end, she says I miss you chow chow, and as I moved to another state that's how I always feel, I will always miss them but I know that they are right here with me always cheering me on to keep going.

This body of work is my whole life, as I drew myself on the cover floating holding a sampler/drum machine from my dad and the records from my mom floating around me … this is 3 summers.

records.note:
We’ve all heard stories about the lost city in the depths of the ocean. There’s always been something that’s drawn me into the idea of mystical creatures living under the sea. This song is off of my debut album, a special piece of my heart and soul. A monumental moment of time in my artist career and I’m so excited to share it right here on Sound exclusively. 

Encapsulating my story of coming to America from South Africa, living in LA in the middle of a global pandemic. Atlantis is about finding a safe haven amidst chaos and the bliss of finding a space to retreat. It took me almost 3 years to finally find that feeling again after moving to a new country and going through so much to make it in LA. I made this song with my favourite artist/producer Os Young, lyrically it really flowed so effortlessly that we immediately knew we had something special and meaningful. 

Visually continuing from Black Ice, building the storyline of KAIEN which is a character based on my life experiences. I teamed up with my good friend and graphic artist Alex Rodrigues to create an underwater backdrop with a modern twist on the lost city of Atlantis. 

This is the second drop of many that I’m planning for my debut album and I can’t wait to continue this journey with you all. 

With love always - Kai

records.title: From Beyond
records.creator: 0x2b4706043bA86AEEa7395942404a82CC6ee3E861
records.note:
„From Beyond“ comes with a story that I’d like to share. It all started with a reel of quarter-inch tape that I discovered in a box in the attic. After some investigation it turned out to be a recording of my maternal grandfather playing the piano. He passed away before I was born so while we never met, this artifact connected us through time. 

It struck me as a strange experience that somebody who was long gone could reach out through the ether, both emotionally and physically. After all, what is a recording but a vibration frozen in time? These particular vibrations had their points of origin when my grandfather played the piano almost 60 years ago, so in a very real sense we made a metaphysical connection through a reel of tape.

This realization haunted me ever since, only waiting for the right moment to materialize as creative spark for a new project. And with my sound.xyz debut scheduled for Halloween, I knew that this was the perfect opportunity to use the recordings of my grandfather playing the piano to communicate with him across the ocean of time. 

I’ve spent most of my adult life in the studio manipulating sounds and frequencies, but it was „From Beyond“ that taught me how my recordings will be my physical presence long after I'm gone.

records.title: Pa' esto nací

records.note:
Before Web3 I was 100% dedicated to songwriting, I always liked rapping, it was the first genre I fell in love with! but I put it aside with the excuse that it was a hobby for me, that I liked being behind the scenes. A year ago I decided that in addition to being a composer, I also wanted to release my music, I felt the call to express what I have inside, and this feeling coincided with the moment I met Web3, it was as if the universe was telling me: Hey you have talent and energy, now I'm going to give you the tools. It's funny, because people saw me and thought I was joking until they heard me rapping... Now, I have more conviction than anyone, and I even created my own crowdfund to be able to finance my first album as a rapper, to become the first latin artist to be born with Web3.

This is my first Hip Hop  song in the space, I had to save it for Sound XYZ. I'm serious when I say I want to make a historic album for rap in Spanish. This song is just the appetizer of all the fire that I'm going to give you, and I wrote it in a small room in my house, inspired by the Californian vibe and my life experiences. 

It talks about how this dream doesn't let me sleep, I feel it all day in my chest telling me to keep pushing, because it's not only going to change my life, but also my family, my colleagues and all the people I love. It talks about how I chose art above all else, because this is what I was born for and I just discovered. Rap is in my veins, despite the fact that I wasn´t born in a city totally influenced by hip hop or trap... it was something innate, that was given to me in an inexplicable way.

The music was made by Yogev, a friend with whom I made a lot of music in the past and with whom I met again on Web3... I already had the idea of ​​the lyrics and the melody, I even knew how I wanted to structure the beat, but I needed a person who understood me and could maximize my ideas. I immediately thought of Yogev, because he was one of the people who told me that I should release my rap when I was just a songwriter, And I knew how talented he was musically.

I want to dedicate this song to all my friends from Web3 who have supported me since day one, and who saw potential in me and my vision. Thank you for collecting,  motivating me and advising me, you are part of this. I promise you the best is about to come.

records.title: Clouded
records.creator: 0xC3aF8EfE3c865b8363A79B13B27dB530Eb5D24Af
records.note:
One of my favorite things about music is its ability to take your mind away from everyday life to somewhere new. I love this feeling of being transported. It’s easy to lose track of everything else when you are lost in a song. That is my goal with every piece of music… I want your mind to drift off from the day to day when you listen.

I wrote Clouded back in early July and immediately knew I wanted to save it for a special moment in this web3 music journey. It was one of those sessions without a specific goal in mind, just playing around with different sounds and letting the idea lead. Continuing that line of thought, the name came from thinking about how clouded our view of the future actually is. Of course we should make plans and chase after our goals, but we don’t know what’s going to happen next. And often that is a beautiful thing. Many of the best moments aren’t things we plan for or even see coming. Our job is just to do our best and see where the journey goes.

Case in point for me is this drop. I didn’t see web3 music coming at all, and it has opened up a whole new world for me this year. Just showing up, creating music, collecting music, and engaging with our community here has made me more hopeful than ever for the future as an independent musician. Dropping on Sound has been a huge goal from the beginning, and I’m so happy with where the journey is at right now. I hope this song transports you somewhere, and thank you so much for your support.

records.note:
Emily Lazar is a multi-disciplinary artist fronting the rock/metal transmedia project, September Mourning. She made history as the first female metal/ hard rock musician to mint and sell an NFT on the blockchain. She has spoken about her accomplishments in Web 3/ NFT's at Harvard (2x), NFT.NYC and ETH Denver Conferences.

September Mourning is a transmedia project based on a comic book series she wrote and published through Image/Top Cow Comics with her business partner Marc Silvestri (Batman/Witchblade/Darkness). September Mourning is the title character. As a human reaper hybrid, she  gives expired souls a second chance at life in another body. In doing so, she messes with  the plans of the antagonist, Fate, who is trying to rid  earth of all the good souls and leave the bad so the world will self-destruct and It can start anew. An epic war between the living and the dead ensues. Emily plays the title character on stage.

Emily designed the world she and her band (Rich Juzwick, Kyle Mayer and Aaron Hoover) bring to life on stage, including costumes, choreography, sets, etc. The band has toured with & opened festivals for Rob Zombie, Marilyn Manson, Slipknot, Mudvayne and others across Europe and the United States.

Black Dave is an artist creating at the intersection of anime, streetwear, rap music and sneaker culture. Entering web3 in late 2020, he’s established himself as a thought leader and innovator within it. Having a background in punk and hardcore, as well as rap and production, collaborating with a metal band only made sense.

"Wake The Dead Featuring Black Dave" takes the September Mourning sound to a whole new level by infusing heavy metal with hip hop and trap music. The anthemic song lyrics by Emily reinforce the theme of the September Mourning storyline which is to own one's own voice and make one's own decisions with purpose and intent in order to squeeze every last incredible drop of life from one's soul while on this planet. Black Dave's lyrics reinforce that as well with a call to arms and intense fighting spirit. 

The artwork features Fate, the antagonist from the books and the subject that the song is rallying against.

I wrote 'In the Leaves' about a dream I had before I decided to quit my stable, full-time design job.

In the dream I kept waking up outside — on the sidewalk in San Francisco, and later in the leaves by a road. I kept choosing that over my bed, and it felt surprisingly calm to wake up outside of my home.

I had a session with Benji Cormack and we talked about this dream and how it seemed to mirror my life choice of staying in the comfort of a full-time job or leaving to focus on music and being satisfied with less.

I quit the job and now I've put out the song.

"I'm waking in the leaves again
Under street signs, never needed more.
Mapping out the turns I take
When I sleepwalk, why's it feel like home?"

"For The Family" is a song I created during our 50th Episode of FSR as an ode to my loved ones and the community we've built.
