records.title: why can't you hate me?
records.creator: 0x2927fa18C66f8eCf5490D48d8Cf37b7B23545FAd
records.note:
I wrote this song during a period of my life when I truly felt like a bit of a fuck up. Despite this, the people closest to me continued to believe in my vision, my music, and just ME... even when I didn’t believe in myself. I’d feel like a “sinking ship” at times yet, everyone came aboard, swords drawn high, ready to go to battle for something greater than ourselves. As I continued to write the song, it more or less turned into a prayer to God. I hope you all love the track, it means a lot to me. 

Now that you know about the song, here's how I got here. I grew up in Indiana but currently live in Nashville. When I was 15 I started playing guitar and writing music but didn't take it seriously until my Sophomore year of college.

In the summer of 2018, leading up to my Sophomore year, my engagement with my fiancée fell through, and I lost all interest in school. I was struggling to heal from the breakup, and I had no idea what I wanted to do with my life. It was during this time that I wrote my first song in over a year called I Tried. To this day, I can't describe how I felt after making that song. I had finally found my way to heal, and, from then on, creating music was all I wanted to do.
 
Around this time, a producer that I had connected with in 2017, named Dylan Stiles, was sending me beats every day. I would write and record to these beats every night using an Xbox headset and GarageBand. As time went on, we both decided that the best thing we could do was to drop out of school and go all-in on music. In July of 2019, with less than 4,000 monthly listeners on Spotify, Dylan and I moved to Nashville to do just that.
 
After a failed EP, we realized I needed a better strategy for putting out music. We decided that the best thing I could do was put out a new song every two weeks until one caught traction. On September 6th, 2019, we released the first song following this plan called I Lost Myself.

Currently, I am a fully independent singer/songwriter based out of Nashville. My team and I have been building my fan base over the past couple years and have amassed 200,000,000 streams, over a million monthly listeners on Spotify, 200k+ subs on YouTube, and more, all independently. While our music hasn’t stopped growing by any means, moving into the NFT space for additional support and a new way to connect with listeners was the logical next step for us.

records.title: Breaking The Cycle
records.creator: 0xbeEb460081C1E3820A6AFAa309C6D3C45F465335
records.note:
Releasing this song feels like a necessary detour. I try my best to be as vulnerable as possible in my music but this was something I didn’t know how to say even though I knew it was necessary. I am many things. A man, a son, a brother, a friend, a musician. But above all else I am a father. That is my ultimate purpose. To lead by example for my sons. To teach them how to maneuver in a world not inherently designed for them to win. To break the cycle.

My journey throughout Web 3 thus far has been a time of affirmation (shoutout to Scolla.) It’s been a time of growth, learning, and healing. It’s been a time of not always doing the easiest (or most politically correct) thing, but having faith that it is the right thing as I continue forward.

I feel like I’m at the crossroad of stepping into my future and healing from my past, all while remaining present. I am working through my struggles in realtime - through music - and I hope that anyone who reads this understands that I am not defined by my circumstances, and neither are you. This has been a season that I feel is coming to a close. So although I am excited to share this piece of my story with you, I am equally as excited to have you with me as the rest of the story unfolds.

One thing that Web 3 has taught me is to better vocalize my needs. To not be afraid to say that I am not ok, or that I need help because we are not meant to walk alone.

I have been dealing with a traumatic situation involving my children and my family and I am thankful that I have the love and support to be able to say that I need help as I give this offering. I called this a necessary detour because that’s exactly how it feels. Like stopping for gas on a road trip. Knowing that this path is meant for me but that I had to take a second to address my needs and decompress before driving again.

So to anyone reading this, thank you for supporting me. Thank you for continuing to uplift me and remind me of my worth in the times when I may forget. Thank you for allowing me the opportunity to support my family by doing something I love. And thank you for helping me break the cycle. 

All love, always.

records.note:
Have you ever gotten to the next level and wondered if you belonged there? Life lately has been what I always imagined it was supposed to be, and yet I still have this lingering unease as I step into the success I’ve created for myself.

  Coming from a single-parent home and contending with the struggles that entailed, I made the commitment to myself that I would transcend my circumstances through my own effort and creativity. I’ve prepared myself to work harder, to do better, to become greater… but one thing I wasn’t prepared for was the feeling of not belonging in the life I had dreamed of.

  Imposter Syndrome speaks to the phenomenon of “arrival fallacy,” in which you’ve achieved what you set out to do… but things but still feel uneasy in the place that your success has brought you to.
Accompanied by fellow artist Rey Morado of ReignCloud Music Group, with production by Dav, Imposter Syndrome is the pure expression of the fear, doubt, and anxiety that comes from leaving behind the patterns of your old life and carving out something new for yourself.

records.note:
I’ve noticed that many of us experience the challenges required to have a healthy relationship. Many artists have made it a point to share their experiences of heartache through relationships. That leads me to believe we are all going through the same thing. It seems most heartache stems from a place of poor communication. The environment for it is neither created nor maintained. That always neglects the elephant in the “RòóM.” Before you know it, the elephant has more room than the two of you.

By making “RòóM,” I decided to face the music...Looking both within and without, I noticed all my experiences put me in a position to be; more self-aware, accountable, and wanting to be my best self. 
Naturally, love, in all use of the word, benefits from this.

The melancholy piano, the muffled drums drowning In space, and the melody all come together to emote what I felt…What I know you may be feeling.
If you do feel this, then it’s for you.

records.title: Overthinking
records.creator: 0x414CA9c0e2FcCc222ca1c5f4cC77Ca685dd03F7d
records.note:
‘Overthinking’ is an eerie, vulnerable, and almost desperate ballad. It captures the exact feelings of being an overthinker. Being swamped with your own bad thoughts that are oftentimes untrue. Needing reassurance from the person you’re thinking about.

This song was so therapeutic and relieving for me to make. The timing of this song was perfect. At that particular moment, I was so overwhelmed with emotions I couldn't make sense of. I couldn't tell if what was going on in my mind was true, or if I was just creating a false narrative in my head. There was no one around me who knew what I’d specifically felt. There was no song for me to play that related to my exact state.

So I made my own.

I started with some simple chords on the keyboard. Just two of them. What caught my ear was the bass within the sound of the piano, and I left it at that. I didn’t know what to start off with lyrically. So I just started recording and sang whatever I felt.

“Why don’t you talk to me”. A simple phrase, yet so intriguing. It makes you think: where was I going with this? I kept up the improvisation and went back afterwards, changing some lyrics and melodies. I didn’t write down one lyric on my phone during this. It was just straight from my emotions. I never want to hold back in my music. I want to say what I feel.

Like many of my songs, they’re personal to me. They all have a story. But like many of us, we all feel heartbreak, desire, longing. And we want to be understood. We want to know that we’re not alone. Words cannot describe how healing this song was for me to make.

‘Overthinking’ is the perfect song for those whose mind wanders. For those whose minds are too loud. For those who need reassurance. For those who want to be understood. ‘Overthinking’ is perfect for overthinkers. I hope you’re able to feel some comfort, and feel some emotion :)

- Mia Lailani <3

records.title: down in florida (demo)

records.note:
Hey, I’m Munn. I grew up in Indiana but currently live in Nashville. When I was 15 I started playing guitar and writing music but didn't take it seriously until my Sophomore year of college.

In the summer of 2018, leading up to my Sophomore year, my engagement with my fiancée fell through, and I lost all interest in school. I was struggling to heal from the breakup, and I had no idea what I wanted to do with my life. It was during this time that I wrote my first song in over a year called I Tried. To this day, I can't describe how I felt after making that song. I had finally found my way to heal, and, from then on, creating music was all I wanted to do.
 
Around this time, a producer that I had connected with in 2017, named Dylan Stiles, was sending me beats every day. I would write and record to these beats every night using an Xbox headset and GarageBand. As time went on, we both decided that the best thing we could do was to drop out of school and go all-in on music. In July of 2019, with less than 4,000 monthly listeners on Spotify, Dylan and I moved to Nashville to do just that.
 
After a failed EP, we realized I needed a better strategy for putting out music. We decided that the best thing I could do was put out a new song every two weeks until one caught traction. On September 6th, 2019, we released the first song following this plan called I Lost Myself.

Currently, I am a fully independent singer/songwriter based out of Nashville. My team and I have been building my fan base over the past couple years and have amassed 200,000,000 streams, over a million monthly listeners on Spotify, 200k+ subs on YouTube, and more, all independently. While our music hasn’t stopped growing by any means, moving into the NFT space for additional support and a new way to connect with listeners was the logical next step for us.

Earlier this year, I was in a long-distance relationship with a girl from Florida. Shortly after her and I broke up, I was back down in Florida with Friends and spent a little too much time and money trying to forget I was hurting. I went to bars and casinos and let loose. Weirdly enough, I had started a demo called "down in florida", months prior, that nearly described the exact situation I now found myself in with her. I didn't have the words to finish the song until I was back in Nashville a week later and decided to continue writing the song from my current situation. Hence, the opening of the second verse "i'm back in Nashville..."

records.note:
When I went full time music in 2016 it wasn’t an easy feat.

Using my skillset to make money was like shooting in the dark abyss. Outside of my performances and few feature verses, I was a freelance videographer and I produced for a few artists. But those who know about freelance work…it’s tough building a consistent pool of clients. Especially ones that are willing to pay.

In the meantime, I would do Lyft, Uber, Postmates -- whatever I could do to make ends meet. I spent late nights driving people to their destinations to make sure we had enough money for our phone bill. I spent rainy cold evenings delivering Postmates meals to get those last few dollars for groceries. And all while maintaining my music career. 

As you can imagine…it was stressful. 

During this time of my life, I wasn’t the warm-hearted pat junior many people know now. I was deeply hurt, ignorantly traumatized and a somewhat cold-hearted pat junior. I was the “no new friends” pat junior. Only open with those who had been with me from day one.

Although I’m a huge fan of Marvel, there are a few DC characters I like. One of them is Batman. And during this time, I thought myself very akin to Batman. Mysterious, extremely cautious, unable to be read, high moral code, protective, still seen as a leader to many but not willing to trust other people or let them in.

Amid creating new music, I remember hearing this beat made by my mentor and producer DSTL (Daniel Steele) and immediately gravitating to it. I remember using every bit of determination and frustration in me to write this record. If it’s one thing life has done to me? It’s made me develop me thick skin and a sharp mind. I was made to muscle through many extreme storms in life due to what I had been through and being a man of big faith. 

That’s the theme of this record. I poured all that mindset into every line when writing this – along with making a lot of cool Batman references and analogies.

I remember performing this record for the first time and it shaking the stage and blowing away the audience.

It’s like I took all the energy off the stage with me when I got done performing it.

records.creator: 0xbCefc4906b443e4DB64E2b00b9af2C39e76c785c
records.note:
When I was in college I got ahold of The Chainsmokers’ managers’ e-mail address. They had just dropped a record called “Everybody Hates Me” and as a new producer on the scene I wanted to take a pass at remixing it. I figured the best case scenario would be The Chainsmokers noticing me and taking me on a world tour with them and the worst case would be no response. To my surprise, the stems were sitting in my inbox within the hour. For the first time in my life, I had a fully processed, industry-standard engineered vocal that I could do anything with. The possibilities were endless. 

I skipped class for a week and went back and forth on seven or eight different versions of the remix - and while I didn’t get the Chainsmokers to sign off on it, I did fall in love with a new process of making music. For the next few years I would wake up every morning, go to New Music Friday on Spotify, track down management e-mails on the artists’ Facebook “about” section and beg for stems. Over the years, I put out a bunch of remixes for various artists - but more importantly I slowly compiled high quality vocals that I could mess with in my spare time. To this day, that remains one of my preferred method of working on records with people; “Ball!” with Kevin George (which was my last sound drop) happened from him sending me an acapella and my imagination running with it.

At the time, I was paid for remixes with exposure - and I wouldn’t have had it any other way. People started listening to my music on Soundcloud for the first time and I started to meet my first music friends through that experience. A lot of them are still my friends today.

However, there are a slew of examples of remixes that came out that went on to perform better than the original song did. More times than not, the remixer is paid in either exposure (like me), or a one time buyout fee which is typically $250 or less for smaller artists. Most of the time, the remixers - who breathe new life into the record - see no upside in the event that the remix is a smash. These artists are also overlooked often and don’t get a chance to tell their musical stories.

The Glass House remixes is a 4 pack of my favorite reworks off my EP “Glass House”. Every remix came out incredible, and flipped my songs into a way I never saw coming.

The pack features artists who vary in Web3 experience - from vets like Clear Eyes and MSFT to newcomers like Veggi and Cudos, I’m stoked to present the first Daniel Allan Remix pack on

records.title: By the Light of the Moon
records.collection: By the Light of the Moon
records.creator: 0x0c4956cAA320ced206049ff8dB698644a2d22769
records.note:
I started writing songs at a very young age, and have written hundreds of them.
Many were not great, but many others I put a lot of effort and time in and have loved them ever since.

“By the Light of The Moon” is one that I have felt so deeply ever since it was written, and have never had the chance to put out. Why, you ask?
Well... because unfortunately in the “web2” way of making music, there is always someone telling you that that songs you write will not work, because of this or that reason. That they’re not pop enough, or they’re too personal, or whatever it is.

And yet you keep writing them, because deep down those songs are the ones that make you happy and they’re literally the only way you have to truly express how you feel.
You know that at some point the day will come where you will have the opportunity to share them with the world, and someone will resonate with them. You have faith.

So that is why I kept writing songs like this one, and even if no one would have ever heard it, it would have been for me.
But since starting my web3 journey, I realized that things work differently here. You need to be authentic and honest. The more you are you, the better.
And this brings me more joy than anything else.

I decided that my Sound genesis should be one of those songs that have been sitting in my hard drive collecting dust for years. It was written 5 years ago, but it’s never left my mind or my heart. And now more than ever, I resonate with the message, so I did a brand new recording of it.

“By the Light of the Moon” is a chant of hope. Things have been hard for many of us, many times. But sometimes all it takes is one glance at the moon, and everything seems a little better.

January 2022, i ended a 2 & 1/2 year relationship with a woman i adore and love.

The idea was to create a playlist album consisting of singles that are released bi-weekly, with music videos, over the course of one full year. Then, at the end of the year period consolidate them in one place for fans to enjoy. I named the project GLORY ROAD. 

"Glory Road" meant the road i needed to take to get towards artistic freedom. On this road i would have to complete 24 singles, shoot and perform in 24 music videos, consistently promote these bi-weekly releases all over the internet, and let my fans in on a side of me i have yet to share. To me, It's the road to becoming the ultimate artist. It's artist development. I learn more and more about who i am as an artist daily. I have to show up every single day, no matter what. This process is the dream.

In February 2022, i signed a 3-chapter 24 song "Glory Road" deal with Guin Records giving me the ability to execute the playlist album. In March we dropped the first song but by September 2022 we decided to discontinue our partnership for the final chapter.

An ode to my 2 1/2 year relationship.

records.title: Joyful Resistance Part I (Kabuki remix)
records.creator: 0x3360A4e0Eb33161dA911B85f7C343E02ea41BbbD
records.note:
22 years ago, I was on tour in Japan and in one of my favorite record stores in Tokyo crate digging. I struck up conversation with another crate digger who turned out to be Kabuki - and that started a whole new world of possibility. Pretty much on the spot, Kabuki asked me if I'd be interested in collaborating on a project and less than a year later I was in Germany in studio with him and his Megashira production partner Mainframe writing and recording their next album ('At Last'). Two whole decades later, we've reconnected with each other thanks to our shared passion for web3 - the power of blockchain!

This remix came into existence thanks to our first Mashibeats community remix contest, with finalists being chosen by our discord community and winners decided by $BUYBACK holders. Kabuki's remix was one of my personal favorites but didn't end up being in the final 4. Those 4 were minted as 1/1s on Catalog and now, today, we're celebrating the release of the remixes on vinyl (!) and very limited digital (no DSPs) with bonus tracks including this remix. To celebrate the vinyl release, Kabuki and I decided to share his amazing remix with the world via this Sound drop. 

The original of this track (a future drop?!) was my creative reaction to the summer of 2020 when we were in full lockdown, BLM was top of mind for the whole planet, which raised the perspective of [joy] as an act of [resistance] and how that sounds in my imagination. I'll leave it to Kabuki to tell us more about his remix:

"... when I heard "Joyful Resistance Part I" for the first time I fell in love with the chord progression: shades of modal Herbie and "Extensions"-era McCoy Tyner conjured a magical mood. I had to figure out how Mark did this! Once I worked out the harmonies I wrote an "answer" to Mark’s phrase, starting a musical conversation between the original and remix versions. 808 drums programmed in a jazz waltz pattern and my trademark ARP2600 synth bass provide the necessary contrast. Music that transcends all styles and traditions..." - Kabuki

zone out to the vibes with us... Joyful Resistance Part I remixed by Kabuki!

records.title: Free to Love
records.creator: 0xbe5DB9E33A2309898D44d9f7A6EE9229EB4d5415
records.note:
Like many of us, my life was turned upside down during covid. I’d been building my career around live shows for 5 years in NYC and was finally getting to a place where agents were reaching out about gigs I'd dreamed of. I remember getting an email in Feb of 2020 to play Music Hall of Williamsburg in April. Of course, that never happened.

Locked in my apartment and falling in love with someone on FaceTime, I began to write prolifically. I was making almost a song per day. Some of those songs ended up on my forthcoming album. Some of them I’ve been holding onto, waiting for the exact right moment to share. 

“Free to Love” was made in a time of intense love, isolation, fear, and euphoria. I pushed myself to fully produce it, play the instruments, and finish it in a day.

Fast forward to last week, I had coffee with an incredible musician and producer named Cam. He’s in a band called King Youngblood and if you don’t know them now, you will next year. His mom Lara is an epic community builder and music industry queen. We were all brainstorming how to get more musicians into web3, since the tech stuff can be such a barrier to entry.

I realized in that conversation, the way to onboard people is through collaboration. We bring people in through their talent, not their Twitter prowess.

So, I sent him the stems and he stayed up until 3AM mixing, mastering, and adding some magic to the song. We’ve never worked together and only met twice before. No revisions needed. He nailed it.

This song goes out to all the creators, doers, community builders, and folks who are working to build a better world for musicians and music lovers.

records.title: blue skin
records.creator: 0x4E29d8fbcb1B92C37077AdC4f18571C5D786D3bD
records.note:
this piece holds a very special place in my heart. arguably the most personal + emotional music i've ever made. some who have listened to this have told me it feels like they are evoking core memories and watching their own lives.

i've never shared this with anyone other than the person this piece is about, but the title comes from a poem from Shel Silverstein. this is how it goes:

“She had blue skin,
And so did he.
He kept it hid
And so did she.
They searched for blue
Their whole life through,
Then passed right by-
And never knew.”

the way i see it is that two souls may cross paths for a second or even have the fortune of experiencing many moments together without really knowing how similar and kindred they really are. sometimes you really can't tell unless you give people a chance and enough time to open up. sometimes it takes a lot to realize what you're walking by or letting go of.

this track is my personal soundtrack to one blue skin encounter i had. i hope it brings you memories of your own. perhaps you've also had many "almost encounters" or short ones that could've been much more.

much love.

records.title: Heaven Or Hell
records.creator: 0x5FFDD9D9b1649dcD59A94840ed936bbD40c2880F
records.note:
Hey web3, I’m Harry and this is my first drop on sound.xyz. I’ve been making music for the past 10 years and over that time I’ve released music in EDM, Hip Hop, Alternative, Indie and Pop genres. With HARRY WAS HERE, my most recent project, I’ve aimed to be as experimental and honest as possible, combining all of my past styles into one genre-less sound. I write, produce, record, mix and master all of my own stuff and love the process of curating everything down to the last detail. When music NFTs started to become a thing, I immediately saw the potential shifts they could have on the music industry, one that leaves most of us artists barely able to sustain a full-time career. I’m incredibly excited to continue using the platform to explore new avenues to get my art out there and connect with people I otherwise wouldn’t be able to reach.

“Heaven Or Hell” is probably the most unconventional track I’ve ever made. The lyrics were adapted from a poem “Last Words” by my grandfather William S. Kilborne and touch on the struggles between good and evil within one’s own conscience. I made this song with the rest of the EP in December 2021 during two straight weeks of rain in Los Angeles, which very much influenced the melancholy atmosphere. The song further questions if we’re being judged by a higher power and whether or not our triumphs and regrets mean anything in a universe so vast and unresponsive. I’m so grateful for the feedback I’ve received on this project and inspired to keep creating things that push the boundaries of my music and the industry we all exist in.

records.creator: 0xE80c7Fee3D41E311e0351244231919E04E699E56
records.note:
I wrote The Song of The Sun & The Moon during the making of my new album "33". I was alone in the woods in Ithaca, NY across from the Dali Lama's Namgyal Monastery watching the sun set with a small acoustic guitar. My nephew had just been born and I was reflecting on my own journey so far. I had just been dropped from a major record label, and had been largely unsuccessful in terms of making a living as an artist, but I felt a peace about it all in that moment. I was proud of myself.

I thought about the lullabies my parents would sing me as a child. My mom would sing Joni Mitchel or John Denver, and my dad would make up his own little songs. Their songs are so ingrained in me, even as I write this. In some way, I wrote The Song of The Sun & The Moon as a lullaby to myself, from myself. It reminds me that every night I die, and every morning I am reborn. 

That is the song! And it goes on. I don't know if it will ever be finished.

records.note: "Montreal" was a record I wrote at one of the lowest points in my life mentally and emotionally. I used this record to recap how ego, selfishness, narcissism, and lack of self awareness tarnished one of the most important relationships in my life. The record is completely transparent and touches on how I wished this relationship had come my way, later in a more mature segment of my life. I wanted this record to be the second release from the album strategically as a juxtaposition to my first release "Count Bands", where I used things like money, ego, and material things to mask insecurities and pain I was feeling. This is just another steep drop in this emotional rollercoaster of an album and opens up a different segment of my life to the world.

records.title: FIGHT FOR THIS
records.creator: 0x4d18f8f2aE19f1E166c97793cceeb70680A2b6D2
records.note:
In the same vein as "u&i", this song is about the struggles of a relationship between two people wanting to fight for each other, but not being be able to fight for the right reasons at the right time. I've experienced this many times before, both sides, being the fighter and the person that someone is fighting for. 

Each side has things that are hard to handle and even harder to do, but this song is from the perspective of a fighter who wants to be fought for, while simultaneously understanding that sometimes a fight isn't necessary.

In writing this song, this description and just in general, I've realised that the word "fight" is one often associated with negativity, with pain, survival and violence, be it towards others, or yourself. But I choose to see it in the light I want it to be in, which is trying your best to make sure the reality you want, with someone you love, can come to life with enough effort, time, patience and fight.

records.title: Grateful
records.creator: 0xE7907a934bf32607D8eB7698FF9ad5701f174c6a
records.note:
"Grateful" is about how to ease the blush of unfamiliarity when entering a new relationship. I wrote it when I made friends with the feeling of having just enough fuel to jump AND just enough fear to shut my eyes when I do it. This song is quite a bit more specific than my previous releases. As “Stuck” talked about trusting the feeling over the circumstance, and “Paint in the Dark” described the over-arching agreements that I have observed in the healthiest love, “Grateful” exemplifies these themes using the intimacy of a pillow talk conversation. It is about putting what I’ve learned into action and trusting what happens next. 

As someone who has spent most of their music career playing shows and performing, “Grateful” has become one of the songs that I use to bring down the energy of a show. It’s the deep breath out, the song that takes the emotional weight off, the settling. Some songs pop out finished within 30 minutes and others take time, and “Grateful” went through many iterations over a few years before I finally landed where I did. I spent a lot of time observing people’s reactions to the lyrics and would continue to edit until I got the reaction that I wanted from my audience. Up until early-2020 the song was called “Quiet” and the chorus was not very strong. I remember finally landing on the melody of the chorus that you hear now when I was just noodling around on a guitar at a friend’s house. I’ll never forget the midnight, one-man, dance party I had in my bedroom because I finally discovered lyrics that mirrored the emotion of the melody of the chorus. Pure celebration, it was a glorious feeling. 

So, when you listen to this song, I want you to flip through you own wonderful, wine-stained memories just like I did. I hope it inspires you to take a conscious breath before you sit down for an intimate moment with that person, and recognize that this will only happen this way once, right now. Enjoy, and thanks for collecting, “Grateful” :)

"Grateful"
Written by Nicolas Cyril De Luca-Verley (Nico Franc)
Produced, Mixed, and Mastered by Dean Woodson and Nicolas Cyril De Luca-Verley (Nico Franc)

Cudos (Dan and Alex) hit me up earlier this summer to work on a song after hearing me on Daniel Allan's "Overstimulated". daddy's money was designed as an all expenses paid trip for you and your friends to fly to sonic paradise. made with only luxury materials from London, Paris, New York, and Amalfi, there's no better way to bring you and your special someone to that sweet, summer soaked place you could only dream of before.

this track holds such a dear place in my heart. i had been a fan of Night Tapes for a few years after hearing their record Forever, which is still one of my favorite tracks of all time. when i got to London they hit me up to work, and after a few buses and cabs i made it to their South London home studio. we shared stories and snacks in a nearby park, and then got started. 

we messed around for a while on some ideas, until they pulled up this synth line that i was immediately swept into, and we dove head first into the energy until 5 in the morning. they gave me the physical tape we recorded a lot of the parts on, and i remember leaving their place with the sun rising and the song looping on my phone. 

when i got back to LA i realized it stood to represent all the things daddy's money was made to, and hit them up to see if they were down to be on the album. really humbled and excited to have them on it and bring them into the space!

records.title: I Wrote this Today
records.creator: 0x130737b2D5d7F73ACFE922204059a4B46Cb1Fa34
records.note:
I am experimenting with not overthinking.
I want to go back to putting out music without thinking about why,
Or to who, and to how many. 
I don’t ever want to stand in my own way.

I am beyond grateful to have jumped into the music nft space in 2021 alongside friends (HI, Songcamp!) to learn, experiment, and experience the beginning stages of what this is and all it can be. I am, to be honest with everyone reading this, still shaking off some web2 trauma. I’m a fully independent singer/songwriter living in a city of artists and I’ve been here for 7 years… so I’m still learning how to act without having to plan so much... the content strategies, make the Tik Toks, delivering 4-6 weeks ahead, getting the spotify meetings, just to wake and hope they remembered you enough the next day. Enough… What a thought! I'm passionate about onboarding artists to web3 so we can all learn more about what that word can mean for us, and about our value as creatives.

(more backstory): 
On January 3rd 2022, an Instagram post from an artist named Chelsea Cutler went viral that caught my attention.. mainly because it spoke so accurately into what I was feeling, but also because of how fast I realized how many people felt the same way. 

The sentence that grabbed me most was “It feels like there is such a massive disconnect between listeners and artists that I haven't experienced before.”
It made me sad. Artists, who’s positions I imagined enjoying being in, sharing vulnerable and honest truth about how they don’t know how to navigate this industry in the form that it’s in today. I guess I sometimes feel like idols of mine have some magic wand, magic helper or something because they feel so far from where I am.. but then I started to grow up and get older in the industry, trying to understand it as best I could with my given experiences, and it kinda is one giant peek behind a curtain.. 

But then you have the choice!
The choices of where to spend your time, 
How you share your gift, who you want to collaborate with…
And. (I agree with Jimmy Iovine on this one), 
You go where your effort is. 


I knew I needed to get out these words yesterday (10/7) and I hope anyone who needs to hear it, will find it. 
Please be encouraged!!!! make your music!!! 
We will only fail when we stop.
KR

A little about us, we both been making music since we were 14. Brett started as a DJ making mashups and mixes and Andy making beats that were about as trash as gas station sushi. We have a lot of respect for the world of Web3. records.title: WE LOVE PT. 1
records.creator: 0x40aE91D5cdF5567d0B7d55E5f4dae2ce2bC1aA59
records.note:
Growing up in Boston, I had a tough time articulating how I truly felt. I guess I was scared people would make fun of me, or that no one else was feeling how I was. I thought, maybe something was wrong with me and everyone else was okay. I would often put a shield up and was always cautious of letting others get too close.

At the time, the only way I knew how to express myself was through music. For some reason, when it came to music, I was able to let go and be completely honest with my lyrics. So, when I started releasing songs in high school, my whole world changed. I realized that no matter what you are feeling, there will always be somebody out there who resonates.

Over the years, I’ve tried to lean into deeper and more honest creations and I’m proud to say that this collection of music is my truest yet.

WE LOVE PT. 1 is the intro to the album. A song about self-discovery and being true to yourself and your needs. The importance of unlearning so you may be free to learn again, and the importance of looking inward. You aren’t capable of loving anybody else until you learn to love yourself first.

on september 5th, late at night, i got a text.  it was from deegan.  an audio file.  no instruments, no production of any kind.  just his voice.  

by the time i had reached the end of the recording, i was tearing up.  i'd never heard him so vulnerable and raw.  i immediately dragged the file into ableton 9 and started producing around it.  i worked until 5 am.  it was the most cathartic musical experience i had had in months.  i hope this song can do for you what it has done for me.  <3

records.title: Loop Jam 0 (#PhaseDance)
records.creator: 0xcF669804AC78CFc589bEaE782f045f961fC10381
records.note:
So, while I make a lot (A LOT) of beats, original compositions, remixes, reworks, and the like, my favorite creations are the ones where I flex my musicality in a more traditional format. These "Loop Jams" and "Jam Sessions" I have originally were ultra-personal for me, virtually for my ears only. Of the 10-12 I may have liberated so far, there exist over 100 variations, both unfinished or roughly arranged into otherwise finished tracks, with me usually setting the musical landscape for me to play my own solos, arrange crazy bridges and vamps, and assemble layers upon layers upon layers of interconnected sounds and phrases, just because I can.

Firstly, what's special about the cover is that it is my genesis DALL-E creation, in which I describe for it, "A translucent, glowing man playing a grand piano, floating through space with an Old Fashioned cocktail and a joint floating behind him, and the Milky Way in the background". I think DALL-E nailed it, don't you?

This track is special, however, because I sample a similar arrangement from one of my late father and I's favorite musicians, Pat Metheny, for what is easily one of my favorite arrangements of all time, "Phase Dance". I hope with every track like this that I do, I am honoring both him and our favorite artist, and that the energy you feel when you listen to this inspires the same kind of feeling I get when I listen to his records: hope, for the future, for all of eternity...

records.title: u&i
records.creator: 0x4d18f8f2aE19f1E166c97793cceeb70680A2b6D2
records.note:
Love is, and always will be, something that brings out the best and worst in all of us. 

I always thought I knew how to go about loving something, whether it was a person, a thing, an experience or myself. Time and time again, I am shown that that love is not what I was taught or know it to be. 

I am always thankful for any moment that shows me just how little I know, especially when it comes to the things I have always believed to be true. In my brief time away, I have had many of those moments, and that's where this song comes from. A special person, a tough situation, the feelings of love, pain, loss and gain all combined into a beautiful and heavy moment.

This is about knowing that what you want is to love, but never being able to get it right.

records.title: someone I don't know
records.creator: 0x19250B770Efd981c855195d0CE674F811f350f42
records.note:
When I was 21 years old I packed two suitcases and moved alone from Montreal, Canada, to New York City. I wasnʼt sure where I would live, how I would earn money, or what my life would look like, I just knew that I needed to leave and that I wanted to sing.

Leaving my friends and family and the life I had at home was one of the most difficult things Iʼve ever done. Honestly, it broke my heart. But I knew I needed the change and the space to chase my dreams.

Iʼve spent a lot of time over the years beating myself up over choosing the life Iʼve chosen instead of staying physically close to people I love. Iʼve lost friends and relationships. Itʼs always been extremely difficult for me to reconcile making the decision to be so far from the people I care most about.

‘Someone I donʼt knowʼ is an apology letter to people Iʼve hurt (even unintentionally) along the way. Itʼs also a letter to myself, in a way, an attempt at forgiving myself for putting my dream of having a career in music first.

Maybe you can relate. Maybe youʼve had to live with a decision that hurt someone even though it was what was best for you. Maybe your heartʼs been in two places at once. Maybe you need to make amends with others- or with yourself. In any case, I hope you love this record. I hope it makes you feel something.

10% of all sales of this record will go directly to charity. This record will be supporting The NCRI Womenʼs Committee, an organization that ‘works to be the voice of Iranian womenʼ, fighting to achieve gender equality and equal rights for Iranian women. Thank you so much for supporting this incredibly important cause with me.

-Sara

records.title: Hurt You
records.creator: 0x54B356F6Eb2bc6Cec1DEfCad29Fc582419B1cB14
records.note:
Let’s see.. long story short. I started making music in high school as a joke and eventually I started realizing it was the only thing keeping me sane. Which I think a lot of people might be able to relate to. By my senior year I was dead-set on making music a career even though at the time  I really had no idea what that would actually entail. Mom was always supportive but insisted I do one year of college to “try it out”. I knew I had to get out of my small town on Cape Cod and I pretty much settled for whatever school in Boston would take me. So I packed up the studio and sent it. 

 	Couple weeks went by and I met a girl , we fell in love , blah blah blah. I dropped out of school, she moved out the country, we made it work. I broke her heart, she took me back, you know all that toxic stuff. And that kinda went on for years you know? I even wrote a whole bunch songs about it lol . But HURT YOU in particular, was a really important one. Imma tell you why. 

	So at first listen you might think “ahh this is just another sad break up song” but this one was different. This was the first song where I actually admitted that there was nothing I could do to fix the damage that I had caused. Only took about 5 years. That was that. It was hard but I finally let her go. 

	Then, about a month after it ended I was invited to LA for my first label meeting. Crazy how life works. Anyways, nothing really happened with the song but a year later I was living in LA,  still working my day job and I get DM from some kid I went to high school with. “Yo Promoting Sounds just posted your song.” I couldn’t believe it, I kept refreshing the link and the numbers just kept going up by the thousands. It was really like the first moment I had where I felt like “Damn, all these years of nothing to finally see some proof that it was possible”.  So not only do I hope this song continues to help people like myself, who rely on music to keep their heads level, but I also hope it inspires them to follow their intuition regardless of how scary the future might seem.

FOLLY OF THE BEAST follows on from recent drop VINEGAR HILL - track 2 in the 3 part collection on Sound. 

The title comes from a quote by novelist Herman Melville (Moby Dick) “For there is no folly of the beast of the earth which is not infinitely outdone by the madness of men” & it really struck a chord with me. The foolishness of “man” is as relevant as ever with the current climate crisis. The lyrics "what is it you want? what do you need? How do you live? Live, for free?"  are urgent questions that need answers. We come from the Earth and are products of it, yet have such a disconnect to it, and it's a troubling paradox.

The BADBOI club EP dropped recently on August 25 and it was fully funded by the collectors from my drop on Sound.xyz, "Push". Everything from the cover art, the press shots, the mixing, mastering to the PR for both Australia & USA, remixes and distribution costs were covered. It takes a village to raise a child & it sure took a village to help make this record...!

So why collect a BRUX nft? I posed this question as a poll to my fans recently & the leading answer was to support the project so more art could be made.

So, here we are.

records.title: ENTROPY ENTENDRE EP
records.creator: 0x24F9756A35Abed17B05Dfa49f9211ED968BB8898
records.note:
This body of work is in essence a reaction to the chaotic nature of the music industry itself and in stark contrast to my previously unhinged approach to production and composition. There was a certain unbridled creativity to the torrent of music that I managed to spew out in the soundcloud renaissance of the mid to late 2010s, but beneath the prolific output was an unwavering paranoia. My fervent output was fueled by a fear that should I got even a week without releasing something, the whole thing would fall apart. Music was seemingly the only thing I was good at it and should it falter to pay the bills I would have nowhere left to turn to. It was that apprehension that fueled my creative output which in retrospective, could have been tempered by a bit of patience and foresight. Multi-drop songs spanning multiple genres, keys, and tempos, was certainty interesting and admirable, but in many ways I failed to zero-in on exactly what it was I was trying to say in dance music, the story I wanted to tell was fractured and lacking a cohesive narrative. 

This EP is my attempt to reel in the array of disparate influences  and styles that have shaped my taste and mold them into something cohesive, while still being able to move a dance-floor in a tangible way. During the first half of this year I unintentionally mired my own personal life by becoming intimately involved with a number of partners who were in very obvious ways detrimental to my musical and spiritual development.   In many ways the uncertainty I was facing with regards to my musical career became reflected in my relationships. Only when I came to terms with the reality that I was self-sabotaging myself by immersing myself in chaotic tendencies was I able to take a step back and re-calibrate. In doing so I was able to listen to my own work with clarity, and hear the dissonance between what it was I wanted to make and what I felt pigeon-holed into making.

What people knew me as was a future bass artist, but the events I had been attending and the music that was resonating me was all techno. Yet there was that nagging voice - echoed in the strong advisement of former managers and agents - that making such a pivot would be career suicide. But my involvement in web3 space (a godsend) increasingly indicated my creative output no longer had to be directly tied to its speculative financial viability. records.title: driving into the sun
records.creator: 0xe6445bd1d9674fE7fbEdAD2F56F3B1eAEA1b029e
records.note:
daddy's money was designed as an all expenses paid trip for you and your friends to fly to sonic paradise. made with only luxury materials from London, Paris, New York, and Amalfi, there's no better way to bring you and your special someone to that sweet, summer soaked place you could only dream of before.

it was my last day in Italy and i had reserved a 125cc Vespa to take around town exploring Naples. when i got to the rental place though, i was informed they had messed up and rented the scooter to someone else. the only one they had left was 300cc, and was ready to be picked up a few miles away at the airport. i had met this girl while i was in croatia that ended up in italy with us, and since she had nothing to do that day she asked to tag along for whatever roads my two wheels ended up on. so we hopped in a Fiat and went to the airport to grab the freeway legal Vespa.

it was there that i found out that the Amalfi Coast was 40 minutes away, and since i had been dreaming of riding a moped down its winding roads since i was a kid, i took one look at my co-pilot and told her to hold on tight. 

we followed the Italian road signs as best we could and after making a few wrong turns we ended up in Amalfi, drinking Aperol Spritzes in the ocean. we went all the way to Sorento, after after another Aperol we made the impulse decision to get matching Vespa tattoos.

by the time we finished, it was about an hour til sundown, so we started making our way back to Naples for dinner with some friends. Naples is more or less West of Amalfi, which meant i was literally driving into the sun. i was nervous and crazy focused, and this song started looping in my head. i asked olivia to take my phone out and start a voice memo, and right there, on the highway of Naples, driving into the sun was born. i didn't change a single word from that initial recording, which i ended up sampling throughout the song.

this is the last song on daddy's money, but daddy's money has no ending. daddy's money is infinite, and daddy's money is for the people. long live daddy's money.

records.title: Stay With Me
records.creator: 0xF9a1cc799186e5A25a7AcB91FA9DCfC9c9B694fe
records.note:
A letter to my first love, music.

After years of bouncing around different EP deals with different labels to stay a float, I wrote Stay With Me. It was during a time where I felt creatively empty. To me, it’s a call out for a second chance. I couldn’t come up with anything. My beats were horrible & I doubted every single lyric I wrote. It was the scariest time of my life.

The business & politics of music had caught up to me. It got so overwhelming to the point where I felt like a failure and even had thoughts of giving up. How could I have gotten to the point where I resented making music? It’s the only thing that truly makes me feel whole.

I had forgotten about the kid who skipped the last two years of high school to learn two instruments, learn how to make beats, record himself & write songs from scratch. I had forgotten the sacrifices i made to build a relationship with music. I had forgotten the reasons why i even love music so much. The freedom it gave me. I almost let the business take that away from me. 

Stay With Me is the 1st song I wrote for Glory Road, and the beginning of Chapter 3. I am no longer with any labels. This time I choose freedom over all. If I don’t have my music, my creativity, then I have nothing. I wanted so badly to make songs that I loved again. I wanted so badly not to doubt my music & Stay With Me was the ice breaker.

records.note:
My entire life revolves around making music. Every day I wake up, brush my teeth, go on a run, and basically make songs until the sun goes down. If I had to estimate, I probably make close to 30 songs/mini ideas per month - and that’s being very conservative.

Out of the 300+ song ideas that I make per year, I realistically only get 12-15 at bats to show DSPs what I’m working on. Often times, that curation has to do with what artists are on what song, who else is releasing in the same week, and a bunch of other politics that don’t make a ton of sense. 

Releasing music shouldn’t be complicated.

Kevin George sent me this acapella last week as my flight from Miami back home to LA was taking off. I produced the entire thing from start to finish on the flight. I tweaked it that night, bounced it and played it at the Glass House release party the next day.

I’m putting this song out to challenge the notion that every song has to have the perfect roll out and campaign. If you love a record, put it out. It doesn’t matter if it took you 3 hours or 3 years 💛

records.title: HEAVEN (with Reo Cragun)
records.creator: 0x82cE5258Aa5925Bb5c9DA07fA7996e73687a440e
records.note:
Sometimes we have to face our darkest thoughts before we can really move beyond them. We did that together with HEAVEN - Reo and I made this song right after we finished his Diary of a Loner album…we were locked in and had been creating together regularly for nearly a full year and were both itching to try something different. I sent him an instrumental inspired by acoustic singer-songwriters and he replied with the start of this heartwrenching song that soon revealed itself as one of the most vulnerable either of us had ever made. 
 
Reo and I bonded over the traumatic health issues and subsequent surgeries we both went through during the pandemic that seriously limited us for too long. Heaven looks that feeling of hopelessness we both felt straight in the eyes and in the end finds a glimmer of hope in it. Hope that we both found with each other as we deepened our creative partnership during that time. We’ve never heard anything quite like it.

This is song 1 from CACOPHONY, a new project from Reo Cragun and myself. CACOPHONY is a beautiful explosion. Deafeningly loud and chaotic and intimate at the same time. And it begins now.

"Count Bands" is a complete ego trip moment in my album.  It is filled with very honest and emotional expressions. I made this record for a mental high, but also for a unique reminder that the ego is always the death of a man.  This is a recurring theme my album touches upon that will explored on a deeper level with each release. I felt that “Count Bands” was a great starting point to kick off the sonically emotional rollercoaster that is my debut album. So what better place to start then at the very top of that roller coaster.

The team and I flew out to Sun Valley, Idaho and locked our selves in a cabin to build out the framework of the album. By day 4 "Count Bands" happened to be a product of that trip. It's aggressive and infectious energy was something that has resonated with me since.

records.title: Bruises
records.creator: 0xDB83ea3B2A65300078532966Fd48322518632EE4
records.note:
hi. i’m Annika Rose. 

i’ve been an artist in the industry since I was 9 years old, and man have i seen some shit - the good, the bad, and the ugly. 

in 2016 i lost my first major record deal, my family broke down and drastically reassembled…. i cycled through more unfulfilling deals and ghostly promises until the world was shut down by the pandemic.  it became increasingly more obvious to me that the only promise i could make was to myself and to my art. and the only way to relinquish control over it was to fearlessly trust in it. 

“Bruises” is a song i wrote about a friend. a friend quite literally covered in self-inflicted bruises, but more importantly it’s become about how others’ metaphorical “bruises” can so quickly become your own; how pain is so contagious, especially around people who you love and care for the most. 

this song is my first audio nft; the daunting yet seemingly very special first step of a journey into greater ownership, creativity, and connection in my art. i’m excited for the world to hear it as a reminder that taking care of your mental health can be the hardest but end up being the most rewarding path to walk. for yourself and for everyone in your orbit.

I'm also constantly focusing my attention on innovation of art, technology, and human connection. With my next project wrapping up and starting to release to the world, you can certainly expect plenty of new releases in the future.

records.title: POLYAMOROUS
records.creator: 0x671041532A344AA7B6F774834cF0C833FD83eb30
records.note:
I grew up in Inglewood, CA by way of Houston, Tx. I had a very interesting childhood geographically being that I moved around a lot back and forth between H-Town, Shreveport and Los Angeles before permanently landing in Inglewood in 2002. Early on as a child, I was teased a lot because I was overweight and talked differently than the other children. I always felt too country for LA, but too proper for the south. At some point, entering adulthood, I found my swag (so to say) and started to express that through music. I’ve been able to cultivate a sound where I get lots of comparisons to Outkast, Ceelo Green, Curtis mayfield, and a host of other legendary artists I love and respect for their craft.

POLYAMOROUS is a song about the struggles of polyamory. This song also touches on the concept and perception of what polyamory truly is, all while giving you a glimpse of perspective from someone going through a challenging time in their relationship. Everyone always knows what they want, but are you always living in reality when you set expectations for your partner in love? Polyamory as a concept deals with people being in multiple romantic/intimate relationships at once, but as you dig deeper, you come to find that polyamorous people believe that just because you love someone, it doesn’t mean you own them.

As a fan of soul/gospel and alternative music, I thought these two sounds blended together were a perfect match to the song concept. I brung in my boy Yared to play guitar on this track to give it that real alternative feel that I love, and I hope you all enjoy!

Golden Egg winner of this NFT will receive the instrumental and a capella versions of this song. All collectors will receive access to my future metaverse performance.

records.title: Check On Me ft. Ro Marsalis
records.collection: Check On Me ft. Ro Marsalis
records.creator: 0x14e5D778c77574106f8241303C9Ec5F418A82085
records.note:
I initially went to therapy for anxiety but quickly discovered it was more than just that.

Being present for people has always been a part of my DNA.  Growing up in a big family gently trained my heart to be intentional with those I love and just people in general. My grandfather was a kind soul and I always remember him teaching me and my cousins during the summers we spent together to watch out for one another. To protect one another. And to check on one another.

I remember at young age my mother walking by my room, peeking her head in and saying, “Hey son, what are you doing? Are you okay?” And in turn as I got older and matured, I would do the same to her…every so often asking her what she was doing and making sure her heart and mind were settled. And if not, she was very open with me about it.

And so, as the years have gone by, I do my best to echo that gesture to others. My family, my friends, and even some just people I know. Randomly, consistently, and genuinely checking in. However, I’ve also come to learn over the years that not all people have the habit of checking on their friends built into their DNA.

Being the strong friend of my circle and influencer of other friend circles also gives me the reasonability to share and spread that sentiment that we should really take time to check on our friends. Because after spending so much time consistently, intentionally, and genuinely checking in on people…I suddenly realized I needed some of those same people to check on me. 

I initially went to therapy for anxiety but quickly discovered I had feelings buried deep beneath my heart that were soon unsurfaced…and inspired me to write this song.

records.title: Meet Me Where I Am
records.creator: 0xd17cC306A72B53834bFe0f5B636F60b03bfe8BBf
records.note:
i started “Meet Me Where I Am” at the beginning of this year as a series of verses about feeling like a stranger to myself. a lot of things in my life were suddenly in flux - and all of the things that usually keep me grounded felt like they were slipping through my hands. i was anxious that when the dust settled, nothing would feel the same again - that i’d never find the comfort & calm i’d become used to and that my relationships with family and friends would never be the same. this song is like an open letter to the people in my life - pleading that they will stick around when things settle.

in early september I minted the stems of “Meet Me Where I Am” with on-chain DAW Arpeggi (https://www.arpeggi.io) as one of the first artists to use their “clips” feature. it has been inspiring to see the bones of this song used in so many different ways - and to see all these stems repurposed on-chain. i’m thrilled to bring “Meet Me Where I Am” to Sound to bring this song in its original form to as many people as possible.

written & produced by ben kessler

records.title: Telephone
records.creator: 0x2f2581c49A79880561032094887F59bd6d777F75
records.note:
Back in December, I spent 5 days in Joshua Tree making music in an airbnb with my 2 favorite producers /best friends Blake Burchette & Tate Gardner. We flew from Nashville with minimal gear, but of course had to bring the Moog Grandmother. Our friend Ben Soto and photographer/videographer met us there for what turned to be such a special, spiritual bonding and creative trip, us four on a Cowboy Christmas in the desert.

"Telephone" was written on our last night in such an interesting way. The whole song was essentially built around random object percussion. I have to shout out Tiny Tamb (the tiny tambourine decor in the airbnb) for really carrying the song. I'll never forget him. But for real, writing this song felt extremely experimental and unique to the room and environment we were in at that moment. It really summed up the trip in a way that I don't think any of us expected. 

This song is about nostalgia. Writing it brought feelings and flashbacks of all those crazy little memories that make up what it feels like to truly live. To be free and young at heart. Nostalgia is familiar, but the feeling's also distant. Whether it's falling in love, bonfires at the beach on a Friday night, or driving around my childhood town, I am reminded of the duality of reminiscing. 

Blast it!

records.creator: 0x6f0c8217E0DC7508d1977EF67Cd75A09CF2308d2
records.note:
About "Nostalgia"

This piano piece arose from a few bars improvisation. I revisited this idea four years later and varied a little around it. Finally, in 2021, I completed the piece, which was then published in 2022. 

In finding a suitable title for this track and listening to it after a few days of absence, I realised it exuded nostalgic feel. The cover art aims to represent this nostalgic approach.
I remembered a silhouette of my profile created by a street paper cut artist in my childhood and felt this form of art would be a fitting choice. After familiarising myself with how to create paper cut art using a program for illustrations, I came up with a somewhat humorous take on the composition process -with me as the model. 

Adding a "paper cut like" artwork, the nostalgic thoughts about a childhood memory, and, of course, the vibe of the composition together was the final step for ´Nostalgia´.

The Golden Egg is a variation of the cover that incorporates the minting process -with the same whimsically smile of an older child.

records.title: Death Valley
records.creator: 0xDC0ECED78FEe73c25d82449B16d7D9E3372f808A
records.note:
"Death Valley" began to take shape even before I'd ever been there. From LA, it was just a drive away. Feeling a need to truly experience the place to finish the song, I ventured there solo on Christmas Day 2020, amidst the backdrop of the pandemic. The desert, the salt flats, the towering mountains – and notably, the profound silence I encountered on certain trails – deeply influenced the song's completion.

At its core, "Death Valley" is a reflection on self-reliance, a reminder about showing up for oneself and recognizing that we often have all we need within. It's about navigating life's vast expanses, much like the contrasting terrains of Death Valley, and finding inspiration and strength in solitude.

Following its 2021 release, I received messages from listeners who shared that the song perfectly echoed their own Death Valley adventures, capturing the essence of their experiences. It's always a heartening feeling when your creation resonates in such a personal way with others.

Now, in 2023, I'm excited to re-introduce "Death Valley" in a fresh format – as my first NFT song release.

records.title: you won't...
records.creator: 0xf7d6e70b7772696e471B3513762D9a9d7853ebD9
records.note:
"you won't..."  is a song I wrote after a difficult breakup in 2019.  I wanted to pour my emotions into music, but was so upset that I couldn't put the feeling into words. I needed to release some energy, so I went back to my hometown to jam with my old high school friends.  During one of our high volume practice sessions I started playing this hypnotic bassline that felt sad and reflective. A couple days later I recorded the bass and the words just came out of me.  


"you won't..." is about the moment you finally realize you've lost someone.  It's about the futility of thinking "what if" and the knee jerk reaction of believing you can fix things even when deep down you know you can't. 


The song was self/written and produced. The music video was shot in Taos, NM. Directed by Pierce Pyrzenski and shot by Mike Curry. It features Suze Meijer as a lead actress.

The world needs a wake-up call.

When I wrote and produced this song I imagined all those people who never had the chance to pursue their dreams.

People who lived hypnotized, attached to social beliefs, and to behaviors that removed their ability to pursue the best version of themselves.

Society and the system have us trapped. Going around in circles.

But if you zoom out, 10,000 feet, I believe that God and the Universe have given us all the tools, wisdom, and light to break free.

Wake up is that burst of energy for you to question things around you.

To make you think that everything you see is a lie and that for us to overcome evil, we need to unite, empower each other, share knowledge, and not comply with everything that the system tells us to do.

We need to take a step forward and take risks to create a forever change.

That we shouldn't fear to be brave, to be bold, and to be audacious in fighting for our purpose through honesty, dignity, and hard work.

One day we will hear Wake Up in the streets, and may that be the time that God sheds light behind our shoulders and helps us triumph over darkness. 

United we rise.

United we wake up.

records.title: Whale & Whale
records.creator: 0xEEe52E778D83EcF54A096288E445Dd93E6EdbFF0
records.note:
"...toothed whales produce short, ultrasonic clicks of high directionality and source level to probe their environment acoustically..." (2007, Madsen)

Immersed in our own bubble of loneliness, we take refuge in our digital lives, closing our eyes to the multitude of experiences and emotions that surround us during our daily lives. Acknowledging the existence of the people around us is the highest form of civilization that can be expected of human beings. The greatness of Life lies in the nuances of the reality that surrounds us. A reality that is fuzzy, intricate and extremely complex in our eyes. The only way we can know it is to create those interactions that this reality, on a subatomic level, create it and keep it alive. 

Some species of whales are capable through their teeth of emitting very loud sounds that are believed to be used to locate other whales even at a distance of many, many miles (called echolocation). The immensity of the ocean, its infinite vastness and its absolute three-dimensionality put these divine creatures in touch with their loneliness and compels them to use sound to contact other fellow creatures, which is in my opinion absolutely poetic.

We also have a voice with which to contact other people, but we forget to use it to learn about our fellow human beings. The artists has an even more powerful tool than just the voice to locate their fellow human beings: Their art. They also forget to use them to impact other people and to change their lives. Echolocation can indeed be performed by humans through their creativity, too. 

In this piece of improvisational piano music I play along with a group of sperm whales performing echolocation.

My genesis is a tribute to this majestic ocean creature and its ability to enchant man throughout its history. A story that has spanned the centuries to me, who decided to leave the water, land and air, becoming an intergalactic whale.

records.title: BUZZIN

records.note:
"Buzzin" is an dark tech vibe beat single created by young music producer Sho. The inspiration for the song came from a nighttime adventure he had during his college years. Sho and his friends decided to attend a secret underground party. The party was located in an abandoned warehouse and was exclusive to those "in the know."

Upon arriving, Sho was captivated by the atmosphere: the flickering neon lights, the deafening bass, and the people around him. What struck him the most, however, was the combination of sounds and light feels like a bee that kept buzzing around the crowd, as if attracted by the music and the enthusiasm of the people.

Sat in his small home studio, contemplating how to translate that night's experience into music. He began experimenting with various rhythms and melodies, eventually finding a musical element that could capture the vibe of that night. He decided to use a synthesizer to mimic the scene hover above his mind and the robust drum set was inspired by opium artists like Ken Carson.

records.title: Water. Life.
records.creator: 0x7Dd44cD59D0320a8A2A0a6F521BFE767108dD2E3
records.note:
I grew up in New York City and it feels like my entire life has been spent reclaiming my relationship with the planet. From having to stay on-guard 24/7 to only experiencing slices of green space, it's really difficult to understand what really matters: Sneakers? Fast fashion? The gangster code?

Growing my own food and plugging into resilient local economies has given me more fulfillment than anything I gained in the warped version of city life. This song is a prayer, a blessing for what we can build using these tools that mean so much more than cool collectibles. We are redefining value and who gets to benefit from it. I hope it resonates with you!

The beat is a collaboration with @DanielBonefont on IG and BandLab.

It's a colourful palette that reflects our goal to explore various cultural and musical landscapes in future projects.

records.title: SELF LOVE (feat. Akacia)
records.creator: 0x2463a967955eF5a4217d843d617EB9182F84b566
records.note:
Hey there, I'm Stan, a music producer based in Brussels,Belgium, and I'm dropping my first track on Sound!

My musical journey began at the age of 6 when I started playing the violin. Later, when my family and I moved to Belgium, I picked up the classical guitar. After years of diving into classical music, I started getting into electronic tunes I heard on the radio. I was completely clueless about how those sounds were made, but with a bit of research and my parents' support, I finally got my hands on my first music-making software at 16.

Once I realized the incredible potential of making electronic music, I made a quick decision to stop my guitar lessons and dedicate myself to it.

During my first year of college, I launched my project as SVDKO and released my debut track, 'Innocence.' A year later, it caught the attention of an audience through some semi-viral moments on Vine and Spotify. That was the turning point when I realized that music could be more than just a hobby; it could become my Plan A.

After releasing several independent songs, having big sync opportunities with the likes of Apple and more recently Dior and crafting a sound that combined rock and electronic vibes during the pandemic - I felt it was time for me to come back to the genre that inspired me in the first place and write a dance and electronic-focused EP.

'SELF LOVE' was actually the first demo I made for that EP, but funnily enough, it didn't make the final cut. SELF LOVE has that rock/electronic blend I liked so much but leans more towards a dance record. I had the chance to collaborate with Akacia on the vocals and ONLYTHENEXT who played a significant role in the production process. 'SELF LOVE' is all about self-empowerment, setting high standards in relationships, and refusing to settle for anything less than genuine commitment and love. At this point in my life, that's the message that resonates with me the most, and I hope you’ll find something in it for you as well ❤️

records.collection: Different Spaces (Feat. Gaspar Narby) - Golden Egg
records.creator: 0x3448882f62D7CC5F91514F0103394a3313DAB26f
records.note:
This track began when I went over to Gaspar's house for lunch a few months back. Both of us had recently gotten pretty addicted to granular synthesis and spent the first couple hours we were with each-other just messing around and making the weirdest noises possible. 

Gaspar then pulled up this beautiful recording of a harpist playing a piece live in this big open space with loads of reverb in the sample. We chopped it up and ran it through a bunch of granular channels until it made this almost digital sounding pluck. I messed about on his Ableton Push creating the beat whilst he cut up some MS-20 white noise stutters for percussion to layer in. 

When I took the track home I sat with it for a bit as I felt it felt a bit too heavy and abrupt than what I usually release but ended up adding a bunch of chords, arpeggios, more drums and arranging it to what it is now. 

The track kind of represents a different space for both of us that neither of us had really ever written in before. It feels much more heavy than a lot of what we make but also very emotional at the same time and I've grown to love the journey that it takes you on. 


Alsooooo, 

Hi, I'm Joseph :)

But I make music a 'Indigo Eyes'

I make A LOT of music... but this is my first to end up on the blockchain :) 

I'm gonna be posting on here pretty regularly as I have a lot I want to put out and this feels like a good place to test the water and see what people are into.

Any support would seriously mean the world to me <3

Catch you all soon!

"Lonely Cowboy" is a deeply moving song that carries the weight of raw emotions within its beautiful melodies. Through this musical masterpiece, Kayo paints a poignant picture of personal struggle and transformation. The song serves as a testament to the healing power of music, as it was composed during a challenging period in kayo's life, becoming a therapeutic outlet for his emotions.

What sets "Lonely Cowboy" apart is the captivating raspiness in Kayo's voice, adding a sense of authenticity and grit to the composition. This quality, combined with the evocative lyrics and melodies, creates a powerful synergy that has the potential to send shivers down your spine. It's especially heart-wrenching to learn that this song, which holds such profound significance, was the last creation on Kayo's stolen laptop, marking the loss of a treasure trove of music. "Lonely Cowboy" encapsulates the essence of how music can be a lifeline, and its listeners can truly sense the depth of emotion and importance it holds for Kayo.

records.title: bololo
records.creator: 0x4a50c7137C6d8A1b0099abd5D1A13A80b3de7867
records.note:
Before you ask, the word 'bololo' is a slang term native to my hometown Barranquilla. we use it to describe a big mess, a brawl, something along those lines. but it can also mean a huge party that is just super out of control.

When I was working on this track initially with The Fund, Mark Johns, and Kate Morgan, they asked if there were any cool spanish words we could write around. I obviously hopped on google and looked up Costeño slang (costeño is what people from Barranquilla are called!) and bololo came up - as you can see we went with it!

I wanted the song to sound like what the word means - hence why the track is pretty crazy production-wise! I also decided to write about a crazy night, I just put myself in the shoes of someone who went out and had one of those nights where you end up in 6 different places, meet 3 people, become friends, and never see them again. I have personally never experienced anything like this so it was pretty fun to just dramatize what this whole ordeal would be like.

We all had the most fun making and recording this song, there are so many little details hidden in it that make it so special, you just have to listen to it over and over again I guess! enjoy "bololo"!!!

records.collection: New Now- Goose Pärk (ft. Giiipson Poet) - Golden Egg
records.creator: 0xE8b8679C248307A37A2Bd35Dd43D2278ba346138
records.note: The song came about when I was sitting around one day thinking about the old Madden soundtracks and how I should make an alternative rock beat. I went into Ableton to make the beat and began to hear the lyrics for the hook in my head. I recorded my hook and began writing the verse; I wanted this song to be powerful for all ages. I only had my hook and verse when I shared it with Giipson Poet, a local artist in my city, who loved the concept of the song and wanted to record a verse. Throughout the process, he noticed that I didn't have much passion in my verse. He helped me by giving me examples of how to better my delivery when recording my verses. Giiipson Poet, also had the idea to include a bridge in the track. I went back to Ableton Live, copied the intro guitar, and added it after each of our verses to add another catchy melody to the track. After this process was done, the mixing process began which took about 2-3 days. We shared the song with a few people and received a great response back. We must say that this song is one for the books and should be enjoyed by all ages.

records.title: The Precipice
records.creator: 0x795050DeCc0322567C4f0098209d4eDC5a69b9D0
records.note:
I made The Precipice while getting acquainted with GrimesAI and going through a mini existential crisis throughout the wave of AI news earlier this year. I've always found technology creatively inspiring but its hard not to think about all the unforeseen risks, especially for frontier tech advancing at an exponential rate.

Given my concerns, I appreciate how Grimes has always embraced tech while not losing sight of what is special about being human. She is also an inspiration to me musically, so I was really excited to make a song using her voice.

The title of the song is borrowed from a book of the same name about existential risk (by Tony Ord). It made me think about how our relationship with AI is similar to extremely passionate love: incredibly exciting and potentially life-changing, but could end like a Shakespearean tragedy if we aren't lucky or prepared. 

That metaphor inspired me to make a music video using the 1993 film adaptation of Romeo & Juliet, reimagined through an AI image generator:
https://youtu.be/_WssPKL1vIA
