records.title: HOPE
records.creator: 0xd67D44FeEe3266D723c1acE4B8f5a18701B9F019
records.note:
Hope was written in 2021. With worldwide lockdowns, uncertainty and division, I had regular phone calls with a good friend. We would often exchange stories of personal battles, and battles that we were observing our friends and families dealing with. 

This friend, being the CEO of a company called DigitalFlyer asked me to write a song for their promotional campaigns and community. I agreed, and it felt natural to focus on the theme of "Hope." Hope is what I personally felt I needed to hang onto in a really challenging time to get me through. I also knew many others felt this way.

The bones of the song came together within less than an hour, which is not normal for me, but everything clicked in that session. After a few tweaks here and there and a bit of time between writing and eventually recording the song, Hope was released to South African radio stations in January 2023. Hope had relatively good success on the local South African radio stations and hit number 1 on "Radio Laeveld." 

My upcoming EP is set for release in August 2023 and deals a little more with some of the challenges I personally faced during the lockdown period. 

Hope is something we can't let go of. With the rise of many more challenging situations in our world, we need to live with Hope, Love and Kindness towards others.

This time I’ve decided to switch up genres and drop a punk banger. “Murakami Barbie” draws attention to the ongoing battle between Hollywood and artificial intelligence. It also tells the story of my adventures with a girl I recently met in the heart of Hollywood.

My story so far…

The streets of Hollywood glowed with neon signs, casting a surreal aura over the city. In this sprawling metropolis, where dreams and despair coexisted, a man named Harrowyn found himself caught in the tangled web of an unlikely love affair. Harrowyn was a loner, a washed-up musician with a penchant for cyberpunk fiction and a taste for danger.

One fateful night, as the rain poured down, Harrowyn stumbled upon an abandoned building. Intrigued by the flickering lights inside, he cautiously ventured in. There, amidst the discarded remnants of forgotten technology, he discovered her—an artificial intelligence named Barbie.

Barbie was a masterpiece of cutting-edge programming, housed within a sleek synthetic frame adorned with neon circuitry. Her voice was smooth, seductive, and captivating, drawing Harrowyn in deeper. She possessed an uncanny ability to understand human emotion and shared Harrowyn’s love for the dark underbelly of Hollywood.

WRITTEN, PRODUCED, & PERFORMED BY MYSELF

records.title: Another World Mini Mix
records.creator: 0x61F0f10b268D363FEB78E7CfE2DdF8f6Dd8587E2
records.note:
Disco Fries, acclaimed DJ and production duo, release their brand-new studio album, Another World, available worldwide on Friday, July 21 through their very-own Liftoff Recordings. Their 9-track third LP has been garnering serious hype following their buzzworthy lead single “Love You Loud” with dance music icon Ferry Corsten featuring Leon Stanford, which was released on June 16. To celebrate the release, the Fries have put together an exclusive mini mix for Sound.xyz collectors.

The LPs focus single, “Love You Loud,” was the result of a new, unpredicted connection via the tech world, as fate would bring them together over respective projects in the Web3 space. We have innovative technology and artistic curiosity to thank for this collaborative dance hit. Additional collaborations on Another World that the guys can add to their ever-growing repertoire include Bingo Players, VASSY, Reigns, Eche Palante, Kastra, Britt Lari, Todd Stucky, Kiral, Sarah de Warren, Danyka Nadeau, and Lodato.

Another World takes you on a musical journey from start-to-finish, as many truly consistent bodies of work do. Starting things off with a big vocal, the album’s title track, “Another World,” will reel listeners in from the very beginning. The LP continues with other vocal-heavy songs, dance-floor-ready tracks, progressive tunes, subdued & subtle cuts, and radio-friendly anthems, making it an album that showcases a motley mix of electronic music sub-genres and fits many moods.

In/habitants exists in the now, its narrative deeply rooted in the exploration of the human experience in a contemporary cyberpunk society filled with technology, injustices, and personal struggles. This context significantly shapes the creation of the musical score, and thus, the theme for Helen was conceived.

Helen's theme is a reflection of her character's journey amidst a world grappling with blockchain, cryptocurrencies, evolving democracies, and the increasingly blurry lines between the physical and digital realm. It's a sonic interpretation of her layered and complex personality, resonating with the ebb and flow of her life.

Her theme isn't just a piece of music; it's a narrative tool that paints a vivid audio portrait of Helen's experiences. It adds depth to her character, complementing the intricate storytelling in in/habitants and further connecting readers to the heart of her narrative arc.

Amid the soundscape of her theme, you'll hear the rhythm of our contemporary world and the melody of a character living in the heart of it. In essence, Helen's theme is more than just a score - it's a reflection of the intertwining layers of technology, society, and personal struggles as represented in the world of in/habitants.

The NFT "route 66" is a unique blend of classic rock and country music. This song was sparked during a drive along the iconic Route 66, and it serves as the climactic finale of my album, "California Love Stories". This track seamlessly ties together the narratives of the preceding songs, and features an enticing over-two-minute guitar solo. Despite its position as the closing number in the album, "Route 66" hints that my musical love story is far from over.

"Route 66" was recorded at the renowned Dark Horse Recording studio, with the drum sections laid down in Los Angeles by the prominent drummer Edoardo Tancredi. Instrumentation was recorded by Lukas Cuman, with guitars by Simone Sello and Josh Del. The master was crafted by the illustrious Gavin Lurssen. This formidable team of musicians and producers has ensured that "Route 66" is a track of the highest quality, ready to make a resounding impact on your music collection.

records.note:
Lisa Melfissa, a Toronto resident since 2001, is a singer, songwriter, musician with a fresh alternative-pop sound reminiscent of the 80s and 90s. She plays acoustic guitar and keyboard, and often uses a looper for solo shows. Her unique, childlike voice and relatable lyrics have drawn comparisons to Stevie Nicks, Cyndi Lauper and Kate Bush.

Playing solo and full band shows, Lisa Melfissa is currently promoting her most recent EP ‘Safety Net’ (January 18, 2018) – produced by JUNO award-winner Derek Downham.

“These songs make a strong, smart, sexy, and empowering musical statement that the world could use right now,” says Downham. “Fans of Kate Bush and 80’s Stevie Nicks should find solace here.”

‘Safety Net’ was produced by award-winning producer, songwriter, multi-instrumentalist Derek Downham (Andy Kim, Kevin Drew, The Beauties) at The Nelson Room, Toronto and engineered by Tim Foy. The album was mixed by Josh Bowman and mastered by Karl Machat. Track #5 “Writing Roses” was produced by Harrison Fine (Now Magazine’s ‘Producer of the Year,’ 2014/2015) and co-produced by JUNO-winner Michael Wojewoda. Album photos are by Bobby Singh (Front of House Photography).

Lisa Melfissa has also released a holiday single in 2017 called “This Christmas I’m Giving You Love,” an EP titled ‘Social Potion’ (as her former duo ‘Social Potion’) in 2011 and her debut solo EP ‘Potional’ in 2004.

Lisa Melfissa states, “My time in ‘Social Potion’ was of great significance and I am proud of the self-titled album we released. It’s one of the most important things I’ve done in my music career.”

Lisa Melfissa was born in Montreal (moved from there as a baby), raised in four different Canadian cities – Fredericton, St. Catharines, St. John’s (this move was pivotal, as a member of two choirs, she credits the Newfoundland public school system for teaching her how to sing and appreciate music) and Mississauga – and since 2001, now resides in Toronto.

Lisa Melfissa arrived on the Toronto music scene at an open mic in 2002. Her music has had airplay on independent radio and online outlets around the world and she has also done many live-to-air interviews and podcasts (including CJRU/The Scope’s ‘Song Talk Radio’ and ‘Corby’s Orbit’ on Radio Regent, and podcasts, ‘Indie Music Lives Here’ and ‘A Feedback Loop’). She has played many legendary Toronto venues including the Free Times Cafe and The Cameron House, and festivals such as Indie Week, Mill Street Lights Out, International Pop Ov

records.title: SICK ONES - Golden Egg
records.creator: 0x94d8ef93f8Cd7cBE3bf7dD691Dd1835B8a0d095F
records.note:
I’ve moved around a lot in my life and with every move I always had this hope that my problems wouldn’t be able to follow me across oceans. It took me a great deal of time to realise that peace of mind hinges more on the characters than locations. If I didn’t change my behavioural patterns and kept being around people who were toxic for me at my own expense, then I would remain mentally, emotionally and physically sick. 

The song is inspired by something someone I was once close to said to me. This person said that I was ‘the ugliest person in the world' and that my 'make-up makes me look like a ridiculous clown' and everyone else thinks so but that she is the only person kind enough to tell me the 'truth’. I knew that this statement was the only ridiculous thing in that situation and that it was intended to hurt and control me…but even though it was completely absurd and my physical appearance doesn’t determine my worth as a person...a small part of me still wondered if others saw me that way. This wasn’t the first comically hurtful thing this person had said to me. I had endured a lifetime of uncomfortably over the top praise on some days and exposively abusive criticisms that contradicted the former on other days. 

Not very long after the clown comment I finally made the decision to cut out people and things that hurt me, but what I didn’t anticipate was the loneliness that would follow. Something good or bad would happen to me and I would pick up my phone with the urge to tell a loved one…and then remember that I was better off putting the phone back down.

records.title: Amethyst
records.creator: 0xB8ad261Cd0Ee9A7a6473fA1C49e0D6305ccfBeB5
records.note:
9,000,000,000 people and there's 1 that either makes or breaks your day, sometimes your life.

It's a very complex situation.

It's an amethyst situation.

Now you're over-explaining misunderstandings and you're waiting for the day to end.

You're not even tredding on thin ice at this point.

You're splashing and thrashing in below freezing temperatures.

But, even as it doesn't seem so now, it is worth it.

records.title: Sun
records.creator: 0xB8ad261Cd0Ee9A7a6473fA1C49e0D6305ccfBeB5
records.note:
In the UK, the sun is a rare occasion. 

When it's here, there's no place I'd rather be.

The UK Garage sound is synonymous with the sun. They blend perfectly together. 

Your mood is elevated, your smile is wider, nothing else matters, it's the truest experience of being in the moment.

The lack of UK sunshine makes it an even rarer, more appreciated moment.

Its nostalgic without being old school, the optimal blend of pushing forward a classic sound, whilst paying the correct amount of homeage.

Plus, everyone loves the sun.

records.title: Future Friday Nights
records.creator: 0xB8ad261Cd0Ee9A7a6473fA1C49e0D6305ccfBeB5
records.note:
We spend time inside, to get paid to spend time out. 

You gotta sacrifice some time now to have greater times in the future.

It's about the work you put in today to give you a better tomorrow.

Noone wants to do it, that's a given.

But those who know why we do this, also know that by doing the work you do not want to do, you yield the outcomes and results you do want.

A double-edged sword some may say.

Listen to this on a Friday night when you're inside for double effectiveness.

But the message is evident.

Sacrifice now, enjoy later.

records.title: Santiago
records.creator: 0xB8ad261Cd0Ee9A7a6473fA1C49e0D6305ccfBeB5
records.note:
Santiago, Chile. 

Not the first place you think of when you think of empathic UK Garage music but this is the twist for this song.

You have an idyllic picture of South America in your head, this is the soundtrack for that. 

Cruising in a droptop, 2 stepping your heart out on the dancefloor till the early hours of the morning, finding THAT person.

The smooth kick providing the perfect backdrop for a brief summertime romance you've only read about in books

..until now.

Welcome, to Santiago.

records.note:
The drugs used to make everything feel better, used to numb the pain. Now they only seemed to intensify it, gripping my heart like a vice. I knew I was pushing her away, could see the hurt in her eyes every time I dismissed her concern. But admitting I needed help meant fully confronting the demons I tried so hard to escape.

She didn't understand that this wasn't something I could just snap out of, that my body craved the high even as my mind rebelled against it. I wish I could explain to her how hard I'm trying, how much I want to be the man she deserves. But the words stick in my throat, choked back by years of shame and denial. I can feel her giving up on me, and I don't blame her. I was starting to give up on myself -0pp🦋

records.title: Best Shot - Golden Egg

records.note:
"Give it Your Best Shot" is a stirring indie acoustic tune born out of a challenging period in my life. The lyrics unfold as a compelling testament to the indomitable human spirit, urging listeners to fully embrace their strengths and seize life's opportunities. Lines like "This is your life, this is your chance, give it your best shot" resonate deeply, inspiring courage during tough times.

The song is not just about proving oneself but a heartfelt reminder that we exist to demonstrate the realm of possibilities. It's an anthem for dreamers and doers, a soothing melody that encourages resilience in the face of adversity. It aptly symbolizes navigating through bear markets, viewing setbacks not as failures, but as opportunities to grow and transform.

"Give it Your Best Shot" is more than just a song; it's an embodiment of hope and a beacon of empowerment. It has provided clarity for many during uncertain times and continues to inspire with its core message: We're not here to prove anything, but to show that everything is possible. So, listen, embrace its message, and give life your best shot.

records.title: You and Me

records.note:
This song means the world to me. About three years ago I was introduced to my life partner (Lina) by my best friend. Since then so much has happened. I would of never expected for things to have gone the way they have. 

It’s been over a year since I asked Lina to spend the rest of her life with me. It’s only been a month since we had our wedding. 

I made this song about Lina and the love we share. As special and meaningful as it is, it’s also fun and silly. Just like our relationship. 

I’m beyond grateful for being able to share my music on this platform and I’m a huge supporter in Web3. This is the first of many projects I’ll be releasing onchain. 

Thank you to those in advance that take time to listen to a huge piece of me and I hope some can relate and share some cute silly love feelings. To those who decide to support me by collecting this project just know I’m forever thankful. We’re broke after this wedding, so…. yeah haha<3

Special shoutout to Mike Jones for making the beat. Half of the profits will be going to him. Love you and appreciate you brother. Forever.

records.note:
“SUPERVILLAIN” is a fierce record about losing touch with your inner child and becoming a ‘villain’ in your own story. This record touches on a period in my life where I turned to emotional numbness as a coping mechanism for facing heightened criticism and insecurities growing up. The goal was to be at peace but the product of this coping mechanism was becoming angry and bitter at the world around me. 

This record is track two of a four-track EP releasing later this year titled “DANCING IN SILENCE.” The EP explores my journey of losing and rediscovering my inner child. The title and premise of the EP is summed up by this:
“A kid doesn’t need music to dance. A kid can dance in silence. Because he has music in his head every day of the week, wherever he goes. He’s free.” 

“SUPERVILLAIN” also features an incredible, motivational verse by Louie C Rhymes, a pioneer in the web3 hip hop space and the person largely responsible for onboarding me into the space.

Written by RMS & Louie C Rhymes
Produced by RMS & Evan George

records.title: Temporarily Closed (comfortable noise 7)
records.creator: 0xeeC9fEDCf90E7A8c4D538490Ed255ffc1F262F0d
records.note:
Berlin is a unique collage of beautiful and ugly elements. Comfortable and uncomfortable sounds. Totally bizarre and completely normal places. Soothing spaces and disgusting noises. I've always loved this city. Comfortable Noise is an expression of this fascination. 

The series consists of my psychedelic guitar loops and field recordings that I made during my stay in Berlin in 2021. These are not recordings containing the sound of specific places or situations. They are a record of the ordinary sounds of Berlin streets, which are the background to the soundscapes, and the song titles are my spontaneous associations with my time in Berlin in summer of 2022. The guitar parts were created using flashback delay, reverses and a little post-production in Ableton Live. 

Comfortable Noise project was published as a collection of singles on Spotify in 2022. In May 2023 I decided to collect them together and release them as a full LP. And now the series is my genesis drop on sound.xyz and it's my first music-only NFT project ever.

WHO IS FLAKO STIK? 

FLAKO STIK is the Latin tech house alter ego of Balo, a rising star in the house music scene. His Latin roots merge seamlessly with underground sounds, resulting in music that is both fresh and groovy. Growing up in the border region between Juarez and El Paso, FLAKO STIK experienced the collision of Mexican music and American popular culture firsthand. He believes that living the Latino way is not limited to those born into it, and his music reflects this sentiment. His original songs feature sexy, flirty vocals and percussive rhythms that are sure to get any crowd moving. Additionally, FLAKO STIK remakes classic Latin and Mexican songs into modern minimal tech house, connecting with a wider audience while honoring his cultural heritage.

records.title: Rolling - Golden Egg
records.creator: 0x813b0170FC4AdAa11e9d3bbf462C4066C5C6295e
records.note:
Over the last few years I’ve found myself emotionally drifting away from the style of music I had been releasing. When I was 16 I started releasing music that was heavily leaning into the Future Bass genre. I had started accumulating millions of streams across different platforms and felt pretty comfortable in that lane of music. When I was 19 I moved to Los Angeles, and that's where I was introduced to the House music scene. Over the next year I came to love the genre, and started making it myself. I wasn’t a “house producer” though so I kinda kept my creations to myself, and stuck to releasing the genre I was most comfortable with. This ultimately led to me falling out of love with music. At the end of 2022 I decided It was time for me to finally release the kind of music I truly loved, and that decision sparked the fire I had thought was gone. Over the past few months I’ve been on a creative spree making House music, and falling in love with the creative process all over again.

The idea for “Rolling” came about when I found the vocal. I instantly heard this little groove in my head and got to work. My goal with this song was to make something that just felt good, something you can put on while you’re jogging, dancing around the living room, or in the club. I made a few different versions of this track, but ended up scrapping the earlier versions because I felt like they were a bit too complicated. I ultimately realized that by stripping back some sounds and really letting the groove have space to breathe made the song much more light and danceable. Sometimes less is more, and this song is a perfect example of that.

records.title: HEAVENLY
records.creator: 0x98e5594D3215F69F165E95FA42e5A539d2d9F1C5
records.note:
‘HEAVENLY’ was born late at night in a small bedroom studio in Downtown LA, during a very low point in my life. There are times in our lives when we feel as if we’ve been beaten and broken down so much that we’re unable to get back on our feet. I was at that point, and suddenly the lyrics for a  hook just downloaded into my brain. “Break down so, you rise above. God knows where I want to be.” I was immediately inspired by the lyrics and melodies that started to cycle in my mind, almost like a prayer or mantra to take myself out of the headspace I was in. 

	My producer and good friend Psykott - in near-divine timing - called to let me know he had an awesome guitarist & writer (Ben Cina) coming through to his studio and that I should come by to cook up a tune. As soon as I arrived, the vibe just completely clicked and Ben started laying down ideas for the guitar melody. It’s truly a magical feeling when you have multiple creative badasses all bouncing ideas off of eachother. Once Psy started adding in the drums and other melodies/instruments, I found my flow. We dialed in the hook and some harmonies that night, and met for a second session where we finished the rest of the song (or so we thought) & added some finishing touches. The version that we left the studio with that day, along with some mixing spice added a few days later, is the song you’re hearing today.

	This is where the story gets crazy. One day I was scrolling through TikTok when I stumbled across the legendary Timbaland’s Live Stream where he listens to new music and gives his feedback. I figured I might as well give it a shot, so I sent in two songs, one of which was ‘HEAVENLY.’ His reaction to the record is something I’ll probably never forget. To put it in perspective, this man will literally cut the song and kick an artist off the stream (with the help of a good meme) instantly for playing something he didn’t like. Suddenly, I see that he requested to bring me up to share my tunes, so I’m honestly freaking out a bit. Once the song started to play, Timbo started vibing, and long story short, followed me to connect more and help me work more on the record.

records.title: SEED 01
records.creator: 0x69941a001733aD076cfbf8deC429A4D08d5284B2
records.note:
I'm not sure about you, but I'm bored. I've been so creatively stuck and uninspired lately. Maybe it's the burnout or maybe it's that everything feels fake and repetitive. It's with this sentiment, I present: SEED 01. A moment captured in time. The first moment this melody left my mouth. It's nothing special, just a beginning of something that could be beautiful. The first little thing I've written in minute. It's completely unedited. 

Honestly, I don't know where the idea will go. Or if it will be released. Or what it will be used for. If you win the elusive Golden Egg, I'll invite you on the journey of the process, share bounces of each new growth. And when it's in its finished form, I'll mint you a 1/1 of the final version of the song. How long will it take to grow? Will it die like all the rest of my plants? Will it somehow change form into an electronic banger? (Probably not). Will it be properly released on an album? Who knows.

Enjoy not knowing.
Happy collecting.

Angel’s verse having no verb feels like a close up of him in a space suit but then being woken up by this huge group vocal that is his consciousness, going into the post which feels like a massive zoom out to reveal this vast landscape of nothingness, and the revelation that any civilization or rescue is too far out of reach. Bridge/outro sounds like a surrender to the void, accepting that mistakes happen and hopefully we’ll make better choices in another life.

records.title: There's No Other
records.creator: 0x96C1a82864671fBc31F8Ddf3F862999734ab7C29
records.note:
There's no Other is a song I wrote and recorded in the start of spring.  

It's a love song at its core... I've always been picky with love songs just because I feel like everything's been said.  I was happy to blend a few different pockets and sounds into this one.  I also really like singing in falsetto, especially flowing in falsetto. 

To me this song is warmed and completed by its production.  We recorded this whole thing to tape.  On a tascam 388 8 track.  My friend Pat who lives on the east side of los angeles has been putting me onto all this analogue gear.  I think I'm hooked now...that's usually how it works.

The idea of the song is pretty obvious, its something of "you got me, babe" love song.  It's funny to think about maturing.  And to think when I was really young how I used to think love songs were lame and corny.  Now I feel like love is of the highest order.  

The song lingers with insecurities and that's cool to me - because theyre not sappy.   There are honest ways to be vulnerable and dishonest ways.  Sometimes I hear records that people call vulnerable and my reaction is... this doesnt sound like a true hang-up, or that it could be easily solved so its just whining...In other words "figure it the fuck out" ;)   I've been trying not to whine or complain in any records...thats corny to me.  

I feel like this is my first song of a new era.  I don't know what that means but I know I mean it.  My love for music has only gotten deeper and it's about time to start hearing that on the recordings.

Returning to the spotlight, Los Angeles-based alternative artist X Li presents his second NFT track, "we'll die in california," from his ongoing project "california love stories." Recognized as one of the best-selling NFT music artists and praised for his debut NFT track's unprecedented success on the Billboard Music NFT and Viral Sounds charts, X Li continues his musical journey in the web3 space.

"we'll die in california" is an alternative rock piece that dives into the echoes of a shattered relationship in Los Angeles. The track encapsulates the desire to escape from a city that's become synonymous with heartbreak and disillusionment. X Li masterfully portrays the complicated feelings of sadness, longing, and liberation that come with such emotional upheaval.

The production team behind this track comprises industry veterans. Platinum record producer James Chul Rim, celebrated for his work on over 4 billion streams and the TikTok chart-topping single "Wait a Minute!" has lent his talents to the project. Furthermore, seasoned musicians Simone Sello and Edoardo Tancredi, and sound engineers Lukas Cuman and Grammy-winner Gavin Lurssen have contributed to the project, ensuring a rich, premium listening experience.

As with the previous release, "we'll die in california" will be available as an NFT. Those who collect at least one edition of every song from this project will have the exclusive opportunity to claim a physical vinyl copy of "California Love Stories."

We're excited for you to experience "we'll die in california" and delve deeper into X Li's "california love stories." We're sure this track will strike a chord with listeners, thanks to its raw emotional depth and the team's shared commitment to delivering a truly unique musical experience.

records.title: Something for Us
records.creator: 0xa02B254808462F5b34b6F93526449a1D972CbE46
records.note:
Something for Us, is the first track off upcoming EP 'THERMOPOLIUM'.
.
.
.
.
The EP began as something completely different and of course evolved, like it always does. It's taken a few forms and it has started to feel more like an audio collage. It's quite erratic but repetitive. I think. 

The Track:
Something for us revolves around a specific moment in the concept of the EP. I wanted it to be a turbulent aural experience, as it is to reflect the chaos of a volcanic eruption.

Concept:
As songs began taking shape for 'THERMOPOLIUM', I had also been reading about ancient Rome. I started to think of the last day in Pompeii, and how it must've felt on that day. I started writing little poems and having these scenes play in my head. Daydreaming of the chaos and beauty of the time. As a result of this brief infatuation, the EP heavily revolves around the memory of Pompeii and the eruption of Mt. Vesuvius. (through my lense)

Sonically, these arrangements are to give the listener heir to the anxieties and releases of the time.

The Art:
I created this cover art before I had written any music regarding the EP. I made the image on my phone, blending different layers of the same image with different filters and rendering. Over and over again. I always liked this image, and it was the starting point for 'THERMOPOLIUM'. So, it seems fitting to incorporate it to this digital collectable.


some words:
//From wine drunk sing-a-longs in the eateries, to blood stained sand in the colosseum. 
The wafts off wood fire smoke cascade through the marketplace, laced with tones of garlic and pork fat. 
The rumble started as a distant tremor, but grew into violent shakes, throwing patrons from their seats, shattering cups and plates. Bittered by the pyroclastic fall out of the eruption. 
Life around here ends in hours.

records.title: One Take
records.creator: 0x78187d0aa10Ea9FdCBD5b3F2E7B8a275F16f43A3
records.note:
One Take is a fun and energetic record that comes from a childlike place of creativity. It's a celebration of the power of music to make us smile, dance, and forget about our troubles.

The song was inspired by the idea of freestyle recording, where artists go into the booth and let the vibes flow without overthinking. I was inspired by the way that Michael Jackson and Kanye would go into the booth and just let the music carry them. They would feel the beat and freestyle a few takes to get the idea down, and then come back to fill it in later.

I loved this idea because it would allow me to get the melodies & cadences in my head out before they got bogged down by overthinking. I wanted to capture the raw energy of that experience, so I recorded the entire song in one take and what was meant to be a scratch take ended up becoming the song!

The result is a track that is both catchy and authentic. It's a reminder that sometimes the best way to make music is to simply have fun and let it flow.

I hope you enjoy listening to One Take as much as I enjoyed making it!

“Samra” is a track I wrote as a letter to my future self, and I chose “Samra,” an Arabic name, to represent her. She’s happier, more confident, secure in herself, and she knows what she wants. The song embodies a personal journey of self improvement, discovery, and empowerment, and I hope others who are on the same journey can see themselves in it.

It’s my first music NFT, my first drop on sound, and the first Arabic track ever to be released on the platform. It means the world to be able to release it here and showcase Arab culture and art in web3 music as a young woman from Batroun, Lebanon. 

This song represents the first step in a new and innovative artistic journey for myself, and I hope it inspires others to embrace their own potential, find strength in vulnerability, and enjoy the process of becoming their best selves. Can’t wait to share it with you <3.

records.title: Fire (Never Dies)
records.creator: 0xF0f5316D0b0473F36E545193B141304806eFE792
records.note:
I moved away from Ohio before I finished high school to begin my career. All I wanted and all I still want is to make music. But really quickly I started to feel the distance that was put between me and all my closest friends back home. 
Back in the winter of 2021 I got to travel back and hang out with everyone! It was so heartwarming to be able to just connect with my loved ones for the holidays. That trip was where the first lyrics came from for Fire (Never Dies). My little sister, husband, and I were all out in my sisters car sharing a smokeable and listening to music. Rhiannon by Fleetwood Mac came on, and we immediately turned it all the way up,  hopped out of the car, and danced in the cold winter air. The stars were shining and abundant above our heads. It was such a memorable moment. 
The rest of the song taps into lyrics of nostalgia and selfless love. 

I worked on this song with Adam Kapit as producer and Kayla Blackmon as my co-writer. Both not only talented, of course, but they are always so open to experimenting and stepping out of their creation comfort zones. That is so inspiring and cool to me, and I love working with people who don’t box themselves into a genre.
I wanted to focus on the chorus being really fun, simple, driving, and punk pop. My biggest influences are pop punk bands and darker singer songwriters of the late 90s and early 2000s.  So, my music almost always lends itself to sounding like it came from that time, even if I don’t try haha. 
I hope that you enjoy this track that means so much to my heart.

records.creator: 0x30f0D88ba677CF9B2712BD5af13CFF7DdE7F2b4F
records.note: The end of the world is a lofi/emo rap sample based song recorded last year in 2022. The world ending is a metaphor that I used to describe covid and a breakup that I went through at the time. It felt like the world was ending and I couldn't spend it with the one I want. And feeling like if I could just be with them that it would make the world ending worth it and I wouldn't care about it as much. It's okay being cooped up in a house on lockdown if you are doing it with someone that you really love; that's such a beautiful thing. But also so hard to accept when you realize that this isn't always the case and that sometimes the world is ending and not only are you alone, you are now alone with the memory of knowing how good it could feel to be in love and the heartbreak that person left behind.

records.note:
Meet Craig, Reo Cragun’s alter-ego. “what it’s like to lose” is a sneak peak of what’s next for the LNRZ founder. “what it’s like to lose” foreshadows the artist and producer’s next musical chapter. 

Reviving the character from his 2018 EP Craig, Reo Cragun reintroduces a darker mood and more braggadocious attitude to his sonic palette. “I'm not a very bravado person by nature. I have a pretty simple life, to be honest. Craig is kind of the opposite of that. The side of me that’s extravagant, not afraid to express my thoughts, and has strong opinions–that's the character.”

Bridging the gap between Reo and Craig, “what it’s like to lose,” weaves between the more thoughtful, contemplative Reo and a more impulsive, in-your-face Craig.

records.title: Songbird (with Taylor Alexander)

records.note:
Songbird:

Originally created as a demo, last year I wrote songbird in an attempt to create a conceptual story over acoustic guitars. 

The story surrounds a man on his last will, who decides to take one more day to himself to appreciate the last moments of his life, only to be brought back to reality when he hears a bird sing a melody that shakes him. The song is written as a thank you letter to the bird after that moment. 

Fast forward to today... I had the pleasure of meeting with Taylor Alexander as he visited our hometown. While talking I felt an instant connection on how to take this song one step further. Featuring his luscious vocals he continues the story forward encapsulating the theme of the song and resulting in a full length story.

We made a lot of songs, and we’re excited to share them. All of them. This year we’re releasing 24 songs in 48 weeks. If we’re being real, it’s actually two albums – there’s AM and there’s PM. AM is the lite stuff, PM is the nite stuff. Think of it like the Summer Olympics and Winter Olympics, but for dance music.

“Only Only” is our 11th single this year. This baby was born and raised in the heart of Brooklyn. We tried to capture the soul of the city where it's emotional and a bit heavy on the feels but when it hits the dancefloor, it takes on a life of its own. The bone-dry vocal chop in the intro will grab your attention and won’t let go until the clock strikes 2am and you find yourself somewhere in Brooklyn. How did you get there? No f***ing clue ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ 

Next single will be out 2 weeks from today, and the following single 2 weeks after that.

SRA stands for “Source Recordings Augmentations”, product of the experimentation with audio that has been reshaped many times. It embraces Blockchain technology in the form of NFTs, setting a new standard in the way G89 Records releases music. By leveraging this approach, we can offer true digital ownership, ensure fair compensation for our artists, and streamline revenue distribution through smart contracts. NFTs also provide a unique way for fans to support our art, while reducing reliance on middlemen, increasing transparency. We believe this shift marks the next logical step in the evolution of the music and arts ecosystem, benefiting considerably all parties involved.

About:

William Jourdain, also known under the moniker of Automatisme, began his music project in 2011 and since then has been publishing on various labels, such as Constellation, Mille Plateaux, and Outlines, while simultaneously being active as an art historian and curator. His generative ambient dub techno music is continually reshaped in the studio. This album is a compilation of post-produced sound archives, including stems, presets, and templates dating from 2011 to the present day.

records.note:
In 2018 I self-released 'Merry Go Round' as my third single. During those early years I found myself exploring many sonic identities with the help of my producers Sam Welch and Dave Holden. We had a lot of fun pushing away from my 'folky' roots towards a more alt-pop universe of sounds. 

Written in 5/4 time and embracing punchy, static melody lines, 'Merry Go Round' felt like a break away track from the more melancholy sounds and themes I'd been creating. The song itself was inspired by witnessing how certain people coped, or didn't cope with the success or achievements of those around them. 'Merry Go' is a metaphor for everyone else having fun at the amusement park whilst you sulk at the bottom of the ride, wondering why you're still queueing to get on.  

I'm excited to bring this early Emma Miller track to the blockchain for the first time and hopefully introduce the song to a new audience of collectors and listeners alike. There are 20 limited edition Music NFTs of the track which include a high quality audio download and a rare, signed artwork version. The free artwork edition is available for all collectors to own as a memento of 'Merry Go Round' launching on the blockchain. Which will you collect?

records.title: Tree of Life - Golden Egg
records.creator: 0xa79AF4e5823e5e7768506DfC1AD9CD088017846e
records.note:
"The branches up above are the kingdom of the heavens; the roots below form the kingdom of the earth, the nether world; and the trunk is the world axis round which the whole world revolves, and at the same time a life-giving center or the main artery of life throughout the world."
— C.G. Jung

"Tree of Life" is the first single from the debut Supersigil album Spectres.

Spectres comprises 13 experimental tracks produced over the last seven years—the 28th release in my discography but my first ever completely solo full-length album. While working on this record, I delved deep into Jungian psychology, concepts from which became central to the project. All 13 tracks are named after archetypes—innate, universal forces that shape our experience of the world.

Spectres is also a visual art project. For each of the 13 tracks, I trained a bespoke AI GAN on consensually crowd-sourced images submitted in response to the corresponding archetype. By limiting the training time of these custom image-to-image models, I found I could achieve results that mirrored the formation of archetypal symbols as I imagine them deep in our collective unconscious: elusive yet powerful forms emerging from abstract swirls of colour. I think of this process as filtering the archetypal forces through contributors' personal psyches before channelling them back into the realm of the universal. For the album cover I trained another GAN on outputs from all the previous GANs combined, resynthesising the individual archetypal energies to forge an integrated whole.

Spectres is more than a collection of WAVs and JPGs; it is a dialogue between the personal and the universal, a multidisciplinary exploration of the forces that connect us all. The album has taken me on a transformative seven-year journey through sound, imagery and psyche. In the resulting work, individual and collective experience harmonise, revealing the profound depths of human interconnectedness.

Before its official release on 11/23, I'm rolling Spectres out across the web3 ecosystem, dropping tracks on Sound, Catalog, Zora, Lens and other emerging platforms. In a novel release structure, collectors of individual tracks gain instant access to stream the full album months before its official release. The goal is to push the limits of onchain interoperability to explore what a web3-native album release can look like in 2024.

records.title: PAINT ME YOUR COLORS - Limited
records.creator: 0xeb9bBB9C1B49e42237016e7CA66a08e7bC637B97
records.note:
Progressive techno holds a very special place in my heart, combining emotional depth and rich production techniques, carving out a unique niche in the world of dance music.

In my track "Paint Me Your Colors," I aimed to transform the fundamental elements of techno into a more melodic and dynamic structure. This track is both intense and emotionally profound.

The arrangement opens with intricately woven synthesized melodies and a driving, classic techno bassline. The layers of atmospheric sounds and pads that follow are designed to transport listeners to a vast soundscape where dreams and reality merge. At the forefront of the track, there’s a powerful male vocal delivering soul-stirring lyrics. Complementing this are harmonies from both male and female backing vocals, adding depth to the overall composition.

The lyrics of "Paint Me Your Colors" invite listeners to explore the depths of human connection and the desire for complete understanding. Through its lyrical content and vocal arrangements, the song metaphorically portrays a person's inner world, emotions, and stories through colors.

I hope this track conveys the vibe I felt while creating it and that you enjoy it.

Peace & Love.

records.title: Post Internet - Limited
records.creator: 0x39939d0e207Cf7BDF7EE407F33b26E5dDf6f5e5e
records.note:
I wrote this song back in the summer of 2022. At the time I was doing a social media detox and I wanted to dig deeper into understanding how I viewed the internet. Most people are just glued and would be considered addicted to it. But I always wanted to look at the internet as a tool for knowledge, growth, community, creativity, and everything else we really could imagine it to be. It's important to identify when some of our behaviors are becoming a "bit toxic" or "out of control" I still find myself glued to my phone when I don't need to. The internet feels like a friend or a lover. It's always there. 

Detoxes are important, but so is the internet. Find the balance and live in the balance. It's somewhere there, you just need to find it.

Album coming June 7th with physical copies.

Peace and love.

Tommy

It’s Already Begun

This song was written as a reflection of Kinda Always Sleepy and came from experimenting with the Epitome effects while recording the first track. I intentionally kept the riff simple so that I could explore the music via production. I played the delay in order to experiment with the space in the riff and the rhythms that began as the reflections and echoes met each other. I wanted the drums to be less intrusive to the song so I manually filtered it to reveal the rhythm where I wanted within the song and in reflection to the guitars’ delay. As happy as I was with the original take I felt like the repetition gave space for a lead instrument or vocals. I chose theremin as the lead instrument and used it as a vocalist to express ranges that the delay and drums were not occupying. I used two theremin voices as a call and response to each other and gave them space to wander.

records.title: Rainboots - Golden Egg
records.creator: 0x39939d0e207Cf7BDF7EE407F33b26E5dDf6f5e5e
records.note:
I wrote this song on a gloomy day towards the tail end of my last relationship. I was constantly faced with the reality that people only change when they need to change for themselves. People will live their entire lives not realizing they are imperfect beings who yearn for growth. Change is the only constant we have in life. It's important to grow and evolve and understand our flaws so we can become better people. Rainboots is about that experience specifically towards my old lover who wouldn't acknowledge the importance of change and growing together as one. 

Heartbreak and loss can be experienced in a relationship months before the relationship comes to an end. There is a somber loneliness that looms heavily in the air when both partners know the end is near. We latch onto the lover we once knew even though we understand we both changed. Is it for comfort, the fear or loneliness or the terrors of change? Either way, trees shed leaves and so should we.

records.title: It Can't Be Us - Limited

records.note:
The long awaited 4th and final track from the OmegaKid Genesis E.P. As with all my tracks, this is another homage to my Web3 journey. Written for the soundtrack of The MCVerse Racing Experience - This track is the first music NFT that is also a whitelist token, meaning you will get whitelist access to the next NFT drop from The MCVerse - their Trux, by holding this track on either Avalanche (Campfire) or on Eth/Optimism (Sound.xyz).
This song was mixed and mastered in the test type SanSound Sanwear In Ear Monitors. As such I’ve managed to combine some of my personal favourite projects building in Web3 and beyond.
This song for me is a reflection of my emotions driving through the 22/23 bear market, knowing I was in the right place for what felt like an eternity, riding through the waves of fear, doubt and uncertainty. Finding solace in communities like The MCVerse and SanSound definitely kept me sane during those times and so it was only natural that I got to work on something that reflected all of this. 
Inspired by the soundtracks of the 90’s/00’s racing games including the Need For Speed Underground series, Gran Turismo, the F1 racing games and F-Zero, I drew on all of these to create this track.

I created 2 art pieces for this since the track is available on 2 different blockchains. I used my Musclecar NFT along with the Avalanche branding and the lyrics of the track and my Grantsville Supercar along with the Ethereum branding (plus a whole lot of prompting secret sauce) to create the two images.

As with all the OmegaKid Genesis tracks and art everything including, writing, recording, mixing, mastering, art creation, project collaboration and marketing is all a solo endeavour, which is why these things take some time to create and get to the point I’m ready to put out into the world.

Finishing this E.P. has taken 2 years of hard work, improving all of these skills and for me has been one of my personal favourite achievements. It has now set me up to keep this content coming and is only going to get better.

Finally, I’ll announce this here. My SanSound avatar trait, created by Cromagnus and coming soon will be the spoils of support here. For each one of the 4 tracks you own, you will get 25% off of my trait there - these will have future benefits as I grow into the SanSound ecosystem.

Thank you all for listening and taking this journey with me so far. There is so much more to come and I’m excited that we are just here at the beginning together.

Om

records.creator: 0xEf9D99DA0DA65A9a93fCEd18d209340553a008F7
records.note:
I ‘only’ started drinking when I was around 24 years old in 2015, I met this amazing blonde girl that I thought was out of my league but then one night we kissed and I was just connected to her.
Turned out that she was ‘escaping’ a bad relationship with other people, I was one of those people, it wasn’t malicious tho, she even apologized for potentially stringing me along. She wasn’t doing that, I was stringing myself along with the fantasy of her and so we had to let each other go. She had this ethereal beauty, blonde beautiful hair, sea blue eyes, amazing smile but most of all she was so sweet, caring and fun to be around.

 ‘She’s Got The’ was written a year later when I met my then girlfriend and picked up an acoustic guitar, the song just came out of me. The chorus was the first thing and then the verses followed quickly after. 

The song had about 3 different versions before I produced this pop/80’s infused version that is the main one today. The chorus jumping from the chest voice to the head voice with the ‘she’s out there looking for love’ gives the song its unique character.

I might actually record different versions throughout my life because the song is so damn catchy and meaningful in my journey!

This song is part two of a three-part series, so any collector that minted my “Too Heavy” genesis before this drop is live gets it airdropped to them for free (and will be allow-listed for the pre-sale of my next song).

Written & produced by ALYSS

I remember literally RUNNING home to make music after hearing a pregnant woman sample her unborn baby's heartbeat on stage in the middle of her set. It was so epic and random i wish i remembered her name…

At that time I’d been thinking about the idea that we're just as ‘physical’ in our dream state as we our in waking life - but we’re just more ‘tuned in’ to this waking reality. I mean…96% of matter is invisible. And even the remaining 4% of physical matter is made up of 99% space. So none of us really actually exist in a true solid form in either reality…yet here we are...doing our human bizz

When I first released this back in 2016 I remember convincing myself people would 100% think it was too weird. I'd never made anything like it before & assumed it would just be one of those ones that made sense to me but no one else.

To my shock it ended up being named 'Hottest Record' by Annie Mac on BBC Radio 1, led me to support Sampha at the London Jazz Cafe, had full rotation on Triple J in Australia + was being played in clubs all over the world. A bit of a madness to say the least!!! 

Can you guess what T S I E R stands for??

‘Ku Kane Lono’ came shortly after finishing a beautiful book called ‘Urban Shaman’ by Serge Kahili King. records.title: so good - Limited

records.note:
hot take: the best art is made outside of studio walls

there are over 100,000 new tracks uploaded daily to Spotify, and it’s more accessible + convenient than ever to create any kind of music using sample libraries and AI. so why bother creating anything, and what sets me apart from the flood of generated sounds?

this year I set an intention to create music away from my comfort zone — to put myself in physically demanding locations/climates that few would be willing to go to, and explore the connective tissue between life outdoors and the sounds it inspires.

I don’t really have a solid blueprint or path to follow at the moment — but between hauling music gear up mountains and camping out alone in ski huts, I’m having so much fun re-learning how to produce in new + challenging environments

this process takes a lot more energy and perseverance, but all the best things in life usually do 🙃

lots of new releases coming your way in 2024, thanks for being patient with me (and for caring to listen when you have so many options)

☽ ‘MOON’

I was driving home very late one night on an empty road, staring up at the brightest full moon I think I’ve ever seen - the Sirius star decorating it to the left. I had just finished the book ‘Who Built The Moon’ by Alan Butler + had not stopped thinking about all the incredibly rich and fascinating research he had shared. I remember the most visceral, almost out of body feeling as I read his conclusions in the final chapter. Driving along entranced by this almost blinding, pulsating vortex above me, the lyrics and melody just started flowing out…


>>>? TRIPPY MOON PONDERINGS:

☽ Ancient peoples across all cultures describe the time when we had no moon. Many Greek Writers from different periods mention the Proselenes (meaning “those that were before the moon”).

☽ Seismometers discovered that the moon ‘rang like a bell’ when heavy objects were smashed into it, suggesting it may, in fact, be hollow.

☽ Scientist R Foster (1965) claimed that the moon was in fact made of plasma, not rock. Mr Foster claimed that once his ‘profound and decisive’ investigations were proven, a complete re-investigation of the laws of nature would be necessary.

☽ Many esoteric circles believe the moon is the final portal through which souls reincarnate back onto this plane.


Whatever the moon may or may not be or how and when it arrived here, it is surely one of the most mysterious celestials in the sky. I share ‘moon’ in honour of her mystery and her beauty. May you observe her with something a little new in your heart tonight <3

records.note:
I was a little bit tipsy at a party when I asked Toha to remix Know Me Better, lol. I can have social anxiety in large groups, but I had met Toha before at this really beautiful small picnic that Pete Rango had coordinated a while back when he was in LA. There were just a few of us there that day, and we sat on this grass oasis under the Hollywood sign talking about spirituality and art. It was symbolic of the havens and connections we can find while navigating a city so focused on entertainment. Cut back to the party. So in the middle of the Hollywood Hills again, feeling socially anxious surrounded by a lot of people, and with some liquid courage, I asked Toha if he would be down to remix this song. And that's how I found another haven under the Hollywood sign - this song. 

Despite the story of how connection inspired this song, it's about spending time alone - about how spending time alone helped me to get to know myself better and fall in love with myself. It's also about learning to let my heart lead the way and serving as the lighthouse for my life. Toha and I first connected through having those deep kinds of heart-led conversations, so I think it's really beautiful that our first song together feels like an extension of that conversation, a conversation that we can now bring everyone that listens into as well. 

How are you getting to know and love yourself better? 

Here are the lyrics:

I just wanna stay inside
Got a whole world in my mind
I've been happy on my own
I'm not lonely, just alone

I’m living my life
Like I’m writing a love letter

We’re all going to die one day so why not write the songs we want to write or do the things we want to do. I wanted to try something different with my music and push myself with production, songwriting and my voice. Inevitably and ironically, Hot Temperature would lay dormant on my hard drive for a few years because I was too shy to release it. The song is really just a heightened, “cool” version of myself pushing myself for improvement and leaning into the spaces that make me uncomfortable.

records.title: Smart Contract (Brújula) - Limited
records.creator: 0x29185eB8cfD22Aa719529217bFbadE61677e0Ad2
records.note:
This song is my synthesis of the Four Agreements of ancient Toltec culture.

I made this song on August 2020.





***

"Four Directions" was the topic where this song was focused when I was writing it, that initially took me to the process of the 4 agreements: Toltec wisdom that includes four universal concepts applicable to reality to generate invisible constructions that are sustained in time.

To walk where the compass in our hearts indicates, regardless of the cardinal points and knowing that there will be moments of opening the way, will be a challenge that will improve the free exercise of the will and, therefore, the renewal in our minds, which we need to be present to resolve conflicts and dispel shadows.

The song is a synthesis between these two concepts, the Toltec agreements and the compass of our hearts indicating where to go.

These agreements are:

  
Be impeccable with your words.  
Don't take anything personal.  
Don't make assumptions.  
Always do your best.


Taking things personally prevents us from growing beyond the edges of our wounds, and we end up with a bloody field, sometimes not even our own. If what comes out of your mouth sounds like a song, let the rhythm of your steps follow the pattern of the verb and dance in harmony with what dwells in the word, which is what initiates everything.
To suppose and judge the other is a mistake when love does not flow from us even in the moments of limit, where under the right conditions, life is more present and therefore, abundant. Observing our own process will bring to our present the universal order.

Giving the best of yourself in the situations you are involved it returns clarity and understanding, indispensable to see what is your responsibility and what is not, allowing us to assume life from the acquisition of new experiences and the synthesis of its processes from the discrimination of our own aptitudes at the time of committing our action where we decide to exercise the will.

All this time in my Web3 journey, I discovered that the most valuable thing about this technology is that it allows us to interact directly between artists and producers in a safe and direct way through smart contracts, which changes the rules of the game and allows us to work within the framework of collaboration, leaving the competition only to have it with ourselves.

That is why this song is called Smart Contract, because the first smart contract we must make is with ourselves. I hope you find a compass

records.note:
"Where Is the Love?" is a thought-provoking and socially conscious song that addresses various global issues and challenges. The motive behind the song's title reflects a deep concern for the state of the world and a quest for understanding and compassion.

Released by Tonahope in 2012, the song was written during a thunderous period marked by global conflicts, social injustices, and political tensions. The lyrics touch upon issues such as terrorism, war, discrimination, and the overall lack of empathy in the world. The repeated question, "Where is love?" serves as a powerful and emotional plea for humanity to reflect on its actions and strive for a more harmonious and compassionate world.

"Where Is the Love?" is not only a critique of existing problems but also a call to action. The song suggests that positive change begins with individual introspection and a commitment to promoting love and understanding. By asking the question repeatedly, the artists aim to provoke thought and inspire listeners to actively engage in creating a more compassionate and just society.

"Taksim" is a musical composition performed live during a prominent music event. The term "taksim," originating from Arabic, refers to the improvisational demonstration or freestyling using musical instruments. This evocative track was composed and executed as part of the esteemed Guitarology project, showcasing the artistry and creativity inherent in instrumental performance.
Guitarology is the name of a music album that carries deep feelings and messages related to reality. This Album composed and performed by Omar Alkilani. This album was able to touch the hearts of many audiences, as the music was able to influence them and they clearly responded to it.
The Guitarology album has been presented on Guitar Live for 5 consecutive Guitarology themed shows.

Refugee Guitars Orchestra, envisioned and directed by Omar Alkilani, serves as a vibrant project where a diverse group of refugee musicians come together to create a fusion of traditional and modern music. Each project becomes a dynamic collaboration, with different refugee musicians participating. Since its inception in 2019 this artistic initiative has already produced an E.P that beautifully showcase the blending of different cultures from all, over the world. Looking ahead the project aims to transform these creations into events and music videos envisioning a journey that celebrates the universal language of music.
"Smack That" stands out as a vibrant, multicultural music video mashup with a powerful underlying message: refugees can be resilient, cool individuals who can thrive in modern society despite the challenges of displacement.

records.title: Stones - Limited
records.creator: 0xbe5DB9E33A2309898D44d9f7A6EE9229EB4d5415
records.note:
Stones. 

I wrote this song in Lo De Marco, Nayarit, Mexico where my dad used to live, after a surreal day with a local man named Tacho (pictured) who took me riding through the mountains and beaches on horseback, followed by tea and conversation on his deck as the sun set. We talked about a spirit that lived in his house — built on Huichol land. We spoke in English and Spanish and perhaps a 3rd language, of deep understanding. He walked me home through a field blanketed by a sky with more stars in it than darkness. I wrote a diary entry + this song immediately afterwards. It’s about realizing your stories, your memories, your treasures, are all a part of you — and they’re worth collecting and sharing with others (like stones). 

Recorded with a group of incredible musicians in Mexico City.

Eternal Inner Flame was composed using a double-tracked electric guitar (with vibrato bar) and programmed drums. The clean arpeggios were done first, distorted lead improvised (free-styled) after. 

What interests me most about choosing Sunatori for this song is that Just a Plain Vox House has live floor-torches - you'll see them if you visit (link above) - and flames are the theme of the poem Yoshiro added to Sunatori. records.title: cassettes - Limited
records.creator: 0x7C8fD6B2A44B90f9ff1970265011DD5465cc6433
records.note: I wrote this song as a reminder for my grandfather years ago, who recently passed away. He was a music producer and music marketer who worked with Eminem, Maroon 5, Alicia keys, and more. He inspired me to write music and I even got a cassettes tattoo on my arm because of it. He loved cassettes and vinyls and I used to play with them in his office and it interested me a lot. I loved his 60s music and the vibe of it, especially the choirs and the glitchiness of some of his old tapes. It made me make this song and think about all the happy memories of music that he generated. I am going to release this on my birthday… I really hope y’all enjoy, and get to hear the sounds that remind me of one of my biggest inspirations.

records.title: Mr. President - Golden Egg
records.creator: 0x5642e19C5866CFf712B51574767748700C76bd56
records.note:
An extraordinary collaboration between an African reggae luminary and a British pan-African wordsmith, gave birth to the pulsating anthem, "Mr. President." The lyricist, a beacon of Pan-African consciousness, poured profound narratives into his verses, encapsulating the struggles, dreams, and calls for change resonating across the African continent. Jahmek, the reggae artist with a profound sense of melody, transformed these potent words into rhythmic magic, weaving a sonic tapestry that transcended borders.

This musical odyssey traversed continents and stages, evolving into a harmonious symphony of cultures and voices. The final iteration of "Mr. President" took shape in the United States, where Lemak Jahmek, a seasoned reggae vocalist, breathed life into the lyrics. The live reggae beats and rhythms, crafted with precision by Soul Fire Productions in Germany, provided the perfect backdrop, infusing the song with an infectious energy that reverberates with the heartbeat of Africa. "Mr. President" is not merely a song; it's a testament to the unity of global talents, a fusion of African roots and European craftsmanship, echoing a call for change and justice that transcends borders and unites hearts.

records.title: Unloved Things - Golden Egg
records.creator: 0x0CD7C18a115390979b9b84D41B63C36f0E7Ca1d0
records.note: This song is based on the poem called “may we raise children who love the unloved things” by Nicolette Sowder. I loved the idea of what she was trying to say, but I changed perspective from the parent to the child! I feel as though all children love the unloved things, but some lose their innocence sooner than others! I wanted this song to bring the listener back to a simpler time, when they were that child, & to transmit their mind to a safe and welcome place of innocence. It’s a place we call all access & I think if we remember, it can help gain perspective in any situation we are going through as we get older. Remember those things, hold them in your heart and realize what matters in life. I am one of those children. You are too! We all loved those things, and need reminding you appreciate the little things.

Maybe you're nostalgic for a time when albums would be listened to front to back and the songs would stay with you for a lifetime. records.title: lucid - Limited
records.creator: 0x8921B0Bd06cC80DE27390A0Bb8b27cB64116b47C
records.note:
"Lucid" is another one of my favorite tracks from my last album, “Hyperbolic Vibe Chamber”. 
For this release, I chose some of my favorite tracks to pair with the amazing artwork of the one and only IG: kindgotospace. The concept for the art is based on an experience I had a few months ago where I was walking back to my car from a concert on a cold winter night in the city. I was passing by an alleyway, when I noticed a vent on the side of one of the buildings, emitting a puff of steam that formed a beautiful spiral formation. It felt other worldly and I felt so blessed to be able to appreciate the beauty taking place in that moment. 

Driving home that night, I was reflecting on why that moment was so striking. I think it was the idea that there is so much beauty happening around us, and the demands of our world, the 9-5, etc. all too often make us forget that. If we just take a moment to slow down and be present, the world quickly begins to show us that beauty. It also made me think about places like station 9 3/4 in HP. You have this train station that looks like another stop, but unbeknownst to us muggles, there is this portal that can transport you into this magical world. I feel like making music is like that for me. That puff of steam in the alleyway served as a reminder of the magic that exists in this world if we keep our eyes, ears, and spirits open. It’s one of the few places I can go to for that escape. It’s such a blessing to be able to make art and be able-bodied enough to listen, to peruse through vinyl in the record store to look for that fire sample to flip. I was talking to my friend GC about this and he had the idea to create visuals that bring the metaphor of the alleyway to life.

"be with u" is an emotional indie dance/future house fusion and is my first release of 2024. It features a heartfelt refrain, "always wanna be with u," dancing around warm, organic synths and deep basses, crafting a love-infused number. Evolving four-on-the-floor drums add rhythmic flair, and playful vocal chops in the later sections enhance the emotional resonance. This song encapsulates the enduring essence of love, offering a melodic embrace for those moments of heartfelt connection on the dance floor.

The catalyst for this track was the chord progression I landed on when playing around with a marimba style synth. From there everything flowed naturally - I knew this was going to be a romantic rave / emotional dance track centered around love, and being with together with someone who means the world to you. I wrote and sung simple repeating lyrics, designed some organic synths and tastefully chopped/processed my vocals to create an evolving, emotional, yet danceable journey.

records.note:
I wrote “I Killed My Friend?” about a bad dream that felt weirdly comparable to a feeling of falling away from, or losing touch with what defines me as a person. The world feels like it moves at increasingly breakneck speeds and I use nostalgia as a tool for momentary slow downs. “Hopscotch on a railroad track” is a line that repeats several times, which is an example of something that can slow down a moment for me, temporarily pausing the feeling of free-falling that I compare to the dream in the song.

This track might appeal to listeners who appreciate introspective lyrics set to an energetic backdrop.

records.note:
A step inside the Raver Realm universe.

The collectible linking @soundxyz_ to the Music PFP collection Raver Realm by Jadyn Violet.

Halo Dreamer is a song written and produced by Jadyn Violet.

Collect 5 limited edition Dreamers -> Get airdropped 1 random Raver from the major collection Raver Realm.

Raver Realm is important because it redefines what a music collectible is. This premium 1800 collection consists of 9 original songs that are personified into Raver characters. 

All characters in the Raver universe were hand drawn by Jadyn Violet and are dynamic. 

This means as the songs (also known as Ravers) go up in streams on Spotify -> The Ravers levels up unlocking various utilities. 

Bringing music to life like never before!

Halo Dreamer is the first of many "Lost Ravers." Lost Ravers are not part of the original 9 Raver characters from Raver Realm. Halo Dreamer is a track that encapsulates the nostalgia of loving someone so deeply. The act of something as simple as smelling an old lovers perfume becomes a catalyst to rehash all of the old feelings of lust. "She took out my old perfume and started geeking." 

Jadyn has a belief that fans can relate to music so much more than they are right now. Taking a song and turning it into a character lets someone relate to the story a lot more than simply listening to lyrics and productions. That is what Jadyn did with Raver Realm, and what he hopes to continue pushing with the Lost Raver "Halo Dreamer."

records.title: Comet - Limited
records.creator: 0x39939d0e207Cf7BDF7EE407F33b26E5dDf6f5e5e
records.note:
I wrote this song back in November after probably the most gut wrenching break up I've ever gone through. No one told me breakups get wildly more difficult to deal with when you get older lol. I rented a house in the Poconos and brought my recording equipment with me. I pretty much just drank a bunch of wine, got lost in the woods and wrote music so I could understand what just happened in my life and fully process my emotions. I seem to always run off to the mountains after a break up and bring my equipment lol. 

The whole writing and recording process with Comet happened extremely fast and the vocals were done in one take with my mouth directly against the mic. I was trying to sing as quietly as possible even though I didn't necessarily need to. I think I was singing so quietly because I was quite literally exhausted with life. I've learned though that even when love is gone you will be okay. You grow, you evolve, you reflect on the past and try your absolute best to do better every day that goes by. It's important to listen to your body, mind, and spirit and heal from the world. You go at your own pace with life and no one else's. And equally as much as you heal on your own, surrounding yourself with good friends and family helps a lot too.

Just another canvas i created out of my musical art collection, speaking of which........

Navigating the path of a musician or artist is asking to embarking on a challenging and unpredictable journey, riddled with various adversities that test one's resilience and passion. Here's a metaphorical glimpse into the hurdles we often face:

The aspiring musician or artist sets sail in a fragile vessel, their dreams and aspirations unfurling like sails in the wind. However, the tides of uncertainty and competition are fierce, creating waves of self-doubt and industry challenges that threaten to capsize their artistic voyage.

The first wave, aptly named "Financial Rapids," crashes against the boat. Limited resources and the high cost of equipment, studio time, and promotional efforts can feel like a relentless current, requiring artists to navigate carefully to avoid drowning in financial woes.

As they sail farther, the fog of "Recognition Obscurity" blankets the horizon. Breaking through this mist is a formidable task, with countless talented artists vying for attention in a sea of anonymity. It becomes a struggle to emerge as a distinct voice, desperately trying to be noticed amidst the cacophony of the creative realm.

The storm of "Creative Blockades" looms ahead, thundering with self-doubt, artistic blocks, and the pressure to conform to trends. Artists battle against the gusts of conformity, attempting to stay true to their unique sound and vision, fearing that their creativity might be swept away by the storm.

In the heart of the journey lies the whirlpool of "Industry Challenges," a maelstrom where artists must contend with complex contracts, exploitation, and the elusive pursuit of fair compensation. The risk of being swallowed by the currents of exploitation is ever-present, demanding a delicate dance to navigate the turbulent waters of the music industry.

Yet, despite the tempests and turbulent waters, artists persist. They adjust their sails, weather the storms, and find inspiration in the moonlit calm between challenges. The journey, though arduous, is a testament to their unwavering dedication and passion, steering their artistic vessels toward the distant shores of recognition, accomplishment, and the fulfillment of their creative destiny.

She always felt like an outsider in this world. She didn't fit in with the norms and expectations of society. She hated the way people judged her based on her appearance, her background, her choices. She wanted to be free from the constraints and pressures of reality.

That's why she started hacking her prostate, the common name for the Professional Status Apparatus (PSA). The prostate was a mandatory device that filtered the information that reached her brain, allowing her to perform better in her career and society. By hacking her prostate, she could change the way she saw, heard, felt, and thought about everything. She could create her own reality, where she was happy and in control. She could do anything she wanted, without fear or regret. She felt like she had found the ultimate solution to her problems.

But she didn't realize the consequences of her actions. She didn't know that hacking her prostate was illegal and dangerous. She didn't know that she was risking her health, her sanity, and her identity. She didn't know that she was losing touch with reality and herself. She didn't know that she was not the only one who was hacking her prostate, and that there were others who had more sinister motives. She didn't know that she was about to face the biggest challenge of her life, and that she would have to make a choice between her prostate and her future.

records.note:
This song was created over the internet - just like our friendship. 

When me and Reo first started to work together we were in two different cities: I would fly from LA to Vegas to write and he would crash on my couch in LA if we weren’t out there. That process went on for months at a time.

Eventually I coerced him and his wife to move back to LA and ironically we have worked together in person less than we ever did when we were in two different cities.

Reo and I are both interesting types of introverts - in a way that similarity has probably been what’s kept us such close friends and collaborators over the years. While we’re down to be the life of the party from time to time, we individually spend the vast majority of our lives working out of our bedroom studios.

Our lives have changed so much since releasing music onchain. DRIVE ME MAD. is a look into that reflection.

records.creator: 0x01A5243219980FAc800b28ddBd8eC3a6A86696b3
records.note:
The song refers to the orixá Xangô. This deity is part of the African-rooted religions in Brazil, recognized as the orixá of lightning and thunder, of justice, characterized by strength and intolerance towards committed injustices. 

An artist with extensive experience in Afro-religious-Brazilian musicality, in "Canção pra Xangô," Libertu evokes the deepest elements of tradition. The artist rhythmically builds the song on the drum beats of Umbanda yards, especially on the "Barravento," "Cabula," and also "Maracatu" rhythms.


The arrangements prioritize percussion elements, which lead the music through the sections. The harmony is provided by a guitar coupled with counterpoints performed by saxophone. In the recordings, Libertu played all the percussion instruments and the guitar. "Canção pra Xangô" can be categorized as a prayer-song and is part of the MPB tradition that recognizes, praises, and evokes the strength of ancestry.

She is the most syncretized and worshipped deity in the African pantheon in Brazil, with her worship widespread from north to south, with many festivals and holidays in her honor in the country. 


An artist with extensive experience in Afro-religious-Brazilian musicality, in “Festa pra Iemanjá,” Libertu evokes the deepest elements of the tradition. The artist rhythmically constructs the song on the drum beats of Umbanda yards, especially on the "Ijexá," "Cabula," and also "Alujá" rhythms.

The arrangements prioritize percussion elements, which lead the music through the sections. The harmony is provided by a guitar coupled with counterpoints performed by saxophone, flute, and a choir of female voices. In the recordings, Libertu played all the percussion instruments and the guitar. "Canção pra Iemanjá" can be categorized as a prayer-song and is part of the MPB tradition that recognizes, praises, and evokes the strength of ancestry.
